data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(Consulting Services - Individual Consultant Selection)

The Oromia Bureau of Industry and Enterprise invites qualified and eligible applicants for the position of Youth Employment Apprenticeship Specialist under the Urban Productive Safety Net and Jobs Project (UPSNJP) financed by the World Bank.

 Positions #1: Youth Employment Specialist for the following cities

City

Required No.

Reference Number

Ambo

1

ET-OROMIA-OJCVB/AMBO-573676-CS-INDV

Asella

1

ET-OROMIA-OJCVB/ASELLA-573672-CS-INDV

Bishoftu

1

ET-OROMIA-OJCVB/BISHOFTU-573663-CS-INDV

Nekemte

1

ET-OROMIA-OJCVB/NEKEMTE-573668-CS-INDV

Sheger (Sebeta & Burayu Work Stations)

2

ET-OROMIA-OJCVB/SHEGER-573659-CS-INDV

Role and KEY RESPONSIBILITIES of the positions

  • Develop a city-level annual work plan and budget for youth employment activities.
  • Identify and map potential host employers (private companies, NGOs, and public institutions) for the Apprenticeship Program.
  • Design outreach strategies to recruit eligible vulnerable youth according to project guidelines.
  • Facilitate the matching process between youth interests/skills and employer needs.
  • Draft and manage Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) between the project, host employers, and apprentices.
  • Organize and deliver pre-apprenticeship orientation and soft skills training (e.g., work ethics, communication, Life skill).
  • Ensure the timely payment of stipends or subsidies to participants.
  • Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual progress reports highlighting achievements, challenges, and lessons learned.

Qualification: Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Economics, Management, Sociology, Development Studies, Business Administration, Public Administration, Business Management, or related fields.

Experience: Minimum 5 years (Bachelor's) or 3 years (Master's) relevant experience in youth employment, apprenticeship, internship, labor market, or related development programs. Experience in donor-funded projects is an advantage with Fluency in Afan Oromo language and English skill

Duration: One year, renewable based on satisfactory performance and project requirements.

Remunerations: will be based on Ministry of Finance Channel One Project Salary Scale.

 

Position # 2: Regional Youth Employment Specialist

Required number: 1

Ref. Number: ET-OROMIA-OJCVB-573656-CS-INDV

Role AND key RESPONSIBILITIES of the position

  • Develop and consolidate the regional-level annual work plan, operational strategies, and budget allocation for youth employment sub-components across all participating cities.
  • Conduct regional market assessments and employer mapping to identify potential high-growth sectors, large private employers, industry parks, and regional employer associations.
  • Provide continuous technical assistance, backstopping, and capacity building to city Youth Employment Specialists and field teams.
  • Consolidate city-level progress reports into regional monthly, quarterly and annual performance reports for submission to MoLS/PCU and regional entities (BoIE/Regional PCU).

 Qualification: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Economics, Management, Development Studies, Sociology, Public Administration, Business Administration, Business Management, or a closely related field.

Experience: Minimum of 7/5 years BA/BSC or MA/MSc of professional experience in youth development, labor market intermediation, employment services, or social protection programs with Fluency in Afan Oromo language and Amharic; working proficiency in English is highly desirable skills.

  • Duration: One year, renewable based on satisfactory performance and project requirements
  • Remunerations: will be based on Ministry of Finance Channel One Project Salary Scale.

Application Documents: Application Letter (indicating City and Reference Number), Updated CV, Educational Credentials, Experience Certificates, and Supporting Documents.

Deadline: Within 10 working days from the date of publication, not later than 4:00 PM.

 

Submission   Address:
Oromia Bureau of Industry and Enterprise Human Resource Administration and Capacity Building Directorate
5th Floor, Oromia Bureau Compound, Sarbet Area, Finfinnee

Tel: +251945712125
Email: negerigobena92@gmail.com

Note: Applicants may apply for only one city/position. Applications for more than one city will be disqualified.

data.title: Recruitment of 1 Livelihood Specialist for Oromia UDHB UPSNJP Regional hub
data.project_name: Urban Productive Safety Net and Jobs Project
data.institution: Oromya Regional State Urban Development and Housing Bureau
data.notice_text:
Request for Expression of Interest

(Consulting Services- Individual Consultant Selection)

Urban Development Bureau, Urban Productive Safety Net and Job Project (UPSNJP)

Grant Number- D732-ET

Oromia Urban Development Bureau invite qualified eligible individuals of the following positions for Regional Urban Productive Safety Net and Job Project PCU, which is financed by World Bank and Government of Ethiopia.

Position # 1: Procurement Specialist for Regional HUB

Required number: 1

Ref # ET-OROMIA-UDHB-573623-CS-INDV for Regional HUB

  Specific roles and responsibilities

  1. Managing the procurement management of the Project for procurement of goods, works and non-consulting in accordance with agreed procurement procedures for the project.
  2. Providing technical support and guidance to other implementing agencies in all aspects of procurement of works, goods and services.
  3. Monitoring procurement in IAs at cities to ascertain compliance with the World Bank and GoE procurement regulations.
  4. Preparing and Updating the UPSNJP Procurement Plan and regularly updating and uploading the documents and information in Systematic Tracking and Exchange in procurement (STEP).
  5. Coordinating/conducting the preparation of Terms of Reference, Request for Expression of Interest, Shortlisting, Invitation of Bid, preparation of a comprehensive and complete Bidding documents for Works, Goods, and non-consulting services. 
  6. Ensure that proper maintenance of files and Procurement Register Books are up-to-date in STEP as well as in hard copy.
  7. Present monthly technical reports and perform any other duties assigned by Project Coordinator.

    Required qualifications and Experience

  • MSc/MA/BSc/BA from a reputable and recognized university in Commerce, Business Administration, Economics, accounting, management or any other related discipline
  • Training in procurement or a professional qualification in procurement.
  • At least 6/8 years’ experience in procurement in a large private/ public sector organization or Projects for Masters and Bachelor degree respectively.
  • At least 2/3 years procurement experience in GOE/IDA funded Projects thorough understanding of World Bank’s procurement regulations, Federal and regional government procurement procedures.
  • Excellent writing and communication skills both in Amharic and English
  • Experience and knowledge on the Systematic Tracking and Exchange in procurement (STEP) is an added advantage.

Position #2: Livelihood Specialist for Regional HUB

Required number: 1

Ref # ET-OROMIA-UDHB-573642-CS-INDV

Specific roles and responsibilities

  • Provide expert technical advice and input to local governments and city project teams on best-practice urban livelihoods approaches and social protection strategies.
  • Develop regional and city-level Livelihood Development Plans, outlining target groups, activities, timelines, resources, and expected outcomes.
  • Coordinate with city project officers, community organizations, and other stakeholders to ensure activities are well-planned, sequenced, and responsive to local needs.
  • Design and implement service linkages (financial literacy, access to finance, market/value chains for input and output sourcing, access to workspaces, etc.) for sustainable livelihood development.
  • Track, document, and report on partnerships, service linkages, and market integration outcomes, providing evidence and lessons to inform adaptive management and continuous improvement.
  • Prepare timely and high-quality progress reports, review reports, mission reports, and project completion reports as required by the project.
  • Carry out any other assignments related to livelihoods and jobs as delegated by the Regional Project Coordination Hub or Project Coordinator.

  Qualification and Experience Requirements

    • Minimum of a Bachelor’s Degree in Economics, Urban Planning, Business Administration, Management, Sociology, Development Studies, or a closely related discipline.
    • At least 8 years (Master’s) or 10 years (Bachelor’s) of progressively responsible experience in urban livelihoods development, enterprise development, or related areas.
    • Demonstrated experience in establishing partnerships and service linkages with private sector actors, NGOs, financial service providers, and government-supported initiatives.
    • Experience supporting market linkages, business formalization, and promoting sustainable exit strategies for project beneficiaries.
    • A minimum of 5 years’ experience working with local governments, urban development agencies, municipal structures, or urban communities.
    • Demonstrated experience in World Bank or other donor-funded project environments is a strong advantage.
    •  Written and verbal communication skills in English and Amharic; knowledge of local languages is an asset.
    • Advanced report writing, data analysis, and presentation skills.

Duration of Assignment: The assignment will be a one-year contract, with possible extension upon satisfactory performance of the consultant for both positions.

Remunerations: As per the revised Ministry of Finance channel one salary scale for both positions.

 

How to apply:

Applicants should enclose their expression of interest including CV, letter of application, Copy of Educational document and Work Experience and other supportive documents to the address HR Administration Building Directorate, 2nd floor of building in person or by e-mail: duressad1976@gmail.com or urgessaregasa234@gmail.com for ten (10) working days starting from this announcement during office hours.

Oromia National Regional State, Urban Development Bureau, HR Administration and Capacity Building Directorate, 3rd floor of building.

Finfine Oromia Bureau Compound, Around Sarbet (Near to Pushkin Square) on the way to Kera left Side

Country: Moldova

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MRCP/CS/C5/01

 

The Government of the Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank (the “Bank” or the “WB”) in the form of a loan/credit toward the cost of the Moldova Rural Connectivity Project. The S.A. “Administraia Naional a Drumurilor” (“NRA” or JSC “National Road Administration”), an implementing agency (the “Client”), intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan/credit to eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Expressions of Interest is issued.

 

The selected Consultant is expected to provide professional assistance to the Client in administration of the WB funded Contract with due diligence and by carrying out the duties of the Engineer as defined in the conditions of the Works Contract.

 

The duties of the Consultant for the supervision of the execution of design and works under Corridor 5, as per the “FIDIC Conditions of Contract for Plant & Design-Build (2nd Edition, 2017; Reprinted 2022 with amendments)” published by the Federation Internationale Des Ingenieurs – Conseils (FIDIC).

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained following a formal request to the Client to procurement.wb@andsa.md.

 

The Assignment is expected to start in May 2027 and has an estimated overall duration of 42 months, which includes 30 months of works supervision and 12 months covering Defects Notification Period the Performance Certificates issue and other closing activities, Final Account and Contract close-out.

 

The estimated minimum number of person-months required for the assignment is 211 person-months. This includes 67 person-months for Key Staff.

INVITACIÓN A PRESENTAR EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS
(SERVICIOS DE CONSULTORÍA-SELECCIÓN DE FIRMAS)


País: El Salvador
Proyecto: “Energía Geotérmica para el Desarrollo Sostenible e Inclusivo”
Préstamo No.: 9788-SV
Título Asignado: Servicios de Supervisión Técnica del contrato identificado como “Servicios de perforación y de suministros de materiales, accesorios, tuberías y servicios complementarios para la perforación de 8 pozos geotérmicos en el campo geotérmico Chinameca”.


Referencia No.: SV-LAGEO-534014-CS-QCBS


La Comisión Ejecutiva Hidroeléctrica del Río Lempa (CEL) ha recibido financiamiento del Banco Mundial para el proyecto “Energía Geotérmica para el Desarrollo Sostenible e Inclusivo” y se propone utilizar una parte de los fondos para la contratación de los servicios de consultoría mencionados en la referencia.


Los servicios de consultoría (“los servicios”) comprenden la supervisión técnica, operativa, de seguridad industrial y ambiental, así como la administración del contrato mencionado en el encabezamiento. Las funciones de la firma consultora se alinearán estrictamente con el rol de “El Ingeniero”, descripto en el contrato estipulado entre LaGeo y el contratista de perforación, bajo las condiciones del Libro Rojo de FIDIC (Edición 2017, reimpresa en 2022). El alcance de las obras a ser supervisadas es la perforación y completamiento de ocho (8) pozos geotérmicos profundos, de los cuales cinco (5) son con fines de producción de fluido bifásico agua/vapor y tres (3) para reinyección de agua geotérmica separada, bajo la modalidad de un Servicio Integrado de Perforación.


Los Términos de Referencia de esta asignación estarán disponibles en la página web de LaGeo (http://www.lageo.com.sv), o podrán ser solicitados directamente al Contratante a través de la dirección de contacto indicada al final de la presente solicitud.


La empresa ejecutora LAGEO S.A. de C.V., invita a firmas consultoras elegibles (¨Los Consultores”) a expresar su interés en prestar los servicios solicitados. En la Expresión de Interés, las firmas interesadas deberán proporcionar información que demuestre que cuentan con las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia pertinente para ejecutar los servicios.


Los criterios para la conformación de la lista corta son los siguientes:

  • Experiencia en la supervisión técnica y operativa de proyectos de perforación profunda (1,500-3,000 metros de profundidad) en campos geotérmicos o de petróleo y gas.
  • Experiencia en la supervisión de obras bajo contratos FIDIC, actuando en el rol de "El Ingeniero".
  • Experiencia en la supervisión de planes de gestión ambiental, social y de salud y seguridad ocupacional, bajo estándares de organismos multilaterales de crédito u otros internacionales equivalentes.

La experiencia deberá registrarse en el formulario EXP-2 Experiencia específica de la firma, que acompaña a esta solicitud de expresión de interés.


Se valorará positivamente:

  • Haber supervisado pozos geotérmicos.
  • Experiencia en la región centroamericana.
  • Contar con sistemas de gestión de calidad, ambiental, y salud y seguridad ocupacional certificados (ej. ISO 9001, 14001, 45001 o equivalentes), y;
  • Experiencia en la supervisión o aplicación del Marco Social y Ambiental del Banco Mundial.


Nota: De conformidad con las Regulaciones del Banco Mundial, NO se deben presentar currículos (CV) de expertos individuales en esta etapa de Expresión de Interés. El personal clave no será evaluado en la conformación de la lista corta.

La expresión de interés de los Consultores es requerida bajo el párrafo 7.16 (conformación de la lista corta) de las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, edición septiembre 2023 (en adelante las Regulaciones). De igual forma, los Consultores interesados deben tomar en cuenta las disposiciones sobre conflicto de interés previstas en la Sección III de las Regulaciones, párrafos 3.14, 3.16 y 3.17, así como la siguiente restricción particular: El Consultor que resulte seleccionado para prestar los servicios no puede tener ninguna relación accionaria, societaria, comercial o de asesoría con el contratista de los servicios integrados de perforación que deberá supervisar. 


Los Consultores se podrán asociar con otras firmas en forma de asociación en participación (Joint Venture), o presentar subconsultores, con el fin de mejorar sus calificaciones. Durante la etapa de Solicitud de Propuestas, los Consultores serán evaluados y el ganador será seleccionado en base al método Selección Basada en la Calidad y el Costo (SBCC/QCBS), descrito en las Regulaciones antes mencionadas.


Los Consultores interesados pueden obtener más información en la dirección abajo indicada, durante los días de lunes a viernes en el horario de las 8:00 AM a las 17:00 horas.


Las Expresiones de Interés deberán ser recibidas por escrito en la dirección indicada a continuación, ya sea personalmente; por medio de correo postal (Courier) o mediante correo eléctronico, a más tardar el lunes 23 de noviembre de 2026, 10:00 AM (GMT-6).

Assignment Tittle:     Request for Expressions of Interest - Recruitment of an Individual Consultant to Develop the Adaptive Social Protection (ASP) Sub-Window Manual and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)

Project Background

 The Government of The Gambia has secured Additional Financing (AF) under the Resilience, Inclusion, Skills, and Equity (RISE) Project (P179233), supported by the International Development Association (IDA) and the Global Shield Financing Facility (GSFF), to strengthen the country’s capacity to respond to climate and disaster-related shocks.

The AF introduces a new Subcomponent 3.4: Strengthening Disaster Risk Financing (DRF) and Adaptive Social Protection (ASP), which aims to integrate prearranged disaster risk financing mechanisms with shock-responsive social protection systems. This includes the establishment and capitalization of an Adaptive Social Protection (ASP) Sub-Window under the Social Protection Fund (SPF).

The ASP Sub-Window will serve as a dedicated, rules-based financing mechanism to enable timely and predictable delivery of emergency cash transfers to poor and vulnerable households affected by shocks such as droughts, floods, and food price crises.

Objectives of the assignment

The main objective of this consultancy is to develop a comprehensive, rules-based ASP Sub-Window Operational Manual and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) that will guide the governance, management, and utilization of funds for shock-responsive social protection interventions.

 

Scope of Services:

The consultant will develop the ASP Sub-Window Operational Manual addressing the following elements:

  1. Institutional and Governance Framework
  2. Define explicit time benchmarks for each step in the response chain (trigger confirmation, activation decision, beneficiary list finalization, payment instruction, first transfer received), calibrated to the project target of 60% of beneficiaries receiving their first transfer within 60 days of trigger activation. Reference the 2-week on-time Nafa payment standard as the operational baseline.
  3. Position the ASP Sub-Window clearly within the national risk-layering framework
  4. Financial and Investment Framework
  5. Activation protocols (“triggers”)
  6. Create a placeholder section that will outline when exactly an emergency response via the ASP Sub-Window will be activated. The consultant should create an outline detailing the type of information required per subsection. This section will then be filled separately.

 

Qualifications & Experience of the Consultant:

The individual consultant should have:

  • A Master’s degree in economics, public policy, finance, or related field.
  • At least 10 years of demonstrated experience in the design or management of disaster response funds and adaptive social protection systems.
  • Proven experience working in developing countries. Experience working in West Africa –ideally The Gambia – is an advantage.
  • Knowledge of the design of sovereign risk transfer instruments is an advantage.
  • Knowledge of the rules and regulations guiding the management of national funds in The Gambia is an advantage.
  • Knowledge of the financial management rules and regulations of the World Bank guiding supported projects is an advantage.
  • Excellent command of the English language
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and experience interacting with senior government officials.
  • Capacity to work independently with minimal supervision and to deliver work within agreed deadlines.

Submission of Expressions of Interest:

The Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs (MoFEA), through the Gambia Resilience, Inclusion, Skills and Equity Project, now invites eligible individual consultants to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2025(“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

A Consultant firm will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultants (IC) set out in the Guidelines for Recruitment of Consultants.

Assignment Title: Independent Verification Agent (IVA) and Technical Quality Assurance (TQA) for the Uzbekistan Rural Infrastructure Development Program – Phase 2

The Government of the Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Uzbekistan Rural Infrastructure Development Program – Phase 2 (RIDP-2), with co-financing from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) expected, and intends to apply part of the proceeds of the financing for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the provision of independent verification and technical quality assurance for the Program. The selected consulting firm will verify the achievement of the Program’s Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs) and Disbursement-Linked Results (DLRs) and assess the technical quality of infrastructure investments implemented under the Program.

The scope of the Services includes, but is not limited to, the following activities:

•          Conduct independent technical quality assurance of designs and completed civil works under DLI 5 (basic-service infrastructure) and DLI 7 (Common Facilities Centers), including compliance with applicable national construction norms and the climate-resilience and seismic design requirements specified for the Program; and

•          Submit verification and TQA reports to the GoU (through the Program Coordination Team) and to the World Bank in a form and substance satisfactory to the World Bank.

•          Verify, within its mandate, whether relevant environmental and social risk management requirements have been applied for sampled subprojects and CFCs, including E&S screening, exclusion criteria, site-specific mitigation measures, stakeholder engagement, grievance mechanisms, labor and occupational health and safety provisions, community health and safety measures, and documented corrective actions.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
Consulting Services For Preparation of an Energy Sector
Investment Program (ESIP) for the Marshall Islands

Grant No.: E331-MH
REGAIN Project
Reference No. MH-MEC-564965

July 31, 2026

The Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (GRMI) has received financing from the International
Development Association (IDA) (the “Bank”) in the form of a grant (hereinafter called “the Grant”), in the
amount of US$60 million, toward the cost of the Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase (REGAIN)
Project (P181250), approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a closing date of September 30, 2030.
The Marshalls Energy Company (MEC), as Employer and implementing agency, intends to apply a portion of
the proceeds of the Grant to eligible payments under a contract for consulting services for the preparation of an
Energy Sector Investment Program (ESIP), under Sub-Component 3.1 (Sector Development Assistance) of the
REGAIN Project. The ESIP shall be prepared in close coordination with the newly established National Energy
Authority (NEA) and shall cover Majuro, Ebeye and the outer island systems.
The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise the preparation of a prioritized, costed, and financeable
Energy Sector Investment Programme (ESIP) for the Marshall Islands, aligned with the Government's existing
Energy Strategy and Integrated Resource and Resilience Plan (IRRP). The Services include, among others:
• Targeted sector diagnostics and strategic review;
• Review and update of the least-cost development pathway, including preparation of an updated and
   integrated IRRP covering Majuro, Ebeye, and Outer Islands;
• Preparation and update of the energy sector investment pipeline;
• Renewable energy and storage target refinement;
• Preparation of a financing strategy;
• Preparation of a policy reform and enabling actions roadmap;
• Preparation of an e-mobility investment and strategic framework;
• Design of the ESIP monitoring and implementation framework;
• Stakeholder engagement, consultations and results validation; and
• Outer-island mini-grid (and, where suitable, mesh-grid) concept design.

The assignment is structured as a lump-sum contract with an estimated duration of 12 months, with an expected
start date in September 2026. The selected firm will nominate a multidisciplinary team, including the Key
Experts described below, and will report to MEC, coordinating closely with NEA, the World Bank, ADB and
other relevant stakeholders.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.
MEC now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.
Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and
relevant experience to perform the Services.
The shortlisting criteria are:

Mandatory requirements


a) Firm Experience:


1. At least 10 years of experience in energy sector planning, energy investment planning, integrated
resource planning, sector development strategies, or related advisory services.

2. Successful completion of at least two similar assignments during the last ten years involving energy
sector investment programs, integrated resource planning, utility master planning, energy transition
roadmaps, or comparable strategic energy planning studies.

geographically dispersed island power systems.

Terms of Reference (TOR)

Preparation of an Energy Sector Investment Program for the Marshall Islands – REGAIN Project

Project ID: P181250
Assignment Type: International Firm (Lump sum Contract)
Duration: 12 Months
Location: Remote with Periodic Missions to Majuro


1. Background


The Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) is one of the world's smallest and most isolated nations. The
country consists of 29 atolls and 5 low coral islands situated on about 181 square kilometres (km2) of land mass
in the Pacific Ocean. Majuro (the nation's capital) and Ebeye, the country's two largest urban centres, account
for about 96 percent of total population while the remaining inhabit outer atolls. The Government of the
Republic of Marshall Islands, (GRMI) and MEC require assistance to increase the amount of renewable energy
generation and BESS in the selected islands to increase access to electricity and to reduce dependence on
hydrocarbon fuels for their remote populations.

MEC, the state-owned energy utility, generates and provides electricity to Majuro Atoll, serving 55 percent of
RMI's population. MEC also manages three mini grids in Jaluit, Wotje, Rongrong (Majuro Atoll) and Kili
Island, the latter having been recently transferred to MEC from the Kili Bikini Ejit Local Government. The
Government has partnered with the World Bank through the Renewable Energy Generation and Access Increase
Project (REGAIN) – an IDA grant of US$60 million approved and effective as of December 13, 2024, with a
closing date of September 30, 2030. The REGAIN project aims to increase renewable energy generation and
improve electricity access while reducing reliance on diesel-based generation.

RMI’s Electricity Roadmap targets an objective of net zero greenhouse gas emissions and the achievement of
100% renewable electricity in the power generation mix by 2050. As a small and geographically dispersed
island nation, RMI remains highly dependent on imported diesel for electricity generation, which exposes the
country to high energy costs and vulnerability to global fuel price shocks. At the same time, growing electricity
demand, the need to improve the reliability of aging infrastructure, and the expansion of services across outer
islands require significant levels of investment in modern, resilient energy systems. Ensuring a reliable, clean,
and cost-effective electricity supply is therefore critical to achieving national climate commitments,
strengthening energy security, and supporting sustainable socio-economic development.

Under Sub-Component 3.1 of the REGAIN project (Sector Development Assistance), MEC plans to undertake a
study to prepare the country’s Energy Sector Investment Program (ESIP). The ESIP shall propose and define a
set of detailed, prioritized energy investments to safely and reliably increase renewable energy penetration in

Majuro and Ebeye grids, as well as other outer islands. The ESIP shall be prepared in close coordination with
the newly established National Energy Authority (NEA), and shall cover the national footprint of RMI,
including Majuro, Ebeye and the outer island systems.


The ESIP shall take into account the full range of relevant existing studies, including but not limited to:
      The Integrated Resource and Resilience Plan 2024-2034, which already sets out a high-level power
     system assessment and identifies a set of proposed investments in Majuro.
      SEDeP and REGAIN projects, including existing and new solar PV and Battery Energy Storage Systems
     (BESS) capacity to be deployed.
      Relevant energy sector programs and studies of other development partners active in the RMI, in
     particular the Asian Development Bank (ADB), such as the Energy Transition Project, to be considered
     to ensure coordination and avoid duplication of efforts.
      RMI Electricity Roadmaps and national targets.


2. Objectives
The objective of this assignment is to prepare a prioritized, costed, and financeable Energy Sector Investment
Programme (ESIP) which is aligned with the existing Energy Strategy and Integrated Resource and Resilience
Plan (IRRP). The ESIP will build upon existing planning and strategy documents and will focus on updating,
operationalizing, and translating these into an actionable investment and implementation framework.


The ESIP should include:
      The identification of investment priorities, including both generation and power grids.
      Descriptions of viable approaches to financing the identified needed investments.
      The enabling actions, including policy options to support the investment program.
      The necessary implementation arrangements required to support delivery of national energy sector
         objectives.


3. Project Description
The proposed ESIP project will support the development of a prioritized, costed, and implementable investment
program for the Marshall Islands’ energy sector, aligned with the Government’s existing Energy Strategy and
considering the Integrated Resource and Resilience Plan (IRRP) for Majuro (prepared in 2024). Building on
these existing strategic and planning instruments, as well as an updated IRRP 1 covering Majuro, Ebeye and the
outer island systems, the ESIP will translate national energy objectives into an actionable pipeline of
investments and enabling measures required to support sector development, energy security, resilience,
decarbonization, and long-term sustainability. The project will consolidate and update existing and official
sector analyses and investment priorities, while identifying financing approaches, implementation
arrangements, and policy actions necessary to facilitate delivery of priority investments.

1 The updated IRRP Will be prepared as part of the present technical assistance and will include updating the existing (2024) IRRP for
Majuro and expanding the geographical coverage of the IRRP to also include Ebeye and the outer island systems.

The ESIP will include targeted sector diagnostics, a review and validation of the existing least-cost development
pathway, refinement of renewable energy and storage deployment trajectories, and the preparation of an updated
energy sector investment pipeline. The project will also assess investment requirements associated with
emerging priorities such as grid modernization, resilience, storage integration, and e-mobility development. In
parallel, the ESIP will develop an overall financing strategy identifying potential public, private, concessional,
and climate finance sources, together with a policy reform and enabling actions roadmap aimed at addressing
barriers to implementation and investment mobilization.


The project will further establish an implementation and monitoring framework to support effective delivery
and tracking of the ESIP over time. Stakeholder engagement and consultation will be undertaken within the
assignment to ensure alignment across government institutions, utilities, development partners, and other
relevant stakeholders.


The resulting ESIP will provide a practical action plan for sequencing and financing priority energy sector
investments and will serve as a key tool for guiding government decision-making, coordinating development
partner support, and mobilizing investment into the sector.


4. Implementation Arrangements


MEC will be the Client and Employer under this assignment responsible for approving deliverables and
payments. NEA, as the national regulatory body for renewable energy in the Marshall Islands, will act as the
principal regulatory interface between MEC and the Consultant. For deliverables with regulatory or renewable
energy policy implications, the Consultant shall obtain NEA's endorsement prior to MEC's final approval. The
Consultant shall work under the direction of MEC and coordinate closely with:


      MEC management and technical staff.
      REGAIN Project Management Services consultant, as applicable.
      Project Implementation Unit within MEC.
      National Energy Authority (NEA), the national regulatory body for renewable energy, serving as the
          regulatory interface between MEC and the Consultant.
      World Bank on matters requiring no-objection, reporting, or implementation support.
      ADB and other development partners active in RMI's energy sector, as relevant.

5. Scope of Service

Task 1. Targeted sector sdiagnostics and strategic review


The Consultant will undertake a focused review of the energy sector to validate key assumptions, identify
material developments since preparation of the IRRP and Energy Strategy, and assess investment-relevant
constraints and opportunities. This is a diagnostic update, as opposed to a full sector assessment.


Specifically, the Consultant will:


(i) Review of existing sector policies, strategies, and plans.
(ii) Review of recent sector developments and pipeline projects.
(iii) Assessment of institutional, financial, and implementation constraints.

(iv) Review of utility performance and sector financing context.
(v) Identification of critical sector gaps affecting investment delivery.
(vi) Validation of key demand, technology, and resilience assumptions relevant to the ESIP.


Task 2. Review and update of the least-cost development pathway.


The Consultant will review the existing least-cost development pathway established under the existing IRRP
(2024) for Majuro and undertake targeted updates where necessary to ensure continued relevance for investment
planning purposes. The Consultant will also expand the geographic focus, to also cover Ebeye and Outer
Islands, incorporating the results the existing IRRP update and the analyses of the Ebeye and Outer Islands into
a single and integrated IRRP covering the entire geographic extent of the Marshall Islands (i.e., Majuro, Ebeye,
and Outer Islands).


The key steps to be implemented include:


(i) The review of the underlying assumptions (especially the demand forecast, and renewable potential)
used in the existing IRRP for Majuro. Preparation of underlying assumptions to be used in the expanded
and integrated IRRP, covering Majuro, Ebeye and Outer Islands.
(ii) Assessment of prevailing conditions, and any material changes, affecting the least-cost pathway,
including:
     a. Demand projections.
     b. Fuel prices.
     c. Technology potential and costs.
     d. Resilience considerations.
     e. Renewable integration requirements, including storage deployment needs.
     f. Policy or regulatory developments.
(iii) Realization of high-level modelling and analytical updates, as required.
(iv) Confirmation of priority development trajectories for generation, storage, transmission, and distribution
investments in the Marshall Islands (covering Majuro, Ebeye, and Outer Islands).
(v) Preparation of the integrated and updated Marshall Islands IRRP document.


Task 3. Preparation and update of the energy sector investment pipeline


The Consultant shall develop a consolidated, prioritized, and sequenced pipeline of energy sector investments.


The Consultant will undertake the following:


(i) Consolidation of existing project pipelines and studies.
(ii) Update of investment requirements identified in the updated IRRP prepared under Task 2 and covering
the full geographic extent of the Marshall Islands, and related studies.
(iii) Identification of additional investment needs where gaps are identified.
(iv) Categorization of investments by subsector and implementation timeframe.
(v) Preliminary costing and sequencing of investments.
(vi) Identification of priority and near-term investments.
(vii) Development of an implementation-oriented investment pipeline, including both generation and
        power grid infrastructure.

It is suggested that the following investment categories be used to group investments by type: renewable
energy; storage; transmission; distribution; resilience investments; grid modernization; energy Access; energy
efficiency; and e-mobility infrastructure.


Task 4. Renewable energy and storage target refinement


This phase is designed to support the operationalization of national renewable energy and storage ambitions
within the ESIP framework.


The Consultant shall undertake the following:
(i) Review of existing renewable energy and storage targets.
(ii) Assessment of the degree of consistency between targets, investment requirements, and implementation
      capacity.
(iii) Refinement of indicative deployment trajectories where required.
(iv) Identification of enabling investments needed to support achievement of targets.
(v) Assessment of the implications for grid infrastructure and flexibility requirements.


It is important to note that the ESIP supports refinement and operationalization of existing targets rather than
formulation of entirely new national policy targets unless specifically directed.


Task 5. Preparation of the financing strategy


Under this phase, a comprehensive financing approach for implementation of the ESIP will be developed.
The Consultant will undertake the following:
     (i) Estimation of financing requirements by subsector and timeframe.
     (ii) Assessment of the public and private financing opportunities.
     (iii) Identification of potential development partner and climate finance sources.
     (iv) Assessment of opportunities for private sector participation and PPP models.
     (v) Identification of financing gaps and constraints.
     (vi) Development of recommendations for investment mobilization and project preparation.


The Consultant is expected to consider possible financing from the Marshall Islands’ public Budget; IFIs and
MDBs; climate finance; green finance instruments; IPPs/PPP structures; and commercial finance sources.


Task 6. Preparation of the policy reform and enabling actions roadmap


The aim of this phase is to identify priority policy, regulatory, institutional, and implementation measures
required to support delivery of the ESIP in practice in the Marshall Islands.


The Consultant will undertake the following activities:
     (i) Identification of barriers affecting implementation of priority investments.
     (ii) Review of the investment-related policy and regulatory gaps.
     (iii) Assessment of permitting, procurement, and institutional coordination challenges.
     (iv) Identification of utility and institutional capacity needs.
     (v) Development of a phased roadmap of enabling actions and reforms.


Task 7. Preparation of the E-Mobility investment and strategic framework

This phase involves the assessment of implications of e-mobility development for the energy sector of the
Marshall Islands and identifies the associated investment and implementation requirements.


The Consultant will undertake the following:
     (i) Review of the existing transport and e-mobility policies and initiatives.
     (ii) Assessment of the expected electricity demand implications of e-mobility uptake.
     (iii) Identification of charging infrastructure investment requirements.
     (iv) Assessment of the main grid and distribution system implications.
     (v) Identification of priority implementation actions and enabling measures.
     (vi) Development of a high-level e-mobility framework aligned with the ESIP.


It is important to note that this framework is a targeted strategic and investment assessment linked specifically
to the Marshall Islands’ energy sector, not a standalone national transport strategy.


Task 8. Design of the ESIP monitoring and implementation framework


This phase comprises the development of a framework for monitoring implementation progress and investment
delivery.


The Consultant will undertake the following activities:


     (i) Definition of the implementation monitoring indicators.
     (ii) Development of reporting and governance arrangements.
     (iii) Identification of institutional responsibilities.
     (iv) Establishment of investment tracking mechanisms.
     (v) Development of implementation milestones and review mechanisms.
     (vi) Preparation of proposals on periodic ESIP update procedures.


It is anticipated that the monitoring and implementation framework will focus on the following key areas (and
others, as appropriate): investment delivery; financing mobilization; renewable deployment; grid expansion;
storage integration; e-mobility rollout; and resilience implementation.


Task 9. Stakeholder engagement, consultations and results validation


The Consultant will consult with and validate key assumptions and contents of the prepared ESIP with key
stakeholders, as appropriate, and to ensure alignment, ownership, and validation of the ESIP.


The Consultant will undertake the following activities:
     (i) Planning and moderation of a stakeholder workshop to present the overall project outputs.
     (ii)Realization of technical consultations as required, and consultations with MEC and the Marshall Islands
          government.
     (iii) Validation of prioritization and financing assumptions


Task 10. Outer-island mini-grid concept design


This phase responds to the need to improve electricity supply on selected outer islands by developing concept-
level designs for island mini-grids (and, where technically suitable, mesh-grid configurations). The concept
designs will inform and feed directly into the integrated IRRP (Task 2) and the energy sector investment
pipeline (Task 3).

The Consultant will undertake the following activities:

     (i) Screening and prioritization of outer islands for mini-grid / mesh-grid intervention, based on
          agreed technical, demand, and socio-economic criteria.
     (ii) Assessment of existing electricity supply, demand profiles, and renewable resource potential (in
           particular solar and storage) for the selected islands.
     (iii) Development of concept-level system configurations, including indicative generation, storage,
           and distribution sizing, and consideration of mini-grid versus mesh-grid architectures.
     (iv) Preliminary technical design and equipment specifications sufficient to support investment
           costing.
      (v) Indicative capital and operating cost estimates and implementation sequencing for each
            prioritized island.
     (vi) Integration of the resulting concept designs and associated investment needs into the integrated
            IRRP and the ESIP investment pipeline.

It is important to note that this task provides concept-level design to inform investment prioritization and
costing, and does not extend to detailed engineering design or tender-ready documentation, which would be
undertaken under subsequent project preparation.


6. Qualifications, Tasks, and Level of Effort of Specified Key Experts


The Consultant shall propose a team adequate for the assignment. In its proposal, the Consultant shall specify:


Each proposed key personnel position;
The name of the proposed expert, where available;
Role and responsibilities;
Minimum and actual qualifications and detailed relevant experience;
Whether the input is international or national / local;
Whether the input is home office or field-based;
Estimated level of effort in person-days or person-months; and
Anticipated timing of deployment and deployment location(s).


At a minimum, the Consultant is expected to consider inclusion of expertise and an indicative level of effort and
split of on-site and remote deployment, as follows:

Expert Position

Key Tasks / Responsibilities

Minimum Qualifications / Experience

Int’l / Nat’l

Team Leader / Senior Energy Sector Specialist

Overall project management and project coordination; lead stakeholder engagement and consultations. Provision of strategic oversight across all workstreams; ensure alignment with the Energy Strategy and IRRP; oversee preparation of all draft and final deliverables; coordinate quality assurance and reporting to the client.

Advanced degree in energy, engineering, economics, public policy, or related field.

10 years of relevant experience in energy sector planning, investment planning, or sector reform.

Demonstrated experience leading similar national-level energy sector assignments.

Strong stakeholder coordination and report-writing experience.

Power System Planning and Renewable Energy Specialist

Review and validate the least-cost development pathway and investment assumptions. Assess renewable energy and storage deployment requirements; Support investment pipeline development and sequencing; Assess transmission, distribution, resilience, and grid integration requirements. Support assessment of e-mobility impacts on the power system.

Advanced degree in electrical engineering, energy systems, or related field.

At least 8 years of experience in power system planning, renewable energy integration, transmission/distribution planning, or energy modelling.

Experience of national or utility-scale planning studies is preferred.

International

Energy Finance and Investment Specialist

Lead the development of the financing strategy; assess investment costs and financing requirements.

Identify public and private financing options, climate finance opportunities, and PPP/IPP structures.

Support investment prioritization and affordability assessment and investment mobilization recommendations.

At least 8 years of experience in infrastructure finance, energy sector investment planning, project finance, or climate finance.

Experience working with development finance institutions and private sector financing structures is advantageous.

International

Policy, Regulatory and Institutional Specialist

Assess policy, regulatory, and institutional barriers affecting implementation of priority investments.

Support preparation of the enabling actions and policy reform roadmap. Assess institutional coordination and implementation arrangements.

Support the development of the monitoring and implementation framework.

Contribute to stakeholder engagement activities.

Advanced degree in law, public policy, economics, energy policy, or related field.

At least 8 years of experience in energy sector policy, regulation, institutional reform, or utility governance. Experience supporting implementation-focused energy sector programs preferred.

International

Local Energy Sector / Stakeholder Engagement Specialist

Support local stakeholder coordination, data collection, institutional engagement, workshop organization, and review of local sector context.

 

Facilitation of coordination with government agencies, utilities, and local stakeholders. Support in project logistics and consultation activities.

Relevant degree in energy, engineering, economics, public administration, or related field.

Minimum 5 years of local sector experience.

Strong knowledge of the Marshall Islands’ energy sector institutions, policies, and stakeholder environment.

Fluency in English and Marshallese is desirable.

National

7. Fees and Reimbursable Expenses


As this engagement will be structured as a lump-sum contract, the Consultant shall submit a financial proposal
(in addition to a technical proposal) that includes:


A total lump-sum price for the performance of the services, payable against the deliverables set out
in Section VIII, supported by a breakdown of professional fees by each proposed expert and personnel
category, indicating the applicable unit rates and estimated level of effort (person-months or person-
days), provided for information purposes; and
Reimbursable expenses, included within the lump-sum price, covering any anticipated travel,
accommodation, per diem, logistics, communications, and other project-related costs necessary for the
performance of the services.


The lump-sum price shall be inclusive of all costs necessary for the performance of the services. The Consultant
shall clearly state the assumptions underlying the proposed costs and provide sufficient detail to allow MEC to
assess the reasonableness of the proposed budget.


8. Deliverables
The project has six (6) main deliverables, as follows:


1. Inception report. This deliverable will include confirmation of the project methodology, workplan,
stakeholder engagement approach, data requirements, consultation schedule, and detailed approach for
preparation of the ESIP. An Inception workshop will be conducted with MEC and other relevant stakeholders
within 2 weeks from the Notice to Proceed to discuss the proposed program of activities and to seek feedback
on improvements, which will be reflected in the inception report.


2. Sector assessment and planning review report. This will be a consolidated report covering: (i) targeted
sector diagnostics; (ii) the results of the review and validation/update of the least-cost development pathway;
(iii) assessment of renewable energy and storage deployment trajectories; and (iv) the assessment of e-mobility
implications and associated investment needs.


3. Updated and integrated IRRP. This IRRP document will cover the full geographic extent of the Marshall
Islands. It will include all relevant updates to the existing 2024 IRRP on Majuro, as well as Ebeye and Outer
Islands. It will be an integrated and fully updated document. (The document may be prepared directly editingthe existing (2024) IRRP document in MS Word version, with all revisions and additions shown in track change
format).
4. Draft investment pipeline and financing strategy report. This report will cover the updated and prioritized
investment pipeline; and the investment sequencing and indicative costing. Furthermore, the report will set out
the proposed financing strategy and investment mobilization approaches; and the policy reform and enabling
actions roadmap. It will also present the outer-island mini-grid and mesh-grid concept designs and their
integration into the investment pipeline (Task 10).


5. Draft Energy Sector Investment Programme (Draft ESIP). This will be an integrated draft ESIP
consolidating all technical analyses, investment priorities, financing approaches, implementation arrangements,
the implementation monitoring framework, and stakeholder consultation outcomes for review and validation.


6. Final Energy Sector Investment Programme (Final ESIP). Final ESIP incorporating key stakeholder
comments. It will include the finalized investment pipeline, financing strategy, implementation roadmap, the
implementation monitoring framework, executive summary, and supporting annexes and presentation materials.


9. Contract Duration
The contract duration is 12 months. The expected start date is estimated to be in September 2026.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

Region: Central Asia, Aral Sea Basin

Countries: Republic of Kazakhstan (the Executive Committee of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea and the Project Implementation Unit are currently based in Astana; on 1 January 2027, the three-year chairmanship of IFAS will be transferred from Kazakhstan to Uzbekistan, and the Project Implementation Unit is expected to be established in Uzbekistan under the Executive Committee of IFAS no later than 1 May 2027), Republic of Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Republic of Uzbekistan.

Project: Central Asia Water Efficiency Cooperation Project under Phase 3 of the Multiphase Programmatic Approach (hereinafter referred to as the “Project” or “CAWEC”)

Grant No.: E709-7C

Assignment Title: Environmental and Social Consultant for the Project Implementation Unit (PIU)

Contract No.: CAWEC-4-CS-IND-4.2

The Executive Committee of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (EC IFAS) received funding from the International Development Association (World Bank) for implementation of the Central Asia Water Efficiency Cooperation Project (CAWEC) and intends to use the funds to pay for advisory services under the Project.

The Executive Committee of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (EC IFAS) is the Implementing Agency of the Project (hereinafter referred to as “EC IFAS”).

The Project Development Objective is to facilitate climate-resilient investments and strengthen the capacity of regional water resources management institutions in Central Asia. The Project is part of a Multiphase Programmatic Approach (MPA) and comprises three components: (i) Preparation of Transboundary Projects; (ii) Information Support and Digitalization for Improved Regional Water Resources Management and Climate Resilience; and (iii) Institutional Strengthening and Capacity Building. The Project aims to strengthen and expand cooperation among countries in the Aral Sea Basin.

           To ensure efficient implementation of the Project, EC IFAS intends to hire an individual consultant for the position of Environmental and Social Consultant

        The objective of the assignment is to ensure effective and integrated support of the Project implementation, including evaluation of risks to environment and society, including relevant vulnerable groups, to build capacity in member countries' water resources management and irrigation sectors, and implementation of principles and standards of International and Industry Best Practice and promoting sustainable practices in the water resources management and irrigation sectors.

  

       Qualification Requirements: university degree in environmental studies, social sciences, or a related field; knowledge of the environmental and social standards of international financial institutions, including the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF); experience in environmental and social risk assessment, stakeholder engagement, reporting, and the delivery of training activities; experience working on projects in the water sector, climate change adaptation, or regional cooperation; and proficiency in MS Office. Experience with Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and familiarity with the institutional framework of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (IFAS) will be considered an advantage.

 

The Consulting Services (the "Services") include the following main functions:

  1. Identifying and promptly addressing environmental and social issues arising during Project implementation;
  2. Compliance with applicable national laws and World Bank Group rules, procedures and standards;
  3. Participation in the preparation of the Project Operations Manual (POM) within the scope of their responsibilities;
  4. Reviewing, as necessary, the Project Procurement for Development Strategy (PPSD), Environmental and Social Commitment Plan, (ESCP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP);
  5. Preparation of Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) where required in accordance with the Project requirements;
  6. Preparing relevant reports;
  7. Maintaining regular communication and coordination with the environmental and social specialists of the national Project Implementation Units (PIUs) on matters related to compliance with the Project’s environmental and social requirements;
  8. Other related tasks (detailed information is attached in the Terms of reference).

     The Environmental and Social Consultant is expected to carry out preparations and deliver the following results:

1. Develop, coordinate, review, submit, and, where necessary, revise environmental and social documentation in accordance with the approved Work Plan and decisions of the Regional Steering Committee (RSC).
2. Develop and implement relevant documents and procedures in accordance with the World Bank’s operational policies and Environmental and Social Standards, including the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment (SESA), and Labour Management Procedures (LMP), as well as applicable national legislation.
3. Develop training materials and deliver training programmes, including training on the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), Project documentation, and issues related to gender-based violence (GBV), sexual exploitation and abuse, and sexual harassment (SEA/SH).
4. Prepare timely reports on capacity-building activities and the results achieved.
5. Prepare coordination plans and reports on engagement with relevant stakeholders and national project implementation teams.           
6. Maintain timely and constructive engagement with the World Bank and obtain the necessary clearances and approvals.
7. Assess environmental and social complaints and grievances in a timely manner in accordance with World Bank procedures and prepare periodic reports for the World Bank. 
8. Monitor, document, and report on the impacts, risks, and outcomes of Project implementation.
9. Provide recommendations on environmental and social matters, stakeholder engagement, and institutional processes within the Project. 
10. Establish and maintain a comprehensive electronic archive of environmental and social documentation, including spatial data.

The duration of the assignment is 6 months from the contract signing date (but no later than May 1, 2027).

Terms of employment: part-time (8-10 working days per month). Duty station: Astana. 

The full Terms of Reference, including qualification requirements, are available on the EC IFAS website at the following link: https://ecifas.kz/publication/

The Executive Committee of International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (the "Client") invites eligible individual consultants ("Consultants") to express interest in providing consulting services for the position of CAWEC Procurement Specialist.

Interested Consultants should provide information confirming necessary qualifications and experience to perform the Services, including a current CV, details of similar assignments, and other documentation evidencing qualifications and professional experience.

Expressions of interest should include the following:

  • An up-to-date CV;
  • description of the experience with performing similar assignments;
  • Information on projects financed by international financial institutions (if any);
  • Letters of recommendation and customer feedback (if any).

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.13, 3.15 and 3.16 of Section III of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, version September 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), which describe the World Bank's policy regarding conflict of interest.

The consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set forth in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Borrowers (September 2025).

            For more information, please contact the address below during working hours from 08:30 to 17:00 (Astana time).

        Expressions of interest must be submitted no later than November 23, 2026, by e-mail or to the address indicated below:

Executive Committee of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea     
Central Asia Water Efficiency Cooperation (CAWEC) Project         
Project Implementation Unit (PIU)

Attention: Saule Shalmaganbetova, Head of the Information and Analytical Department of the Executive Committee of IFAS   
Email: Shalmaganbetova@ecifas.kz

Cc: A. Temirbekova, PIU Procurement Specialist   
Email: anara.temirbekova@gmail.com

 

Address:

1 E-179 str., position 40, Astana, Republic of Kazakhstan

The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) and eight Pacific Island member countries (Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu) have received financing (grants and credits) from the World Bank Group's International Development Association (IDA) towards the Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project (the Project) and will apply part of these proceeds to the contract below for Consulting Services.

The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) is seeking a qualified and experienced national Finance Officer (FO) to support the financial management and administration of the Project, including financial reporting, budget monitoring, maintenance of financial records, and compliance with World Bank and PIFS requirements.

The Finance Officer will report to the Project Coordinator and will work closely with the Financial Management Specialist on a daily basis and with other PIFS staff, as relevant.

This is a full-time work assignment at the PMU housed within the PIFS office in Suva. In line with the project timeline, the engagement will initially be for two (2) years with an extension of a further two years (based on consultant's performance evaluations and project needs) thereafter, until 2030.

Under the overall direction of the Project Coordinator and the direct supervision of the Financial Management Specialist, the Finance Officer will support the financial management and administration of the Project, including:

  1. Processing and recording financial transactions.
  2. Maintaining financial records and supporting documentation.
  3. Monitoring project budgets and expenditures.
  4. Supporting the preparation of financial reports, withdrawal applications, and other financial documentation.
  5. Coordinating project payments and maintaining financial registers.
  6. Supporting audits, reconciliations, and compliance activities.
  7. Maintaining project financial filing systems.
  8. Providing financial and administrative support to project activities, workshops, meetings, and missions.
  9. Undertaking other finance-related duties as assigned.

 

Applicants will be evaluated based on the following criteria:

Mandatory Criteria

A minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in finance, accounting, bookkeeping, financial administration, or financial management, including experience supporting donor-funded, government-funded, regional, or development partner-funded projects.

Eligibility to Work in Fiji

  1. Project Overview

Project Name

Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project

Activity Reference Number (STEP)

FJ-PIFS-575741-CS-INDV

Position Title

Finance Officer

Location of Role

The position will be based at the Project PMU Office in PIFS, Suva, Fiji with possible travel to participating countries.

Eligibility

Must have the legal right to live and work in Fiji

Implementing Agency

Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS)

https://forumsec.org

Duration of Assignment

An initial two-year contract, with the possibility of a further two-year extension based on satisfactory performance, or until the Project's closing date of August 2030, whichever is earlier.

Agency Description

The Pacific Islands Forum was established to bring together the region to address pressing issues and challenges, and foster collaboration and cooperation in the pursuit of shared goals. PIF’s mandate is to strengthen cooperation and integration in the Pacific region through the pooling of regional governance, resources and the alignment of policies, furthering Forum members' shared goals of economic growth, sustainable development, good governance and security. Founded in 1971, it comprises 18 members: Australia, Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Kiribati, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Republic of Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu. The PIFS is a vital platform for Leaders to convene, engage in discussions and agree on policies that will benefit the people of the region.

Participating Countries

The Pacific Island Countries (PICs) participating in the regional project comprise Fiji, Solomon Islands, Kiribati, the Marshall Islands, Samoa, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.

Overall Project Objective

The Project Development Objective is to enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in the participating Pacific Island Countries.

Project Length

August 2024 to September 2030

 

  1. Project Background

The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat (PIFS) has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Development Association (IDA) and will act as the Implementing Agency for the regional Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project (the Project), which will enable continuous access to correspondent banking services in Pacific Island Countries (PICs). The PICs covered by the regional project include Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu.

Financial systems in PICs are characterized by low levels of financial access and uneven development of national payment systems. Commercial banks dominate the financial sector in all PICs. In several countries, significant portions of the population lack access to basic transaction accounts, limiting their ability to participate in economic activity and access financial services.

Correspondent Banking Relationships (CBRs) underpin international trade, tourism, remittances, and humanitarian financial flows. The withdrawal of these relationships presents significant risks to economic development and financial inclusion across the Pacific region.

To address these challenges, the World Bank is providing funding to PIFS to implement the Pacific Strengthening Correspondent Banking Relationships Project. The Project includes two components: (i) Temporary Correspondent Banking Services and (ii) Enabling Environment and Regulatory Harmonization. The Project is being implemented by a dedicated Project Management Unit (PMU) within PIFS.

PIFS seeks to recruit a qualified and experienced Finance Officer to support project financial management and administration functions within the PMU. The selection will be undertaken in accordance with the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and applicable project procedures.

 

2. Objective of the Position

The main objective of the Finance Officer is to support the Financial Management Specialist in ensuring sound financial management of the Project through the accurate and timely processing of financial transactions, maintenance of financial records, preparation of financial reports, and compliance with World Bank requirements, PIFS policies, and applicable statutory regulations.

 

Scope of Services

Under the overall direction of the Project Coordinator and the direct supervision of the Financial Management Specialist, the Finance Officer shall undertake the following activities:

i. Process and record financial transactions in accordance with project systems, procedures, and approved controls;

ii. Maintain accurate and up-to-date financial records, including invoices, receipts, payment vouchers, statements, and supporting documentation;

iii. Assist in monitoring project budgets and expenditures and support budget tracking activities;

iv. Assist with maintaining and updating project registers including Contracts, Leave, Assets, Withdrawal Applications, and other financial records;

v. Support the preparation of Interim Financial Reports (IFRs), Statements of Expenditure (SOEs), withdrawal applications, donor reports, and other financial reports as required;

vi. Coordinate project-related payments in accordance with PIFS financial procedures and World Bank requirements;

vii. Ensure financial transactions comply with project internal controls, donor requirements, and applicable financial regulations;

viii. Support project audits by preparing schedules, retrieving supporting documentation, and responding to audit queries;

ix. Assist with monthly account reconciliations and financial record verification processes;

x. Maintain organized filing systems for financial records in both electronic and hard-copy formats;

xi. Assist in monitoring consultant and supplier payments and contract financial obligations;

xii. Contribute to continuous improvement of financial management systems, procedures, and controls within the Project Management Unit;

xiii. Provide administrative and financial support to project activities, workshops, meetings, and missions as required;

xiv. Undertake any other finance-related duties assigned by the Financial Management Specialist or Project Coordinator.

 

 

3. Specific Contract Deliverables

The Finance Officer will be on probation for the first six months of the assignment. A performance evaluation will be undertaken against the deliverables listed below. Additional deliverables may be agreed with the Project Coordinator and Financial Management Specialist.

5. Institutional Arrangements

Introduction

JSC Georgian Economic Development Corporation (GEDC), within the Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Project supported by the World Bank (WB) intends to apply part of the loan proceeds for consulting services of Procurement Manager (National Consultant).

The Project Development Objective for the Relief and Recovery for MSME operation is to provide relief to MSMEs and support their recovery, including by strengthening the enabling environment for access to finance.

 

Project Description

The Project is being implemented nationwide and consist of four components:

Component 1 – Financial relief and recovery for MSMEs

Component 2 – Digital payments & financial infrastructure upgrading

Component 3 – Project management and monitoring

Component 4 – Contingent Emergency Response Component

A substantial portion of the Project activities fall under Component 1. The component will support the expansion of the following financial instruments implemented by GEDC: (a) grants for MSMEs through GEDC’s Micro and Small Entrepreneurship Support Program, (b) co-financing of interest payments through GEDC’s Produce in Georgia Program, and (c) partial credit guarantees (PCGs). The component will also provide non-financial support in the form of training and technical assistance to help firms adjust to new conditions, improve their business skills, and increase their resilience.

  • Sub-component 1.1 provide micro-grants to finance working capital and fixed assets for micro and small firms.
  • Sub-component 1.2 co-finance interest payments on loans underwritten by participating financial institutions (PFIs).
  • Sub-component 1.3 provide partial credit guarantees for loans issued by PFIs.
  • Sub-component 1.4 provide technical assistance for COVID-proofing and digitalization of MSMEs.

Scope of Work

Procurement Manager / Individual Consultant shall assist the GEDC in all procurement activities related to implementation of WB financed MSMEs Project in accordance with the New Procurement Framework  - Policy, Regulations, Guidance issued for the projects After July 1, 2016 according to the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers - PROCUREMENT IN INVESTMENT PROJECT FINANCING -  Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016 and revised in September 2025.

This includes not only procurement activities where GEDC is the beneficiary of the loan proceeds, but also the activities where GEDC is acting as a procuring agency for other agencies, which are final beneficiaries (GEDC’s fiduciary responsibilities are defined in the Loan Agreement).

Anticipated Procurement Activities

The remaining procurement activities under the Project may include, but are not limited to:

  • Event Organization Services: Procurement of services related to the organization and technical support of business events and other similar activities under the Project.

The scope and selection methods of these activities will be determined based on the Project's needs and the approved Procurement Plan, in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

Key Responsibilities

In order to achieve the objective of this contract, the Procurement Manager / Individual Consultant shall:

  • Lead the process of preparation of Project Procurement Plan, its update on a regular basis in close partnership with the GEDC in alignment with the WB rules and regulations;
  • Administer the entire process for the procurement cycle, ensuring compliance with the WB regulations:  selection of the appropriate procurement methods, preparation of the Terms of References, cost estimates, Requests for Expression of Interest, Requests for Quotations/Bids/Proposals, evaluation reports, participation in contracts’ negotiations and awards, as well as in contracts’ execution, getting the WB approvals, as appropriate.
  • Lead contract administration, including framework agreements and managing call-off contracts in each framework agreement.  
  • Keep all relevant procurement documentation on file in an orderly manner and make it available for the authorized national inspecting agencies, auditors, and the WB upon request;

  • Prepare quarterly and annual procurement reports including contract monitoring and management;
  • Cooperate with the GEDC for regular preparation of Project Management/Financial Reports, as part of the WB project and financial reporting requirements;
  • Participate in contract management, monitoring and supervision, including but not limited to ensuring timely submission of all deliverables specified under the contract.
  • Perform other procurement related tasks as required.

 

Qualification and experience

  • University-level degree in business administration, finance, law, or related discipline;
  • 5 (Five) years of practical experience as a procurement or contract specialist;
  • At least 3 (three) years of working experience in procurement and contract management of projects funded by the WB and/or other International Financial Institutions (IFIs);
  • Knowledge of the World Bank procurement regulations, local taxation, banking and other pertinent regulations affecting national and international procurement;
  • Experience with World Bank Systematic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement (STEP) portal;
  • Proven teamwork skills;
  • Superior verbal and writing communication skills in Georgian;
  • Strong verbal, reading and writing skills in English;
  • Good negotiating skills;
  • Proficiency in various software under OS Windows (MS Office, Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access, Adobe).

Reporting

The Individual Consultant shall directly report to the Project Manager.

Facilities and Services to be provided by the Client
