Assignment Title: Senior International Advisor for Forestry Sector Reform in Moldova

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MD-NOIEP-577223-CS-INDV

Moldova “Restoring Ecosystems for Marine Pollution Prevention” (REMAP) Project, financed by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and supported by the World Bank, is implemented through the National Office for the Implementation of Environmental Projects (NOIEP) under the Ministry of Environment (MoE). REMAP is a flagship national initiative promoting Nature-based Solutions (NbS) to restore ecosystems and reduce land-based pollution in the Dniester River Basin. The project aligns with Moldova’s priorities under the EU approximation agenda, the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and the Paris Agreement, demonstrating that healthy, community-supported ecosystems underpin climate resilience and sustainable livelihoods.

REMAP supports ecosystem restoration and sustainable watershed management to reduce land-based nutrient pollution entering the Dniester River and ultimately the Black Sea. Its Project Development Objective is to increase the area under sustainable landscape management practices in targeted areas within the Dniester River Basin in Moldova. Institutional strengthening and improved forest governance, including implementation of the Forest Code No. 69/2024, are central to achieving this objective.

The Senior International Advisor shall serve as the Minister of Environment's principal international strategic and technical advisor on forestry sector reform. The Advisor shall provide independent, high-level guidance on transition implementation, governance modernization, EU accession alignment, and resource mobilization, while bringing relevant international experience to bear on Moldova's specific circumstances and priorities. All reform decisions and implementation authority remain with the competent national authorities.

The minimum qualifications and experience for the requested position are:

Education:

  • Advanced university degree in public administration, public policy, economics, environmental policy, law, organizational development, or related discipline. Qualifications or substantive professional experience in forestry, natural resource management, or environmental governance are a strong advantage.

Essential Requirements:

  • At least 15 years of relevant experience in high-level advisory roles, institutional reform, public-sector restructuring, state-owned enterprise transformation, or environmental governance, including demonstrated experience advising ministers or senior government officials.
  • Proven strategic advisory capacity: the ability to provide frank, forward-looking counsel to senior decision-makers on politically sensitive reform processes, not merely technical analysis.
  • Hands-on implementation experience in at least one substantial institutional or sector reform following formal political, legislative, or governmental decisions, including organizational integration, transition management, and stabilization. Experience limited to assessments or reform design is insufficient.
  • Experience in financial mobilization, including engagement with international donors, development banks, or climate finance mechanisms.
  • Strong understanding of EU accession processes and environmental acquis, particularly as they relate to forestry, land use, or natural resource management.
  • Excellent analytical, drafting, communication, and facilitation skills; fluency in English.

Desirable:

  • Reform experience in Baltic, Balkan, Eastern European, or post-Soviet EU candidate country contexts.
  • Experience with anti-corruption frameworks, digital governance, or transparency systems in natural resource sectors.
  • Knowledge of carbon markets, ecosystem service payments, or climate finance instruments.
  • Familiarity with World Bank or EU-financed operations.
  • Proficiency in Romanian and/or Russian is a significant advantage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. Ukraine has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Housing Repair for People’s Empowerment Project (HOPE) (the “Project”) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services under Component 3 “Project Management and Capacity Strengthening”.

The consulting services (the “Services”) comprise implementation, analytical support and technical support for the State Register of Damaged and Destroyed Property (RDDP or the “Register”). The assignment aims to support the continuous functioning and effective use of the Register and the services implemented on its basis, and to strengthen the Client’s institutional capacity.

The Services cover five principal service areas:

  1. First-line support and service request analysis: receive, register, classify and analyse user requests; resolve routine issues; escalate matters requiring the Registry Administrator (L2) or the Client (L3); track requests through resolution; and identify recurring issues and best practices.
  2. Implementation support: support the roll-out and use of RDDP services and new or updated functionality, update user instructions and collect feedback on implementation.
  3. Knowledge Base: maintain, populate, structure and update the RDDP Knowledge Base, including guidance, frequently asked questions and documented resolution practices.
  4. User training and methodological support: deliver regular training, webinars and consultations; prepare learning materials; and transfer practical knowledge to users and designated MRIT representatives.
  5. Data analytics and dashboards: configure, maintain and develop Power BI dashboards and analytical reports; support data integration, ETL processes and data quality; and transfer dashboards, documentation and configurations to the Client.

Duration and contract arrangements

The Services are expected to commence upon the contract’s entry into force, and continue until November 30, 2027. The contract duration may be extended by mutual agreement of the parties in the event of an extension of the Project implementation timelines.

The Services shall be provided under a Time-Based contract, with payment based on actual person-hours worked, supported by approved monthly timesheets and Consolidated Reports. Approval is subject to the applicable service levels and reporting requirements specified in the Terms of Reference (ToR). The estimated level of effort is up to 45,360 person-hours. This estimate is indicative and non-binding; the Client has no obligation to utilise the full estimated number of hours.

The Consultant shall use Jira Service Management or an equivalent service request management system and other software necessary for the assignment. Microsoft Power BI licences shall be procured and administered by the Consultant as reimbursable costs, subject to the Client’s prior approval and evidence of price reasonableness, in accordance with the ToR and the Contract.

L1 ticket receipt, logging, handling and resolution shall be provided from 08:00 to 20:00 on Business Days (12×5), with escalation and continued monitoring of Critical Tickets as specified in the SLA. Weekly operational reports and monthly consolidated and time and effort reports shall be submitted in accordance with the ToR.

Detailed information on the scope, deliverables, reporting, staffing and Service Level Agreement (SLA) is provided in the attached Terms of Reference.

Qualification criteria for the Consultant firm

The Ministry for Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport of Ukraine (MRIT) (the “Client”) invites eligible consulting firms (the “Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants shall provide information demonstrating the qualifications and relevant experience required to perform the Services. The firm-level criteria are set out below.

No.

Criterion and Requirement

Assessment

1.

Financial Capabilities

Minimum average annual turnover of USD 600 000 equivalent, calculated as total certified payments received for contracts in progress and/or completed within the last 3 (three) years, divided by 3 (three) years.

technical support (helpdesk/service desk) of an information system with at least 1,000 active users;

Pass/Fail

Pass/Fail

Mobilization Capacity and Operational Readiness

The Consultant shall demonstrate the organizational and operational capacity to mobilize the required team and commence service delivery within 10 calendar days of contract signing. To confirm this, the Consultant shall provide a concise mobilization plan and staffing availability confirmation.

Pass/Fail

The requirements above reproduce the firm qualification criteria in the ToR. Mandatory qualification requirements shall be assessed on a Pass/Fail basis. Experience described as an advantage is not a mandatory qualification requirement.

For a JV, the combined assessment rules set out under “Associations and conflict of interest” shall apply. The Pass/Fail assessment shall apply to the JV as a whole. The mobilization plan and staffing availability confirmation shall cover the JV’s proposed service delivery arrangements, identifying the responsibilities and resources of the relevant members.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at this stage of the procurement process. Individual CVs and full Technical and Financial Proposals are not required with the EOI. Key personnel qualifications will be reviewed at the proposal stage in accordance with the RFP and the ToR.

Information to be included in the Expression of Interest

To demonstrate its qualifications and experience, each Consultant shall submit:

  1. A letter expressing interest in the assignment, identifying the Consultant and any proposed association, and providing the name and contact details of the authorised representative.
  2. A description of the firm’s core business, organisation, technical and managerial capacity, and staffing resources relevant to the Services.
  3. Information substantiating average annual turnover under Criterion 1, including certified payment amounts for the last three years, the calculation of the average and supporting financial records.
  4. Relevant contract/project references demonstrating compliance with the mandatory experience requirements and, where provided, experience described in the ToR as an advantage. Each reference shall state the project title, client, country/location, funding source, objectives and a brief description of the project, contract value, commencement and completion dates, current status, the firm’s role and percentage share of participation in the contract (both in percentage and monetary terms), and the functions and outputs actually delivered. Any affiliated or parent firm and its role shall be identified separately.
  5. Supporting evidence for the cited assignments, such as relevant contract extracts, completion or acceptance certificates, client references or other documents confirming successful performance and the claimed experience. References shall clearly identify the information-system user numbers, public-sector/registry context, BI tools, Knowledge Base activities and training participant numbers, as applicable.
  6. A concise mobilization plan and staffing availability confirmation demonstrating the ability to commence service delivery within 10 calendar days of contract signing.
  7. The qualifications and experience summary below, with clear cross-references to supporting contracts, documents and EOI pages.

For a JV, each member shall provide its own supporting financial information under Criterion 1, and the EOI shall include the combined turnover calculation for the JV. Each contract or project reference and each training participant total claimed under Criteria 2–6 shall identify the JV member whose experience is being relied upon, its role and the services it actually performed. The qualifications and experience summary table shall identify the relevant JV member or members and cross-reference their supporting evidence.

The same contract or project may be referenced under more than one criterion where it demonstrates the respective experience. The relevant scope and the Consultant’s own contribution shall be clearly identified.

Associations and conflict of interest

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, provided that the total number of firms in the association (including joint venture partners and/or sub-consultants) shall not exceed 3 (three) entities and shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. The EOI shall identify the proposed roles and the firm responsible for each cited assignment. The qualifications of sub-consultants shall not be taken into account in evaluating the Consultant for shortlisting.

For a joint venture (JV), the requirements under Criteria 2-7 shall be assessed on the basis of the combined qualifications and experience of all JV members. No JV member shall be required individually to meet the full requirements under these criteria.

For Criterion 1, the JV’s average annual turnover shall be calculated by adding the total certified payments received by all JV members over the same three-year period specified in the criterion and dividing that sum by three. For contracts previously performed as a member of another JV, only payments attributable to the respective member’s own participation shall be included.

For Criteria 2, 4, 5 and 6, qualifying contract and project references and training participant totals of JV members may be combined. Each reference shall satisfy the applicable requirements of the relevant criterion. Separate contracts or projects shall not be combined to satisfy a requirement that must be met within a single contract or project. The same contract, project or training activity shall not be counted more than once under the same criterion solely because more than one JV member participated in it. Experience gained under a previous JV contract shall be assessed on the basis of the services actually performed by the respective member, supported by appropriate evidence.

Participants are responsible for conducting their own due diligence to identify institutional or other relationships between the Consultant, joint venture members or sub-consultants and entities involved in Project management or implementation, including MRIT, the Registry Administrator and entities involved in developing or operating the RDDP.

In particular, participation of state-owned enterprises or institutions as joint venture members or sub-consultants may raise conflict-of-interest or eligibility issues where an institutional relationship with the Project Implementing Agency, Ministry for Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport of Ukraine (MRIT), is relevant under paragraphs 3.17(d) and 3.23(b)(iii) of the Procurement Regulations. Such relationships shall be fully disclosed in the EOI. Failure to disclose relevant information, or identification of a conflict of interest or ineligibility under the Procurement Regulations, may result in rejection of the EOI.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17, of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers for Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Fourth Edition, November 2020 (the “Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest, and paragraph 3.18 concerning unfair competitive advantage.

Selection method

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. The relative weights of technical quality and cost, the minimum technical proposal score and the proposal evaluation criteria will be specified in the RFP.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-IC-NIO-7.13.1 – Regional Project Manager 1)

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

Grant No. TF0C5794

Assignment Title: Regional Project Manager 1

Reference No. LEARN-IC-NIO-7.13.1

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is implementing projects financed by the World Bank, including: Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (UIHERP) and Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine Program (LEARN) Program and plans to prepare and implement new operations in cooperation with the World Bank (hereinafter referred to as the Operation(s)).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan). The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of the Consultant's assignment is to manage and coordinate the implementation of NUS reform initiatives within the designated geographical area, ensure effective adaptation of national programs to the regional context, and maintain close cooperation with local education authorities.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time November 24, 2026.  

TERMS OF REFERENCE

 

for consulting services (individual consultant)

 

Regional Project Manager 1

 

Contract No. LEARN-IC-NIO-7.13.1

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

URTF Grant No. TF0C5794

 

 BACKGROUND

 

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is implementing projects financed by the World Bank, including: Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (UIHERP) and Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine Program (LEARN) Program and plans to prepare and implement new operations in cooperation with the World Bank (hereinafter referred to as the Operation(s)).

LEARN

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School”” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The total LEARN financing amounts to US$737 mln provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) – US$675,9 mln and Investment Project Financing (IPF) – US$61.1 mln.

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is funded by a US$235 mln credit provided by Bank resources, supported by credit enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT NUMBER 9721-UA). An additional US$150 mln is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (LOAN NUMBER 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT NUMBER 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million. On June 9, 2026, the Loan Agreement (Third Additional Financing for the Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development was signed in the amount of US$286 mln (LOAN NUMBER K019-UA).

 

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT NUMBER TF0C5794).

On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

For this program, “strategic communication and public engagement” refer to three critical aspects of ensuring the effective implementation of education policies and public trust in reforms:

i. Transparency and trust, including timely and clear communication about key initiatives, accessible information for stakeholders, and proactive crisis communication strategies to address concerns and misinformation.

ii. Awareness and outreach, especially the development of targeted campaigns, public information materials, and digital engagement strategies to ensure broad understanding and support for educational transformations among educators, parents, students, and policymakers.

iii. Capacity building in communication, ensuring that education institutions, regional authorities, and key stakeholders are equipped with the necessary tools, guidelines, and skills to effectively communicate and engage with the public regarding policy changes, funding mechanisms, and international support programs.

Effective communication is a key instrument for building trust in education reforms, shaping public perception, and ensuring stakeholder engagement. The Operation of the World Bank is inlined with the Strategic Action Plan and Communications vision of the Ministry.

 OBJECTIVE

 

The objective of this assignment is to manage and coordinate the implementation of NUS reform initiatives within the designated geographical area, ensure effective adaptation of national programs to the regional context, and maintain close cooperation with local education authorities.

 SCOPE OF SERVICES

The Consultant shall provide the following services, including but not limited to:

  • Manages the implementation of NUS reform initiatives in the designated geographical area.
  • Coordinates with local education authorities and stakeholders to ensure effective implementation of the reform.
  • Monitors progress and implementation challenges of the reform at the regional level.
  • Provides feedback on regional adaptation needs and implementation challenges to NIO management.
  • Supports capacity-building activities of regional education institutions.
  • Maintains regular communication with regional stakeholders.

REPORTING

The Regional Managers Coordinator reports to the LEARN Project Coordinator / Co-Coordinator and works under the supervision of the Head of the New Ukrainian School (NUS) Implementation Office. In carrying out their duties, the Consultant works closely with the Deputy Heads of the NUS Implementation Office and the Heads of the relevant functional units to ensure coordinated planning, management, and implementation of communication activities across the NUS reform portfolio.

The Consultant shall submit monthly reports describing the tasks performed, key results achieved, and challenges identified..

 RESOURCES PROVIDED

MoES provides the Consultant with the information necessary to perform his/her assignment in a timely manner. At the same time, the Consultant independently arranges his/her own workplace, including the equipment necessary to perform his/her functions (e.g., PC, communication means and office equipment).

 QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

  • At least 2 years of experience in managing education projects and administering/implementing them
  • At least 1 year of experience in cooperation with national and local authorities
  • At least 2 years of experience in the education sector, preferably in school education
  • Experience in cooperation with international financial or donor organizations
  • High level of English proficiency (upper intermediate or above)
  • Fluency in Ukrainian

Desirable skills and qualifications:

  • Experience in managing education projects
  • Knowledge of the specifics of the regional education system
  • Understanding of project management methodologies
  • Knowledge of the principles and objectives of the NUS reform
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail
  • Excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills
  • Ability to work under conditions of high uncertainty
  • Crisis management experience

 

 DURATION AND PLACE OF WORK

The Consultant shall provide services until 31 August 2028, with the possibility of extending the contract term until the completion of the LEARN Operation.

The Consultant is expected to work on a full-time basis.

Services are planned to be provided in Kyiv, Ukraine. Business trips of the Consultant to other regions of Ukraine may be required to support the implementation of the Operation.

The Consultant may be expected to provide services remotely; however, at the Client's request, he/she shall arrive and/or provide services at the Client's premises as soon as possible.

Contract terms and working arrangements are subject to negotiation.

APPLICATION PACKAGE

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua, Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org and maryna.chubenko@mon.gov.ua  indicating the email subject: " LEARN-IC-NIO-7.13.1: Selection of Regional Project Manager 1: [NAME]".

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time November 24, 2026.

If the Consultant fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the Consultant's application.

The Government of the Federal Republic of Somalia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Somali Sustainable Fisheries Development Badmaal Project (SSFDP) and intends to apply part of the proceed for consulting services.

The Consulting Services include institutional strengthening of fisheries cooperatives and associations in the Phase 1 pilot locations of Hirshabelle (Warsheikh and Elmaan), Jubaland (Calanley and Madawa), and Banadir Regional Administration (Mogadishu). REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

SEYCHELLES

GFPP - Seychelles’ Transformative and Resilient Inclusive Digital Economy (STRIDE)

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: P515960

 

Assignment Title: Recruitment of an Environmental and Social (E&S) Specialist

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): SC-DICT-002-CS-INV

 

The Government of Seychelles has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the GFPP - Seychelles’ Transformative and Resilient Inclusive Digital Economy (STRIDE), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include providing dedicated environmental and social risk management support to the STRIDE Project Implementation Unit (PIU) to ensure that all project activities are prepared, implemented, monitored, and reported in compliance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), including the Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs), and the environmental and social regulatory requirements of Seychelles. The Services will encompass the identification and assessment of environmental and social risks and impacts, preparation and implementation of required environmental and social instruments, monitoring of mitigation measures, stakeholder engagement, grievance management, capacity building, and periodic reporting to support effective environmental and social risk management throughout the project lifecycle. The duration of the Services is 12 months from the date of contract effectiveness, with the possibility of extension through Project implementation, subject to satisfactory performance and availability of funds.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The Department of Information Communications Technology (DICT) now invites eligible individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • A minimum of a Bachelor’s degree (BSc) in Environmental Science, Social Science, Development Studies, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resource Management, or a related field. A Master’s degree (MSc) in a relevant discipline is an advantage.
  • At least [7] years of relevant work experience (BSc) or [5] years of relevant work experience (MSc) in environmental and social risk management.
  • Demonstrated experience in environmental management for small to medium-scale civil works, or construction of critical information infrastructures (e.g., data centres and submarine cables).
  • Experience preparing and implementing Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), or equivalent environmental and social instruments.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment:

1. The Bank requires that Consultants:

  • provide professional, objective and impartial advice;
  •  at all times hold the Borrower’s interests paramount, without any consideration of future work; and
  • in providing advice, avoid conflicts with other assignments and their own interests.

2. Consultants shall not be hired for any assignment that would be in conflict with their prior or current obligations to other clients, or that may place them in a position of being unable to carry out the assignment in the best interests of the Borrower. Without limitation on the generality of the foregoing, Consultants shall not be hired under the circumstances set forth below:

  • for any assignment that, by its nature, creates a conflict of interest with another assignment of the Consultant;
  • Consultants that have a close business or family relationship with a professional staff of the Borrower, or of the project implementing agency, or of a recipient of a part of the Bank’s financing, or any other party representing or acting on behalf of the Borrower, that is directly or indirectly involved in any part of:
  1. the preparation of the TOR for the assignment;
  2. the selection process for the contract; or
  3. the supervision of the contract; may not be awarded a contract, unless the conflict stemming from this relationship has been resolved in a manner acceptable to the Bank throughout the selection process and the execution of the contract.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (08:00 to 16:00 hours).

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail,) by 24th November 2026.

Department of Information Communications Technology

Attn: Mr. Benjamin Choppy - Principal Secretary

3rd Floor, Caravelle House

P. O. Box 737

Victoria

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: P515960

 

Assignment Title: Recruitment of Procurement Specialist

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): SC-DICT-001-CS-INV

 

The Government of Seychelles has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the GFPP - Seychelles’ Transformative and Resilient Inclusive Digital Economy (STRIDE), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) providing procurement management support to the STRIDE Project Implementation Unit (PIU) to ensure that all procurement activities are carried out in full compliance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations and approved project procedures. The Services will cover the planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of procurement activities, including the preparation and updating of procurement strategies and plans, bidding documents, requests for proposals, procurement notices, and contract documentation. The Services will manage procurement processes through the World Bank’s Systematic Tracking of Exchanges in Procurement (STEP), facilitate interactions with the World Bank and support evaluation and contract negotiations in accordance with applicable requirements. The Services also include the provision of technical guidance on procurement matters, maintain supplier and consultant performance and procurement records, and establish effective procurement filing and monitoring systems to support efficient and transparent project implementation. The duration of the Services is 13 months from the date of contract effectiveness, with the possibility of extension through Project implementation, subject to satisfactory performance and availability of funds.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The Department of Information Communications Technology (DICT) now invites eligible individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in one of the following: Law, Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Economics or related areas;
  • At least 5(five) years of successful experience in procurement, with a minimum of 2 (two) years in projects financed by the World Bank or similar multi-lateral institutions at a Procurement Specialist/Officer level;
  • Experience in managing at least 20 procurement activities simultaneously over a period of 2 years.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Seventh Edition, September, 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment:

The Bank requires that Consultants:

  1.  provide professional, objective and impartial advice;
  2.  at all times hold the Borrower’s interests paramount, without any consideration of future work; and
  3. in providing advice, avoid conflicts with other assignments and their own interests.

Consultants shall not be hired for any assignment that would be in conflict with their prior or current obligations to other clients, or that may place them in a position of being unable to carry out the assignment in the best interests of the Borrower. Without limitation on the generality of the foregoing, Consultants shall not be hired under the circumstances set forth below:

  • for any assignment that, by its nature, creates a conflict of interest with another assignment of the Consultant;
  • Consultants that have a close business or family relationship with a professional staff of the Borrower, or of the project implementing agency, or of a recipient of a part of the Bank’s financing, or any other party representing or acting on behalf of the Borrower, that is directly or indirectly involved in any part of:
  1. the preparation of the TOR for the assignment;
  2. the selection process for the contract; or
  3. the supervision of the contract; may not be awarded a contract, unless the conflict stemming from this relationship has been resolved in a manner acceptable to the Bank throughout the selection process and the execution of the contract.

TÉRMINOS DE REFERENCIA

FIRMA CONSULTORA PARA APOYAR LA PREPARACIÓN DE SUBPROYECTOS DE ELECTRIFICACIÓN MEDIANTE EXTENSIÓN DE REDES

1. ANTECEDENTES, OBJETO Y ALCANCE

El Gobierno del Estado Plurinacional de Bolivia, a través del Ministerio de Hidrocarburos y Energías (MHE), por intermedio del Viceministerio de Electricidad y Energías Renovables (VMEER), y ejecutado por la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto del Programa Electricidad para Vivir con Dignidad (UEP PEVD) en coordinación con la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto de la Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (UEP ENDE), impulsa la implementación del proyecto "Mejora del Acceso Sostenible a la Electricidad en Bolivia - Infraestructura Descentralizada para la Transformación Rural (IDTR III)", financiado con el apoyo del Banco Mundial (US$ 125 millones). Este programa constituye uno de los pilares estratégicos más relevantes para la expansión de la frontera eléctrica en el territorio nacional, orientando sus esfuerzos hacia comunidades rurales de alta dispersión geográfica y vulnerabilidad socioeconómica en departamentos como Potosí, Tarija, Santa Cruz, Beni y Pando.

Las áreas de intervención del IDTR III abordan geografías complejas (Amazonía, Chaco, Valles y Altiplano). Diseñar redes eléctricas en estos entornos requiere análisis especializados de servidumbres de paso, coordinación con distribuidoras locales (p. ej., empresas filiales de ENDE) y la optimización topológica de las redes para minimizar caídas de tensión y pérdidas de energía en largas distancias.

La ejecución exitosa de las redes de distribución en media y baja tensión, así como de las infraestructuras asociadas, requiere de una fase crítica de preinversión e ingeniería de detalle. En este contexto, la realización de estudios técnicos, ambientales, sociales y de diseño final para líneas de transmisión y redes eléctricas de electrificación rural resulta indispensable. Para garantizar que los subproyectos cumplan con los estándares internacionales de ingeniería, rentabilidad, sostenibilidad y marcos salvaguardistas socioambientales exigidos por el organismo financiador, la UEP PEVD, en coordinación con la UEP ENDE, requiere la contratación de una Empresa Consultora Especializada. Dicha entidad asumirá la responsabilidad de estructurar los estudios de ingeniería, levantamientos topográficos, diseños de trazo, dimensionamiento electromecánico y la evaluación de impacto ambiental y social necesarios para la posterior licitación y construcción de las obras, en el formato establecido en el Manual de Elaboración y Evaluación de Proyectos de Electrificación Rural (MEEPER 2025), aprobado mediante Resolución Ministerial N° 085-2025.

Los EDTP deberán identificar y evaluar los riesgos e impactos sociales de cada subproyecto, conforme al Marco de Gestión Ambiental y Social (MGAS) y a los Estándares Ambientales y Sociales (EAS) del Banco Mundial aplicables, particularmente EAS1, EAS2, EAS4, EAS5, EAS7 y EAS10, según corresponda, incluyendo los riesgos asociados a Pueblos Indígenas, vulnerabilidad y exclusión, tierras y servidumbres, participación y conflictividad social.

2. DENOMINACIÓN DE LAS PARTES

Para efectos de los presentes Términos de Referencia, se utilizarán de manera uniforme las siguientes denominaciones:

  • Entidad Contratante: la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto IDTR III del Programa Electricidad para Vivir con Dignidad (UEP PEVD), responsible de la etapa de preinversión de los subproyectos, dependiente del Viceministerio de Electricidad y Energías Renovables (VMEER) del Ministerio de Hidrocarburos y Energías (MHE), revisara la identificación y priorización de los subproyectos.
  • UEP ENDE: la Unidad Ejecutora del Proyecto IDTR III de la Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (ENDE), titular de los subproyectos, responsable de tramitar y obtener la Licencia Ambiental y las demás licencias, autorizaciones y permisos que requieran los subproyectos, así como de llevar adelante la licitación e implementación de las obras. Revisara todos los productos de la consultoría y aprueba el diseño final. También será el responsable de obtener la certificación de la aplicación en el diseño técnico, de los estándares constructivos de las empresas distribuidoras.
  • Supervisión: el equipo técnico designado por la UEP PEVD en coordinación con la UEP ENDE para el seguimiento, revisión y aprobación de los productos de la consultoría. Los especialistas sociales de la UEP PEVD y de la UEP ENDE revisarán y darán conformidad a los instrumentos y productos sociales antes de considerar completo el EDTP de cada subproyecto y de proceder con la licitación.
  • Consultora: la empresa consultora adjudicada y contratada, responsible únicamente del diseño técnico (E.D.T.P.) final y de la elaboración de toda la documentación de respaldo, incluida la documentación ambiental y social y los Pliegos / Documentos de Licitación de obras en formato del Banco Mundial y de ENDE. La Consultora no es responsable de tramitar ni de obtener licencias, autorizaciones o permisos.
  • Proponente: la empresa consultora que presenta su propuesta durante el proceso de contratación.
  • Empresa Distribuidora: la empresa que opera el servicio de distribución de electricidad en el área del proyecto.

3. OBJETIVO

3.1 Objetivo de la Consultoría

Elaborar los Estudios de Diseño Técnico de Pre inversión (E.D.T.P.) y toda la documentación de respaldo, en los que se establezcan claramente los aspectos técnicos, económicos, sociales y ambientales del proyecto, de manera que permitan tomar una decisión objetiva respecto al uso adecuado de los recursos de inversión, así como los Pliegos / Documentos de Licitación de obras en formato del Banco Mundial y de ENDE para la ejecución de las obras. Cada EDTP deberá demostrar la viabilidad social del subproyecto y asegurar que el diseño incorpore medidas para evitar, minimizar o mitigar impactos sociales y promover el acceso inclusivo a los beneficios, conforme al MGAS y al Plan de Compromiso Ambiental y Social (PCAS).

Los estudios se enmarcarán en el Reglamento Básico de Pre inversión, en el cumplimiento del Art. 6°, establecido en los procesos, procedimientos e instrumentos técnicos del Sistema Inversión Pública y Financiamiento Externo (S.I.P.F.E.).

3.2 Objetivos Específicos

  • Desarrollar el diseño técnico de subproyectos de electrificación rural, el mismo deberá ser desarrollado en formato MEEPER y utilizando los estándares constructivos respectivamente de las distribuidoras.
  • Desarrollar los documentos Sociales y ambientales aplicables por subproyecto, de acuerdo a lo establecido en el Marco de Gestión Ambiental y Social (MGAS) para el proyecto IDTR III, incluyendo, conforme al screening social establecido en el MGAS, la preparación de los instrumentos y medidas sociales requeridos, como, cuando corresponda, diagnóstico o evaluación social, participación, atención a grupos vulnerables, Pueblos Indígenas, tierras y servidumbres, mecanismo de quejas, salud y seguridad comunitaria y otras medidas pertinentes.
  • Desarrollar los pliegos de licitación completa, en formatos de los pliegos del Banco Mundial y de ENDE.
  • En algunos casos se podrá tomar en cuenta el diseño de un sistema de suministro de energía eléctrica capaz de sustentar procesos productivos de desarrollo local y micro regional, cumpliendo los parámetros de calidad exigidos en la Metodología para la Medición y Control de Calidad de
  • Distribución (MMCCD) de la AUTORIDAD DE FISCALIZACIÓN DE ELECTRICIDAD Y TECNOLOGÍA NUCLEAR (AETN)
  • Dimensionar los proyectos adecuadamente para satisfacer la demanda de energía eléctrica de los pobladores del área del proyecto.

4. ALCANCE

La Consultora asumirá la responsabilidad por los resultados y la calidad de los productos entregados. Los alcances del trabajo de consultoría son los siguientes:

Delimitación de responsabilidades: el alcance de la Consultora comprende exclusivamente el diseño técnico de los subproyectos y la elaboración de toda la documentación de respaldo (documentación ambiental, social y de servidumbres, y Pliegos de Licitación en formato del Banco Mundial y de ENDE). El trámite y la obtención de la Licencia Ambiental y de las demás licencias, autorizaciones y permisos corresponden a la UEP ENDE, que los gestionará en base a la documentación elaborada y presentada por la Consultora.

  • Coordinación con la UEP PEVD, dependiente del VMEER del Ministerio de Hidrocarburos y Energías (MHE), para la identificación y priorización de los subproyectos y con la UEP ENDE para el diseño técnico final del subproyecto y toda la documentación de respaldo anteriormente mencionada..
  • Verificar toda documentación del proyecto para la ejecución del mismo, y calidad de los trabajos a realizar.
  • Realizar la verificación en campo de las familias beneficiarias en coordinación UEP PEVD, los consultores departamentales de UEP PEVD, la Supervisión y las organizaciones sociales . Para identificar y validar a los beneficiarios se aplicarán criterios transparentes, y la coordinación con organizaciones sociales no será el único mecanismo de validación; se incorporarán mecanismos para reconocer hogares o personas vulnerables con riesgo de exclusión del acceso al servicio.
  • Elaborar las especificaciones técnicas para la ejecución de los proyectos.
  • Recabar la información establecida en el Prólogo del MEEPER 2025 (AETN, Empresa Distribuidora, INE, municipios y gobiernos autónomos, e INRA) y elaborar la documentación de respaldo requerida para que la UEP ENDE gestione la revisión del Estudio y la emisión del Certificado de Conformidad por la Empresa Distribuidora, la autorización del Plan de Desmonte ante la ABT y, cuando corresponda, las autorizaciones del SERNAP y de la ABC así como el Certificado de Uso de Suelo.
  • Realizar informes periódicos del avance del trabajo de Consultoría, y reuniones semanales de avance de la consultoría conjuntamente con UEP PEVD y UEP ENDE.
  • Cumplir lo establecido en la Ley de Medio Ambiente Nº 1333 y sus Reglamentos, elaborando toda la documentación ambiental requerida y establecida en el MGAS para el Proyecto, en base a la cual la UEP ENDE, como titular de los subproyectos, tramitará y obtendrá la Licencia Ambiental ante la Autoridad Ambiental Competente. La Consultora no es responsible del trámite ni de la obtención de la licencia.
  • Elaborar los planes conforme a los Estándares Ambientales y Sociales (EAS) del Banco Mundial en el marco de lo descrito en el MGAS (como el Diagnóstico Socioambiental, la estructura del PGAS Contratista (PGAS-C), para su posterior desarrollo por el contratista de obra, y los requisitos y medidas ambientales y sociales específicos del subproyecto para los pliegos, con el presupuesto socioambiental detallado, planes ambientales y sociales entre otros)). La Consultora elaborará la estructura del PGAS-C (contenido mínimo, componentes y matriz de medidas ambientales y sociales) a partir de los riesgos e impactos identificados en cada subproyecto. El PGAS-C es un instrumento operativo del contratista de obra: este lo desarrollará posteriormente sobre la base de dicha estructura, y estará sujeto a revisión y aprobación antes del inicio de obras, de acuerdo con el MGAS.
  • Realizar un screening social por subproyecto, previo a la definición de los instrumentos, seguido de una evaluación proporcional de los riesgos e impactos sociales y de la preparación de los instrumentos previstos en el MGAS. Las medidas resultantes deberán incorporarse al diseño, al presupuesto y a los documentos de licitación.
  • Asimismo, cumplir  lo establecido en el Documento Base de Contratación (DBC) del proceso, los presentes Términos de Referencia, el Contrato, el Manual de Operaciones del Proyecto IDTR III, el Plan de Compromiso Ambiental y Social (PCAS), MGAS y las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones y Estándares Ambientales y Sociales del Banco Mundial aplicables.
  • Llevar informes adecuados de las áreas intervenidas para el proyecto (georreferenciado, planos, mapas y otros).
  • Realizar los planos topográficos y estacado de los subproyectos.
  • Se planificará y coordinará con el VMEER y UEP PEVD el tamaño de los subproyectos de acceso a electricidad, dando prioridad a subproyectos que tengan mayor cantidad de beneficiarios y mayor monto.
  • El PEVD y ENDE definiran y acordar[an con la firma en la negociación el número de subproyectos, comunidades, familias o usuarios, ni los kilómetros de red estimados, y cuánto corresponde a cada departamento.
  • Se propondrá los precios unitarios de mercado de los materiales de construcción y se coordinará con VMEER y la UEP PEVD los precios unitarios a utilizar en los diseños, que determinarán el costo total para la licitación e implementación del subproyecto.

5. JUSTIFICACIÓN

El Proyecto "Mejora del Acceso Sostenible a la Electricidad en Bolivia (IDTR III)", financiado por el Banco Mundial mediante el Préstamo BIRF N° 96110 por US$ 125 millones, tiene como objetivo ampliar y mejorar el acceso a servicios de electricidad sostenibles en las zonas rurales de Bolivia. Sus metas al cierre, previsto para el 31 de marzo de 2030, incluyen 34.500 nuevas conexiones eléctricas y 107.000 personas con servicio eléctrico nuevo o mejorado. El Proyecto es ejecutado por el Ministerio de Hidrocarburos y Energías (MHE), a través de la UEP PEVD, dependiente del VMEER, y por la UEP ENDE.

Para avanzar con la implementación del IDTR III, en particular de las inversiones de extensión de redes del Componente 1, es imprescindible contar previamente con una cartera de subproyectos debidamente identificados y con estudios de preinversión aprobados. Sin esta cartera no es posible iniciar los procesos de licitación ni la construcción de las obras, lo que pondría en riesgo el cumplimiento de las metas físicas y del cronograma de desembolsos dentro del plazo de cierre del Proyecto.

En este marco, la UEP PEVD, en coordinación con la UEP ENDE, aún y prioriza la identificación y la elaboración de los estudios de preinversión de los subproyectos de electrificación rural en los departamentos priorizados de Pando, Beni, Santa Cruz, Tarija y Potosí, que comprenden:

a) Identificación de los subproyectos: verificación de comunidades y familias beneficiarias, de la demanda y de la factibilidad de conexión a las redes existentes de las empresas distribuidoras.

b) Diseño técnico: Estudio de Diseño Técnico de Preinversión (EDTP) de cada subproyecto, elaborado conforme al formato y contenido mínimo del MEEPER 2025, incluyendo el cumplimiento del indicador de costo eficiencia (Costo de Inversión/Familia).

 c) Aspectos sociales y ambientales: elaboración de toda la documentación ambiental conforme a la Ley N° 1333 y sus reglamentos, en base a la cual la UEP ENDE tramitará y obtendrá la Licencia Ambiental, así como de los instrumentos exigidos por los Estándares Ambientales y Sociales (EAS) del Banco Mundial en el marco de lo descrito en el MGAS ( como el Diagnóstico Socioambiental, la estructura del PGAS Contratista (PGAS-C), para su posterior desarrollo por el contratista de obra, y los requisitos y medidas ambientales y sociales específicas del subproyecto para los pliegos, con el presupuesto socioambiental detallado, planes ambientales y sociales entre otros) y de las actas de conformidad de servidumbre y de participación de las comunidades.

d) Pliego de licitación: elaboración de los Pliegos / Documentos de Licitación para la ejecución de las obras en formato del Banco Mundial (Documentos Estándar de Adquisiciones – Solicitud de Ofertas para Obras) y de ENDE, con especificaciones técnicas, planos, cómputos métricos, precios unitarios, presupuesto referencial (incluyendo presupuesto socioambiental) y requisitos ambientales y sociales, de modo que la UEP ENDE pueda licitar los subproyectos inmediatamente después de su aprobación.

El MEEPER 2025, aprobado por el Ministerio de Hidrocarburos y Energías mediante Resolución Ministerial N° 085-2025 de 20 de junio de 2025, que abroga la Resolución Ministerial N° 030-2023, constituye el instrumento técnico de referencia para la elaboración y evaluación de proyectos de electrificación rural. Esta versión fue actualizada en coordinación con las principales empresas distribuidoras del país e incorpora nuevos índices de costo eficiencia, con un factor de ajuste global de 1,53 sobre los valores referenciales de inversión por usuario según piso ecológico. Los subproyectos que se presenten en el marco del IDTR III deben cumplir el contenido mínimo, la documentación y el indicador de costo eficiencia establecidos en el Anexo I del MEEPER 2025 para su evaluación y aprobación.

Por lo expuesto, la presente consultoría resulta indispensable para conformar una cartera de subproyectos técnica, social y ambientalmente viables, listos para su licitación y ejecución, que permita avanzar con la implementación del IDTR III, evitar retrasos, sobrecostos y reformulaciones durante la etapa de construcción, y asegurar el cumplimiento de los compromisos asumidos con el Banco Mundial.

Para efectos de los presentes Términos de Referencia, un subproyecto es socialmente viable cuando, antes de la licitación, se han evaluado los riesgos sociales pertinentes, realizado la participación requerida, identificado y gestionado las tierras y servidumbres, y definido todas las medidas sociales necesarias.

16. ESTIMACIÓN DE LA DURACIÓN DEL SERVICIO

El plazo para la elaboración del Estudio de Diseño técnico de Pre Inversión es de 150 días calendario, desde la emisión de la Orden de Proceder.

Por tanto, el estudio tiene un plazo máximo de Ciento Cincuenta (150) días calendario, sin reducción por días feriados, lluvias u otros agentes naturales. Este plazo, o el que se acepte a tiempo de firmar el Contrato correrá a partir de la fecha de la orden de proceder emitida por la Supervisión, independientemente del pago del anticipo.

18. SUPERVISIÓN DE LA EJECUCIÓN DEL ESTUDIO

La UEP PEVD, en coordinación con la UEP ENDE, designará a los técnicos que conformarán la Supervisión para la realización del Estudio de Diseño Técnico de Pre inversión "ELABORACIÓN EDTP PROYECTOS ELECTRIFICACIÓN RURAL FORMATO MEEPER" para el efecto los proyectos tendrán un proceso de revisión Semanal hasta que se cuente con la revisión final del diseño final de cada subproyecto.

Los diseños en borrador a ser presentados para revisión de la Supervisión deben ser presentados en un ejemplar físico y digital.

Los Estudios Finales aprobados por la Supervisión, debe presentarse de forma obligatoria en Triple ejemplar (un original y dos copias), incluyendo tres copias en CD bajo formato AutoCAD o DXF para sistema Windows, Word y Excel.

19. COORDINACIÓN DE TRABAJO

Para cumplir el cronograma de ejecución del proyecto de pre inversión y realizar una mejor coordinación y trabajo eficiente, la Consultora debe cumplir los siguientes aspectos:

  • La Consultora, de forma obligatoria, debe contar con una oficina y un teléfono fijo en Bolivia, a efectos de coordinación directa con los beneficiarios, la Entidad Contratante y la UEP ENDE, lo cual será verificado por la Supervisión.
  • Coordinación permanente y obligatoria con la Supervisión, a cargo del Gerente del Proyecto.
  • La Consultora está obligada a presentar el Equipo de Profesionales propuesto en la adjudicación del estudio, que tendrá a su cargo la elaboración del proyecto; dicha presentación se realizará cuando se emita la Orden de Proceder.
  • Coordinación con el personal clave propuesto, de acuerdo al requerimiento de la Supervisión.
  • El proponente no debe estar comprendido en el artículo 43 del D.S. 0181 (NB-SABS).
  • La Consultora tiene la obligación de Contactarse y apersonarse permanentemente con la UEP PEVD.

20. EXPERIENCIA GENERAL DEL PROPONENTE

El proponente deberá acreditar una experiencia general mínima de diez (10) años en elaboración de consultorías o implementación de proyectos.

. Como respaldo, deberá presentar las actas de recepción definitiva correspondientes u otro documento que acredite la experiencia

21. EXPERIENCIA ESPECÍFICA DEL PROPONENTE

La experiencia específica mínima requerida del proponente es haber efectuado cuatro (4) consultorías de ingeniería de preinversión, diseño, supervisión o construcción y tendido de redes eléctricas de media y baja tensión.

  • La Consultora asumirá la responsabilidad técnica total de los servicios profesionales prestados bajo contrato. La revisión, aceptación y aprobación de los informes parciales y del informe final por la Supervisión durante la elaboración del estudio no exime a la Consultora de la responsabilidad final y total del mismo.

 

24. ANEXOS

25. PROPIEDAD INTELECTUAL

Los originales de los documentos, libretas de campo, memorias de cálculo, planos, diseños y otros documentos que elabore la Consultora pasarán a ser propiedad de la UEP PEVD y de la UEP ENDE; en consecuencia, deberán ser entregados en su totalidad, quedando absolutamente prohibida la difusión de dicha documentación, total o parcialmente, sin consentimiento previo y por escrito de la Entidad Contratante.

Este derecho continuará vigente aún concluida la relación contractual entre partes.

26. INFORMES DE ACTIVIDADES

La Consultora presentará cada uno de los productos establecidos con un Informe y toda la documentación adjunta al mencionado producto; las observaciones que realice la Supervisión deberán ser subsanadas por la Consultora en el plazo máximo de tres (3) días calendario para proceder a su aprobación; caso contrario, se aplicarán las multas correspondientes hasta la entrega del producto definitivo.

Así mismo, la Consultora deberá presentar el Informe Final, en el plazo máximo de siete (7) días calendario posterior a la emisión del Informe de Conformidad del Último Producto.

27. DOCUMENTOS QUE DEBE PRESENTAR EL PROPONENTE

Para su postulación, los proponentes deberán presentar los respaldos necesarios de todos los formularios correspondientes al proceso siendo una causal de descalificación la no presentación de los mismos.

27.1 De la propuesta electrónica

De las propuestas digitales, el proponente deberá verificar su correcto enlace de su propuesta al proceso a participar, en caso de encontrar fallas en el archivo al momento de la apertura de sus propuestas la Entidad Contratante no se responsabilizará ni asumirá los errores, debido a que el sistema del SICOES es del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas Públicas.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Country: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

Project: Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project Phase Two (LLRP-II)

Assignment Title: Consultancy service for Detail Design for Adigafelema irrigation scheme from groundwater sources [40 Ha]

Credit No.: IDA- 7519-ET

Procurement Reference No.: ET-DR-RPCU-571065-CS-QCBS

  1. The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank (IDA) and IFAD toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project Phase Two (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the detailed design of the Adigafelema irrigation scheme from groundwater sources [40 Ha] in Aseliso Woreda.
  2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the following:

The objective of the assignment is to prepare a bankable, climate-resilient, environmentally sustainable, socially inclusive, and implementation-ready irrigation scheme in accordance with national standards, the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and IFAD SECAP. Specifically, the Consultant shall:

  • Verify existing groundwater investigations (hydrogeology, boreholes, pumping tests, water quality) and assess long-term sustainability of abstraction; no new production well design is envisaged unless instructed;
  • Undertake baseline, socioeconomic, gender and social inclusion, soil and land suitability, agronomic and agricultural economics studies, and a climate-risk assessment;
  • Carry out topographic and geotechnical surveys and the feasibility study, including technical, economic and financial analysis of alternatives;
  • Prepare the ESIA and applicable ESF instruments (ESMP, SEP, LMP, IPMP, GBV/SEA/SH risk assessment);
  • Prepare detailed designs of the solar-pumped, pipe-supported surface irrigation system and drainage, drawings, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities, cost estimates, tender documents and construction readiness package; and
  • Develop the operation and maintenance framework and Water Users Association arrangements, and build the capacity of stakeholders.

The Consultant shall carry out all investigations, surveys, analyses, assessments, stakeholder consultations, designs, cost estimates and tender document preparation to achieve the objectives above, in accordance with generally accepted professional standards, whether or not a specific activity is cited in the Terms of Reference. The estimated level of effort is 25.25 key-expert staff-months. The assignment duration is three (3) calendar months (twelve weeks) from the contract commencement date, and the assignment is expected to start on February 25th, 2027.

The Dire Dawa Administration Agriculture, Water, Mines and Energy Bureau, LLRP-II Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and services.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained from the address given below.

3. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in irrigation and water resources engineering consultancy services; provide the company profile, registration certificate, and number of years in business;
  • Relevant experience: proven experience during the last ten (10) years in feasibility studies, detailed design and ESIA of irrigation and drainage schemes (preferably groundwater-based and/or solar-powered schemes) and preparation of tender documents; experience on World Bank- or IFAD-financed projects is an advantage. For each assignment, indicate the client, location, irrigated area, contract value, duration and the firm’s role, supported by contract or completion certificates;
  • Technical and managerial capability of the firm: managerial and organizational structure, survey and field equipment, design software (e.g. for hydraulic and pipe network design), quality assurance systems and capacity to mobilize field teams. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.
  • 4.The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: the selected Consultant will prepare the detailed design, technical specifications, bills of quantities, cost estimates, and tender documents for the construction of the irrigation scheme. Accordingly, the Consultant and any of its affiliates, joint venture partners and sub-consultants shall be disqualified from providing goods, works or non-consulting services resulting from or directly related to this assignment, including the construction works and the supply and installation of the solar pumping system. COUNTRY:                                       Federal Republic of Somalia

Assignment Title:                          Consulting Firm to Undertake the Independent Valuation of Assets for the Somali National Fiber Infrastructure Company (SONFIC) Special Purpose Vehicle

Reference No.:                                SO-MOCT-FGS-580867-CS-CQS

Place of assignment:                   Mogadishu, Somalia

Submission Date:                         November 25, 2026, 2.00pm (local time, Mogadishu, Somalia)

The Federal Republic of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP), and the Ministry of Communications and Technology intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) are required to be undertaken by an external consulting firm supporting the client, the Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT), FGS, through the EA-RDIP Project Implementation Unit (PIU), to carry out the “Consulting Firm to Undertake the Independent Valuation of Assets for the Somali National Fiber Infrastructure Company (SONFIC) Special Purpose Vehicle”. Under Component 1 of EA-RDIP, the Government is establishing a national wholesale, open-access fiber backbone through the Somali National Fiber Infrastructure Company (SONFIC), a Special Purpose Vehicle formed in September 2026 by the Government and five licensed telecommunications operators (the “Founding Operators”). Existing operator Inter-City fiber and related assets are to be contributed to SONFIC in return for shares, on the basis of an independent valuation. The Firm will act as Independent Valuer and will: (i) establish a verified inventory of the assets proposed for contribution by each Founding Operator, including technical audit, ownership, title and encumbrance checks; (ii) determine which assets are eligible; (iii) determine the fair value of each contribution under the International Valuation Standards (IVS) and IFRS 13, using cost, market and income approaches; (iv) convert accepted values into Class A share allocations and value the options for any excess contribution; and (v) hand over the asset register, valuation model and working papers to MoCT/PIU and train staff. The results must be auditable and suitable to support the SONFIC Board and shareholder resolutions authorizing each allotment. The consultant firm will undertake all the specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference (ToR). The assignment is expected to be completed within approximately three (3) months (thirteen (13) weeks) from contract effectiveness.

Terms of Reference (ToR) can be found at the following website: https://moct.gov.so/en/jobs/  or it can be provided upon submission of application in person or by e-mail. The e-mail address is provided below.

The Ministry of Communications and Technology now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.).  The short-listing criteria are as follows:

The short-listing criteria are as follows:

  1. Core business of the firm and at least eight (8) years of relevant organizational experience in asset valuation, financial advisory or transaction advisory services, with evidence of the company registration certificate, business license or operational permit, and a company profile indicating services offered and years in operation.
  2. The firm should demonstrate successful completion of at least three (3) comparable valuation assignments for telecommunications, fiber optic or other network/linear infrastructure, including at least one (1) involving contributions in kind, Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) or joint venture formation, or the determination of shareholding among multiple contributors. Demonstrated application of the International Valuation Standards (IVS) and IFRS fair-value principles, and experience in physical verification of assets, including in difficult-access environments, is required. For each assignment, firms should indicate the client, contract value, duration, scope of services and the firm’s role.
  3. Demonstrate experience of relevant services implemented in Somalia, or in Africa, fragile/conflict-affected or comparable environments similar to that of Somalia; experience with public-sector clients and World Bank-financed assignments will be an advantage; and
  4. The technical and managerial organization of the firm, including documented quality-assurance systems and the capacity to manage and protect commercially sensitive data. (Provide only the structure of the firm’s organization.) Do not provide CVs of staff. Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated July 2016 and revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023, (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In particular, the Consultant shall be independent of SONFIC, the Founding Operators and their shareholders, and shall disclose any past or present relationship with them in its Expression of Interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint venture and/ or a Sub consultancy.
