data.notice_text:
TERMS OF REFERENCE

National Individual Consultant

Site Engineer (One Position)

 

Title

Site Engineer

Contractual Arrangement

Local Recruitment

Expected Start Date

December 9th 2026

Contract Duration

Eight (8) months (December 2026 – August 2027), with possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance, project needs, and availability of funding.

Level of Input

Full-time

Project

Nurturing Early Skills through Technology (NEST) Project

Financing Partner

The World Bank

Hiring Organization

Shanti Volunteer Association (SVA)

Duty Station

Battambang Province (covering project sites in Kos Kralar, Ek Phnom and Thmar Kaul Districts)

Contract Type

Time Based

 

1.  Background

The Nurturing Early Skills through Technology (NEST) Project is funded by the Japan Social Development Fund (JSDF) and administered by the World Bank. The Project is implemented by Shanti Volunteer Association (SVA) in close collaboration with the Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS) of Cambodia.

The Project aims to enhance access to and quality of Early Childhood Education (ECE) through the promotion of learning through play and the integration of digital technology in target districts in Cambodia. The Project supports teacher professional development, establishment of an ECE digital resource platform, parental and community engagement, improvement of preschool learning environments through construction and renovation, and implementation of pilot school meal programs.

The Project is implemented in selected districts in Battambang, Banteay Meanchey, and Pailin provinces, targeting public preschools with the objective of strengthening equitable access to quality ECE services for young children aged 3–5 years.

Under Component 2 of the Project, SVA will implement phase 1 of civil works activities, comprising: (i) construction of 8 new preschool buildings, toilets, water tanks and 6 kitchen facilities; (ii) renovation of 17 existing preschool buildings; and (iii) outdoor environment improvements at  25 targeted preschools. These works are spread across three districts in Battambang province and one district in Banteay Meanchey Province, and procured through Request for Bids (RFB) and Request for Quotations (RFQ) methods.

To strengthen day-to-day site supervision during the main construction period, SVA seeks to recruit a Site Engineer based in Battambang Province. The Site Engineer will provide full-time, on-site supervision of the prime contractor(s) at project sites in Battambang Province, under the technical guidance of the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer.

 

2.  Objectives

The objective of this assignment is to ensure that the prime contractor’s civil works at project sites are executed in accordance with the approved drawings, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities (BoQ), and contract requirements, through on-site supervision by the Site Engineer.

Specifically, the Site Engineer will:

  • Provide full-time, day-to-day on-site supervision of the prime contractor’s works at project sites in the assigned province.
  • Ensure quality of materials and workmanship are complied with specification, approved drawing, method statement and schedules.
  • Ensure that the prime contractor executed all work in compliance with approved Environmental and Social(E&S) document
  • Maintain accurate and complete site records, including site diaries, inspection checklists, measurement records, and photo documentation.
  • Provide verified site-level information (progress, quantities, defects) to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer to support progress monitoring, payment certification, and completion.

 

3.  Scope of Work

Under the technical guidance of the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer, the Consultant shall undertake the following tasks at project sites:

a.  Site Mobilization and Pre-Construction

  • Become familiar with the approved drawings, technical specifications, BoQs, contract documents, and contractors’ work programs for each assigned site, and report any discrepancies to the Civil Engineer and SVA Engineer.
  • Participate in site handover to contractors and in pre-mobilization meetings with contractors, school representatives, and the SVA project team.
  • Sites readiness: coordinate with contractor’s supervisor and relevant stakeholders at target schools during contractor mobilization.
  • Prepare and submit updated sites plan including photos
  • Confirm that contractors have mobilized the required personnel, equipment, materials, site signage, and safety arrangements before works begin.

b.  Day-to-Day Site Supervision and Quality Control

  • Conduct full-time, day-to-day supervision of civil works at assigned sites, prioritizing site visits according to construction schedules and critical activities.
  • Inspect and verify key construction stages before contractors proceed (e.g., reinforcement and formwork inspection prior to concreting), using standard inspection checklists.
  • Verify that materials delivered to site comply with approved samples and technical specifications, and reject and record non-compliant materials.
  • Witness and record field and material tests (e.g., concrete slump tests, sampling of concrete test cubes, compaction checks), and follow up on test results.
  • Issue site instructions to contractors on quality and workmanship issues within delegated authority, and refer matters beyond this authority, including design changes and variations, to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.

 

c.  Site Records, Progress Monitoring and Reporting

  • Maintain a site diary for each site, recording daily activities, workforce and equipment, weather conditions, materials delivered, inspections, instructions issued, visitors, and issues.
  • Maintain photo documentation (before, during, and after works) and inspection records for each site.
  • Monitor actual progress against contractors’ approved work programs, and report delays together with proposed corrective measures.
  • Prepare weekly site progress reports and monthly reports, and submit them to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.
  • Participate in regular site meetings and record minutes and agreed actions, as required.

d.  Measurement and Payment Support

  • Verify at sites the actual completed works in Activity Schedule submitted by contractors
  • Prepare measurement sheets and supporting documentation for contractors’ payment applications, for review by the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.
  • Record and report site conditions or instructions that may give rise to variations or claims, with supporting evidence, for review by the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer.

e.  Environmental, Social, and Safety Compliance

  • Monitor contractors’ daily implementation of occupational health and safety (OHS) measures, including use of personal protective equipment (PPE), site fencing and barricading, safety signage, safe working at height, and first aid, with particular attention to the safety of children, teachers, and community members at operating preschools.
  • Monitor implementation of E&S mitigation measures at construction sites, including dust and noise control, waste management, drainage, and agreed working hours, in coordination with the E&S Specialist.
  • Monitor contractor compliance with labor management requirements, including workers’ code of conduct and prevention of child labor.
  • Report E&S incidents, accidents, and non-compliance to the E&S Specialist and SVA Project Manager immediately, and in any case within 24 hours, and follow up on corrective actions.
  • Liaise with school directors, School Management Committees (SMCs), and local authorities on site-level matters, and refer community concerns and grievances to the Project Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM).

f.  Completion and Handover

  • Participate in pre-completion and final inspections, and prepare defect (snagging) lists for each site.
  • Monitor rectification of defects by contractors and confirm completion of rectification works.
  • Compile site-level completion documentation, including as-built mark-ups, photo records, test records, and site diaries.
  • Support the handover of completed facilities to schools, School Management Committees (SMCs), and relevant government counterparts.

 

 

4.  Expected Outputs and Deliverables

The following deliverables are expected over the course of the assignment. Timelines are indicative and subject to adjustment based on project implementation progress and construction schedules.

#

Deliverable

Timeline

1

Inception Work Plan and site supervision schedule for assigned sites

Within two (2) weeks of contract signing

2

Site diaries and inspection checklists for each site

Daily (submitted with weekly reports)

3

Weekly site progress report (progress, quality issues, instructions issued, E&S/OHS observations, and photos)

 

Weekly

4

Monthly report, including progress against work programs and E&S compliance

Monthly

5

Material inspection and test records, and measurement sheets supporting contractors’ payment applications

 

As required, in line with contractors’ payment schedules

6

E&S and OHS incident reports

Within 24 hours of occurrence

7

Defect lists and pre-completion inspection reports for each site

Prior to practical completion at each site

8

Site completion documentation package and Final Report

Upon practical completion of each site; Final Report at end of contract

5.  Work Supervision

The Consultant will work under the overall supervision of the SVA Project Manager and will receive day-to-day technical guidance from the Civil Engineer Consultant and the SVA Engineer.

The Consultant will coordinate and liaise with:

  • The Civil Engineer and the SVA Engineer to ensure a consistent supervision approach across provinces;
  • PMU members and field staff;
  • The E&S Specialist and other technical consultants engaged under the Project;
  • Contractors, site supervisors, and construction personnel at project sites;
  • School directors, School Management Committees (SMCs), community representatives, and sub-national authorities at project sites.

The Consultant shall submit site records and weekly reports to the Civil Engineer Consultant and SVA Engineer, and monthly reports to the SVA Project Manager through the SVA Engineer, for review and approval. The Consultant shall participate in regular coordination meetings, site meetings, and World Bank supervision missions, as required.

6.  Contract Term and Location of Assignment

The contract period is eight (8) months, from December 2026 to August 2027, with possibility of extension subject to satisfactory performance, project needs, and availability of funding.

The Consultant will be engaged as a full-time Individual Consultant (IC) under the NEST Project and is expected to be present at project sites on a daily basis throughout the assignment period.

Key arrangements are as follows:

 

  • Duty Station: Battambang Province (covering project sites in Kos Kralar, Ek Phnom and Thmar Kaul Districts)
  • Contract Modality: The contract will be time-based, with remuneration at a fixed monthly rate for the duration of the assignment.
  • Working Arrangements: Full-time, in accordance with SVA working hours. Work outside regular working hours may be required in line with construction activities, subject to SVA policy.
  • The Consultant is expected to work primarily at project sites and to make their own arrangements for workspace. No office space will be provided by SVA; however, the Consultant may use the SVA Battambang Office for meetings or as required. The Consultant is expected to provide their own computer, smartphone for photo documentation, and personal working equipment.
  • Payment Modality: Payment shall be made on a monthly basis upon submission and approval of monthly reports and agreed deliverables.
  • Travel costs directly related to project implementation and approved by SVA, including daily travel to project sites, will be covered in accordance with SVA travel policy.

7.  Consultant Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Engineering, Architecture, or other relevant technical field. A technical diploma with additional relevant site experience may be considered.

Experience

  • Minimum two (2) years of relevant professional experience in site supervision of building construction and/or renovation works.
  • Hands-on experience in site-level quality control, including stage inspections, material checks, and quantity measurement.
  • Experience in maintaining site diaries, inspection records, and progress reports.
  • Experience in construction of schools or other public or community buildings is an advantage.
  • Experience working on World Bank-financed or other internationally funded projects is an advantage.

Technical Competencies

  • Sound practical knowledge of building construction methods, materials, and quality control at site.
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, technical specifications, and Bills of Quantities.
  • Ability to carry out site measurements and quantity verification.
  • Familiarity with occupational health and safety (OHS) requirements and environmental and social compliance in construction settings.
  • Ability to keep accurate records and prepare clear and timely reports.
  • Proficiency in MS Office (Word and Excel); knowledge of AutoCAD is an advantage.
  • Fluency in Khmer is required; working knowledge of English, both written and spoken, is required.

Other Considerations

  • Willingness to reside in or near the assigned province and to travel daily to project sites, including remote rural areas.
  • A valid driving license is required.
  • The Consultant must not hold a government position during the contract period.
  • The Consultant must not have any conflict of interest with contractors engaged under the Project.

 

8.  Guidelines for Applying

Interested candidates should submit the following documents to the contact below, with the subject line:

“Application for IC – Site Engineer (Battambang) – NEST Project: [Your Full Name]”

Required submission documents:

  • Updated Curriculum Vitae (CV) clearly demonstrating qualifications and relevant experience.
  • Cover letter outlining suitability for the role, expected monthly rate, and availability.

 

Submit to:

 

Ms. Chea Sopheavy

Position: Procurement and Operation Officer, Shanti Volunteer Association (SVA)

Address: No. 8, Street 424, Sangkat Tomnob Teuk, Khan Boeng Keng Kang, Phnom Penh

Email: info@sva-cambodia.org

 

Copy to:

 

Ms. Ayano Kikuchi

Position: Project Manager, NEST Project, SVA

Email:  kikuchi@sva.or.jp

Applications will be accepted until November 25th, 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further assessment. The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Revised February 2025), under the Individual Consultant (IC) selection method.

Terms of Reference

Consulting Services for the Expertise of Projects under the Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Project (TRIP)

 

TRIP-CQS-EX-01

 

  1. Background

The Tourism and Regional Infrastructure Program (TRIP) aims to promote Armenia’s tourism potential through targeted infrastructure investments and soft interventions in several regions of the country. The Program will support seven out of the twenty identified tourism clusters: Areni, Yeghegis, Jermuk, Dvin, Gyumri, Dilijan, and Goris, focusing on wine, wellness, adventure, cultural, educational, and ecotourism across the regions of Ararat, Vayots Dzor, Shirak, Aragatsotn, Tavush, and Syunik.

The Program will contribute to improving access to tourism clusters and developing infrastructure at tourist destinations. It also aims to make more effective use of Armenia’s natural resources and human capital by enhancing the business and professional skills of residents in neighboring communities, with a view to maximizing the potential for job creation. In addition, the Program is aligned with the World Bank’s approach to attracting private investment in these tourism clusters.

The objective of the Program is to improve access to climate-resilient infrastructure and increase tourism’s contribution to the local economy in the clusters supported by the Program.

 

The consulting firm will be selected using the Consultant’s Qualifications Selection (CQS) method, in accordance with the World Bank’s Guidelines for the Selection and Employment of Consultants by World Bank Borrowers.

A one-time contract will be concluded with the Consultant, under which the Consultant will be tasked with reviewing the designs of three subprojects.

 

  1. Objectives

The Consultant shall review the design documentation for the following subprojects:

 

  1. “Improvement of the Dvin Archaeological Site and Adjacent Area and Development of Tourism Infrastructure”;
  2. “Partial Renovation of Dashtadem Fortress, Establishment of a Museum, and Improvement of the Area Adjacent to the Monument”;
  3. “Reconstruction of the Drinking Pavilion in the City of Jermuk, Republic of Armenia.”
  1. Scope of Services of the Consultant
  • Conduct an appraisal of the submitted designs, including verification of architectural, structural, engineering, and technological solutions and calculations, as well as construction work quantities and cost estimates, to ensure compliance with the requirements of applicable regulatory documents and standards.
  • Cooperate with the Client’s specialists during the appraisal of each assigned design project and provide the necessary information and clarifications regarding applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Carry out the appraisal activities in accordance with the schedule agreed upon with the Client.
  • In the event of new circumstances or requirements, review any revisions made to the design documentation and, where necessary, make corresponding amendments to the appraisal report.
  1. Consultant’s Reporting Obligations
  • As a report on the services performed, the Consultant shall submit an appraisal report for each design project reviewed.
  • The deadline for submitting the appraisal report for each project shall be agreed upon by the Client and the Consultant, taking into account the complexity and scope of the work, but shall not exceed 15 working days. The agreed deadline shall be specified in the terms of reference for the respective project and endorsed by both the Client and the Consultant.
  • The Organization shall submit to the Client an expert examination report prepared in accordance with the requirements established by the legislation of the Republic of Armenia, in Armenian, in two (2) hard copies and one (1) electronic scanned copy.

The Loan Agreement for Montenegro's project (Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization and its Alignment with SEPA Standards Project (TARGET Instant Payment Settlement Clone Project – TIPS Clone Project)). Project no. P509405 was signed on 30th of July 2025.  The Government of Montenegro aims to modernize payment systems through the improvement of the legal and regulatory framework and the modernization of financial infrastructure.  This Project will assist authorities in supporting the modernization of the payment’s infrastructure. The proposed Project builds directly on the existing engagement and supports authorities with necessary investment activities.   The overall Project have three components:

(i)        Providing technical assistance for setting up a new payment system and developing the broader payments ecosystem.

(ii)       Supporting the implementation and operation of the new payment system.

(iii)      Project Management.

The Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) is preparing for future participation in the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and, ultimately, in the Euro system, in line with Montenegro’s broader strategic objective of European Union (EU) accession. This process requires the continued alignment of CBCG’s institutional, operational, legal and technical frameworks with relevant EU standards and practices applicable to central banking and financial market infrastructures.

The Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) is the Project Implementing Entity and will have overall responsibility for project implementation and intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for the experienced and qualified Consultancy firm is to ensure the CBCG to development of a clear TARGET Services Accession Strategy and a comprehensive but proportionate implementation roadmap for Montenegro’s participation in relevant TARGET Services. The assessment shall be tailored to Montenegro’s monetary and institutional circumstances and to the practical needs of the CBCG and banking community. The Consultant shall focus on analysis and recommendations at a level sufficient to support strategic decisions and define subsequent implementation work. Detailed system specifications, extensive institution-by-institution audits, drafting of complete legislative instruments, vendor selection, live testing and migration execution are outside the scope unless separately agreed.

The ten areas correspond to the required substantive outputs described in ToR.  Findings may be consolidated into coordinated reports rather than duplicated across separate studies. MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT, HIGHWAYS AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS

Project: Regional Empowerment through Vibrant, Inclusive, and Viable Economies (REVIVE).

Project ID: P511605.

Credit No: 7985-LK.

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Detailed Design and Construction Supervision for Arugambay Tourism Cluster development.

PP ref no: LK-REVIVE-PMU-573674-CS-QCBS.

1. The Government of Sri Lanka has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Empowerment through Vibrant, Inclusive, and Viable Economies (REVIVE) Project. The Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development (MoTHUD), serving as the Executing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the review and validation of conceptual master plans and feasibility studies; site surveys and engineering investigations; preparation of implementable, climate-resilient detailed designs, Good for Construction drawings, design calculations, technical specifications, bills of quantities, cost estimates and World Bank-compliant bidding documents; intermittent technical support during works procurement; full-time construction supervision and contract administration; and support during the Defects Liability Period for investments at the Arugambay Tourism Cluster development including beachfront redevelopment, a lagoon ecological restoration, road improvement, tourism or public-realm development and refer to Annexure A of TOR.

3. The total duration of the assignment is expected to be approximately forty six (46) months: Phase A – Detailed Design, Bidding Documents and intermittent procurement support, ten (10) months, including four (4) months for detailed design and up to six (6) months for procurement support; Phase B – Construction Supervision and Contract Administration, twenty four (24) months; and Phase C – Defects Liability Period Support, twelve (12) months.

4. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.transport.gov.lk/ (Media > Procurement > TORs).

5. The Chairman of the Ministry Consultants Procurement Committee, on behalf of the REVIVE Project, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required firm-level qualifications, relevant experience and institutional capacity to perform the assignment.

 The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

(a) Legal Status, Core Business and Institutional Experience: The Consultant shall have been legally registered and in operation for at least fifteen (15) years and shall have a minimum of ten (10) years of institutional experience in detailed engineering design of multidisciplinary infrastructure, tourism or public-realm development construction supervision with contract administration. The Consultant shall submit supporting documents, including Certificate of Incorporation/ Registration, Company Profile and nature of business and evidence of relevant institutional experience.

(b) Comparable and Relevant Assignment Experience: The Consultant shall have successfully completed at least three (3) comparable consultancy assignments involving detailed engineering design and/or construction supervision with contract administration of similar nature, scope, scale, and complexity within the last ten (10) years. At least one assignment shall have included both detailed design and construction supervision with contract administration, and at least one shall have involved multidisciplinary infrastructure, tourism-related infrastructure, or public-realm development. The same assignment may satisfy both requirements. The Consultant shall provide relevant assignment details, including name, Client, location, commencement and completion dates, scope, contract value (USD equivalent), level of effort (person-months), and supporting evidence of successful completion, such as contracts, completion certificates, or client references.

(c) Management Capacity: The Consultant shall demonstrate adequate organizational, management, and technical capacity to undertake the assignment, including multidisciplinary engineering investigations, detailed design, procurement support, construction supervision, and contract administration. The Consultant shall provide relevant information on its organizational structure, technical resources, and management capacity to demonstrate its ability to perform the required services.

(d) Technical Capacity: The Consultant shall demonstrate the availability of adequate qualified and experienced professional resources and the capacity to mobilize multidisciplinary specialists required for the assignment. The Consultant shall provide information on its professional staff resources, including relevant specializations and experience. Individual Key Experts and their qualifications will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

(e) Additional Relevant Experience: Experience in World Bank or other multilateral development bank-financed assignments, coastal or environmentally sensitive settings, and in Sri Lanka, South Asia, or comparable island environments with similar physical, climatic, and institutional conditions will be considered an advantage during shortlisting.

6. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

7. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In accordance with Paragraph 3.17 - Consultants previously involved in the preparation of conceptual plans, feasibility studies, or related studies for the assignment shall disclose such involvement in their Expressions of Interest. To avoid any unfair competitive advantage, the Client shall make available to all shortlisted Consultants, together with the RFP, all relevant information that may provide a competitive advantage to any previously engaged Consultant.

8. A Consultant will be selected by following Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method in accordance with the procedures set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations: “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2025)”.

9. Interested Consultant may obtain further information from Senior Procurement Consultant, REVIVE Project at the address below during office hours 09:00 to 15:00 hours (+94 112 - 869521) Facsimile: +94 112 861 860, E-mail: proc.revive@gmail.com only on working days.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – SELECTION OF INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS)

 

Republic of Uzbekistan

Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project

Credit No.: 7425-UZ

 

Assignment Title: Stakeholder Engagement Specialist for the construction and renovation of ITES Centers

Reference No.: UZ-DIP-581365-CS-INDV

 

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the International Development Association toward the cost of the Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project. “Administration of Technology Park of Software and IT” LLC (IT Park), as the Implementing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds to engage an individual consultant as Stakeholder Engagement Specialist for Component 2.2 of the Project.

Under Component 2.2, the Project finances the construction and the reconstruction of ITES Centers in the regions.

To meet the requirements of the Project’s Environmental and Social Commitment Plan, IT Park will engage three individual consultants under separate contracts: an Environmental Specialist (including Occupational Health and Safety), a Social Specialist and a Stakeholder Engagement Specialist. This Request for Expressions of Interest concerns the Stakeholder Engagement Specialist.

The Stakeholder Engagement Specialist will support IT Park as the lead specialist for stakeholder engagement, information disclosure and the Project Grievance Redress Mechanism for the construction sites, in line with World Bank Environmental and Social Standard 10, the Project’s Stakeholder Engagement Plan and the legislation of the Republic of Uzbekistan on citizens’ appeals and access to information.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include, but are not limited to:

  • update of the SEP for Component 2.2, stakeholder mapping for each site and maintenance of the stakeholder register;

MINISTRY OF MINES AND MINERALS DEVELOPMENT

 

EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES

 

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

INDIVIDUALCONSULTING SELECTION

OPEN-NATIONAL

The Government of the Republic of Zambia will implement the Support to Transparency in Energy Transition Minerals Development Project with the involvement of the Zambia EITI National Secretariat within the Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development (MMMD). The Project development objective is to support the Government of Zambia to strengthen the transparent management of energy transition minerals through the EITI process. The Project is structured around three components: Component 1, Implementation of Data Integration and Online Reporting System for EITI Mainstreaming; Component 2, Enhancing Transparency and Accountability in Zambia’s Extractive Industries; and Component 3, Project Management. 

The Ministry seeks to recruit suitably qualified and experienced individual to express interest in the position of Environmental and Social Specialist under the Support to Transparency in Energy Transition Minerals Development Project.The successful consultant will support the implementation of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), including environmental and social risk management, stakeholder engagement, grievance redress mechanisms, environmental disclosures, and compliance with the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP).

 

1.0 JOB TITLE; ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL SPECIALIST

    1. JOB PURPOSE

The Specialist’s role shall be anchored in the Project design and shall support ESF consistency across the following components and activities:

  1. Component 1, the ZEITI data platform upgrade for online EITI reporting, data integration and interoperability activities, the audit of the Mineral Output Statistical Evaluation System, and assessment of cross-border mineral trade data between Zambia and the DRC;
  2.  Component 2, technical assistance for compliance with the 2023 EITI Standard, production and dissemination of ZEITI reports, support for state-owned enterprise disclosures, environmental and social disclosures, and stakeholder engagement on extractive sector governance; and
  3.  Component 3, project management, procurement, reporting, stakeholder coordination, grievance management, capacity building, and implementation of ESCP, SEP, GRM, and simplified ESMP requirements.

1.2 RESPONSIBITY

  1. Support the Zambia EITI National Secretariat in managing environmental, social, health, and safety risks and impacts of the Project in accordance with the ESCP and relevant ESSs.
  2. Ensure that Project-financed terms of reference, procurement documents, consultant contracts, studies, ICT and data activities, consultations, capacity-building activities, and outputs under Components 1, 2, and 3 integrate applicable environmental and social requirements.
  3. Support inclusive, accessible, and SEA/SH-sensitive stakeholder engagement, grievance management, labor and OHS provisions, incident and accident reporting, and environmental transparency in the energy transition minerals value chain.
  4. Build practical capacity within the Zambia EITI National Secretariat, the PMT, Project stakeholders, and relevant counterpart agencies on environmental and social risk management, social inclusion, grievance management, stakeholder mapping and engagement, and community health and safety.

1.3 QUALIFICATIONS AND WORK EXPERIENCE

  1. Advanced degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, social development, sociology, natural resource management, public policy, mining governance, or a related field.
  2. Minimum of 8 years of relevant experience in environmental and social risk management, stakeholder engagement, environmental governance, or public sector technical assistance, preferably in mining, natural resources, transparency, or digital governance programs.
  3. Demonstrated knowledge of the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework or comparable international standards, including application of ESF requirements to technical assistance, studies, data systems, stakeholder engagement, and capacity-building activities.
  4. Experience supporting SEP and GRM implementation, inclusive and SEA/SH-sensitive stakeholder engagement, labor management measures, worker grievance arrangements, occupational health and safety provisions, codes of conduct, and incident or accident reporting is required.
  5. Knowledge of environmental data disclosure, EITI-linked transparency initiatives, environmental compliance information, tailings governance, mine closure and rehabilitation, water quality, climate considerations, or related mining-sector issues is an asset.
  6. Strong analytical, writing, facilitation, coordination, and stakeholder engagement skills; fluency in English is required. Local language skills and experience in Zambia or the region are assets.

 

1.5 SUBMISSION DETAILS

Interested individual consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services as required in Terms of Reference. The submissions should include a cover letter summarizing the relevant experience and indicating its relevance to the assignment at hand. Applicants must meet the World Bank's eligibility requirements, including provisions relating to fraud, corruption, and sanctions. The UI is also supported by the International Labour Organization’s (ILO) Decent Work Agenda, recognizing its role as a key labour market stabilizer and a worker protection mechanism.

data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES)

Country: Pakistan

Project: Getting Results: Access and Delivery of Quality Education Services in Balochistan (GRADES-B)

Project Number: P507512

Assignment Title: Hiring of Consulting Firm for Engagement of a Third-Party Validation (TPV) Firm for Verification of Community-Based School Sites Identified by District Education Groups (DEGs) under GRADES-Balochistan

Reference No. PK-PMU-SED GOB-576103-CS-CQS

The Government of Balochistan, through the Government of Pakistan, has secured USD $100 Million funded through IDA capital credit financing from the World Bank to implement the Getting Results: Access and Delivery of Quality Education Services in Balochistan (GRADES-B) project. The project is designed to increase girls’ and boys’ enrollment in pre-primary and primary grades, and to improve reading and numeracy proficiency in primary grades, all in project-supported schools.

The GRADES-B project aims to address educational disparities in Balochistan by enhancing access, quality, and equity in education. The initiative focuses on foundational literacy and numeracy, increased enrollment, and sustainable systemic reforms. The proposed project is structured around four components to address systemic challenges in the education sector of the province. They focus on improving access to education and enhancing teaching quality, strengthening data-driven accountability, building resilience to climate change, and introducing emergency preparedness mechanisms to minimize disruptions.

Project Management Unit (here and after as the Client) intends to apply part of the proceeds to cover eligible payments for hiring the services of Consulting Firm for Engagement of a Third-Party Validation (TPV) Firm for Verification of Community-Based School Sites Identified by District Education Groups (DEGs) under GRADES-Balochistan (here and after as the Consulting Firm).

The consulting services (“the Services”) include provision of Engagement of a Third-Party Validation (TPV) Firm for Verification of Community-Based School Sites under GRADES-Balochistan, ensuring full consistency with the TOR’s referred to in this REOI.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment can be found at the following website:  https://pmubesp.gob.pk/  or can be obtained at the Office Address, House # 74-A Chaman Housing Scheme, Airport Road Quetta.

The Project Management Unit, Balochistan Education Support Project now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A consulting firm(s)/ Joint Venture(s) will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification based Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” September, 2023.

Required Expertise and Qualifications of the Firm

The Firm must be a legally registered organization (in Pakistan) with demonstrated technical capacity to conduct large-scale, geographically dispersed field verification exercises. The Firm should have:

  1. At least 10 years of experience of working in Social Sector particularly Education;
  2. Must have completed at least 3 similar experiences of conducting Third Party Validations in GIS-based geo-tagging, mapping and spatial/distance analysis;
  3. Demonstrated experience in digital/mobile data collection (e.g., KoBoToolbox, ODK, SurveyCTO or similar platforms);
  4. Proven capacity to mobilize and manage field teams across multiple, geographically remote and hard-to-access districts of Balochistan (including Sherani, Chaman, Washuk, Duki, Kohlu, Barshore, Jhal Magsi, Kachhi, Sohbatpur, Chaghi, Kharan and Musa Khel);
  5. Experience of working with government departments, education projects or development partners in Balochistan or similar rural contexts;

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, i.e. 0900 to 1700 hours.

Expressions of Interest (EOI) may be delivered in written form to the address given below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by 27th November, 2026 16:00 Hrs. EOI can be transmitted electronically by email to the email address ps.gradesb@gmail.com  and couriered subsequently.

 

Project Management Unit, Balochistan Education Support Project

House # 74-A Chaman Housing Scheme Quetta

Quetta, Pakistan

Fax: +92812864297

JAVNI POZIV ZA IZRAAVANJE INTERESA

 

Bosna i Hercegovina dobila je zajam za finansiranje od Svjetske banke za troškove Projekta unapreenja geoprostorne infrastrukture i procjene vrijednosti nekretnina (Projekt GIVE) i namjerava da iskoristi dio ovog kredita za plaanja po ugovoru za pruanje konsultantskih usluga za angaman Individualnih konsultanata u sljedeim Opinskim sudovima u Federaciji BiH (FBiH):

Federalna uprava za geodetske i imovinsko-pravne poslove i Jedinica za provedbu Projekta GIVE ovim putem pozivaju sve kvalificirane i zainteresirane Individualne konsultante da izraze svoj interes za pruanje usluga za gore navedene pozicije.

Opis projektnog  zadatka:

Individualni konsultant e na poziciji privremenog asistenta raditi na poslovima auriranja i sistematske uspostave i/ili zamjene zemljišnih knjiga prema podacima nove izmjere u zemljišnoknjinim uredima i izdvojenim organizacijskim jedinicama navedenih opinskih sudova.

Potrebne kvalifikacije:

  • Pravni fakultet VSS - VII stupanj ili visoko obrazovanje prvog, drugog ili treeg ciklusa po Bolonjskom sustavu školovanja sa najmanje 180 ECTS bodova;
  • Poznavanje rada sa MS Office programima;
  • Najmanje 1 (jedna) godina radnog iskustva na poslovima sa visokom strunom spremom;
  • Znanje iz oblasti zemljišnoknjinog prava koje se primjenjuje u FBiH.

 

Poeljno je da Individualni konsultant u vrijeme prijavljivanja na oglas posjeduje uvjerenje o poloenom ispitu opeg znanja, strunom ili pravosudnom ispitu izdato od nadlene institucije u F BiH, ali nije eliminatorno.  

Zainteresirani su obvezni uz potpisanu prijavu sa kratkim ivotopisom, sa adresom i obvezno naznaenom e-mail adresom da dostave traene dokumente:

  • univerzitetsku diplomu Pravnog fakulteta – VII stupanj, ili visoko obrazovanje prvog, drugog ili treeg ciklusa po Bolonjskom sustavu školovanja sa najmanje 180 ECTS bodova, te dodatak diplomi/diploma supplement, ako je steena po bolonjskom sustavu studiranja; ili uvjerenje o diplomiranju koje nije starije više od godinu dana od dana sticanja traene strune spreme;
  • Potvrde ili uvjerenja poslodavca ili poslodavaca kojim se nedvosmisleno dokazuje koje je poslove obavljao i u kojem razdoblju ili Uvjerenje o o radnom stau iz Zavoda za penziono/mirovinsko i invalidsko osiguranje (listing), uz obavezno dostavljanje potvrde koja razjašnjava šifre zanimanja iz uvjerenja (listinga),
  • Pismo preporuke ili druga slina isprava se uzima u obzir kada sadri sve elemente potvrde ili uvjerenja;
  • Uvjerenje/Potvrde/Certifikati o poloenom kursu ili edukaciji izdate od strane institucija koje se bave obukom za rad na raunaru ili uvjerenje o prijepisu ocjena izdato od strane visokoškolske ustanove.

 

Zainteresirani Individualni konsultanti su duni da dostave dokumentaciju (originale ili ovjerene kopije) kojom potvruju da ispunjavaju potrebne kvalifikacije navedene u ovom Pozivu za izraavanje interesa.

Odabir Individualnih konsultanata e se izvršiti putem pismenog i usmenog dijela testiranja, a testiranje e se provesti u navedenim opinskim sudovima u skladu sa Uputstvom za testiranje i odabir kandidata za radno mjesto „Privremeni asistent na poslovima auriranja i zamjene/uspostave zemljišnih knjiga“ u zemljišnoknjinim uredima Opinskih sudova Federacije BiH“. Pismeni i usmeni dio testiranja sadravat e pitanja iz oblasti Zakona o zemljišnim knjigama (SN FBiH br. 58/02, 19/03, 54/04 i 32/19 – Presuda Ustavnog suda F BiH, br. U-22/16 i 61/22), Zakona o stvarnim pravima (SN FBiH br. 66/13, 100/13 i 32/19 – Odluka US) i Pravilnika o postupanju u zemljišnoknjinim stvarima (SN FBiH, br. 5/03, 10/07, 80/11, 6/22 i 101/23).

Nepotpune (prijave bez adrese i kontakt informacija, bez priloenih dokaza o traenim kvalifikacijama), neblagovremene i neuredne prijave nee se uzimati u razmatranje.

Oekivani poetak rada u opinskim sudovima je 01.01.2027. godine, a taan datum ovisit e od datuma završetka procedure. Rok završetka angamana ovisit e od broja zaprimljenih prijavnih listova u opinskom sudu. Rad e se odvijati u navedenim zemljišnoknjinim uredima i izdvojenim organizacijskim jedinicama, a sukladno standardnom radnom vremenu opinskog suda.

Privremeni zemljišnoknjini asistenti e biti odabrani u skladu s procedurama Svjetske banke, objavljenim u priruniku “Pravilnik o nabavkama za zajmoprimce IPF“, rujan 2023, revidiran veljaa 2025. i rujan 2025. godine („Pravilnik“). Zainteresiranima se skree panja na paragraf 3.14, 3.16 i 3.17 Svjetske banke „Pravilnika“ u kojem se utvruje politika Svjetske banke o sukobu interesa.

Izrazi interesovanja moraju biti dostavljeni najkasnije 15 dana od dana objave ovog oglasa u dnevnim novinama, na adrese opinskih sudova koje su navedene na njihovim zvaninim web stranicama u kojima zainteresirani kandidati apliciraju za oglašavanu poziciju. Krajnji rok za dostavljanje prijava je 27.11.2026. godine.

Za sve dodatne informacije moete se obratiti i na sljedeu adresu: Federalna uprava za geodetske i imovinsko-pravne poslove, Projekt GIVE, Hamdije Kreševljakovia 96, 71000 Sarajevo, Bosna i Hercegovina, Tel: + 387 33 586-063, E-mail: give_procurement@fgu.com.ba .

REPUBLIQUE DEMOCRATIQUE DU CONGO

MINISTERE DE L’ENTREPRENEURIAT ET DEVELOPPEMENT DES PETITES ET MOYENNES ENTREPRISES

UNITE DE COORDINATION DU PROJET TRANSFORME/RDC

PROJET D’AUTONOMISATION DES FEMMES ENTREPRENEURES ET MISE A NIVEAU DES PME POUR LA TRANSFORMATION ECONOMIQUE ET L’EMPLOI

« TRANSFORME-RDC »

 

N° de crédit / N° de don : Banque mondiale, Crédit n°7101-ZR / Don E0280-ZR

Titre de la mission : Sélection de deux ONG pour la Mise en œuvre des activités de prévention et réponse aux EAS/HS liés au Projet sur les villes du Lobito.

N° de référence : ZR-TRANSFORME-574830-CS-CQS

Date de publication : 12 novembre 2026

Date de clôture :  27 novembre 2026

 

AVIS D’APPEL PUBLIC A MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

 

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Démocratique du Congo a sollicité et obtenu un crédit et un don de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA) d’un montant total équivalent à 300 000 000,00 USD en vue de financer le coût du « Projet d’Autonomisation des femmes entrepreneures et une mise à niveau des PME pour la transformation économique et l’emploi (TRANSFORME-RDC)» et se propose d’utiliser une partie des fonds de ce crédit et don pour financer les services des : « Organisations Non Gouvernementales (ONG) Chargées de la mise en œuvre des activités de prévention et réponse aux Exploitations et Abus sexuels/Harcèlement Sexuel (EAS/HS)».

 

  1. Le présent avis d’appel public à manifestations d’intérêt fait suite à l’Avis Général de Passations des Marchés publié sur UNDB le 12 septembre 2022 ainsi que sur les sites de Mediacongo (www.mediacongo.net) et de PADMPME (www.padmpme.cd) respectivement le 13 et 14 septembre 2022 et paru dans le journal « La Prospérité n°5916 » le 14 septembre 2022.

 

  1. Les services comprennent : (i) la réalisation des activités de lutte contre les EAS/HS dans le cadre du Projet TRANSFORME devant prendre en compte et contribuer à la mise en œuvre des principes exigés, (ii) l’actualisation de l’étude d’évaluation des risques et la cartographie des services de VBG dans la zone d’exécution du Projet, (iii) la Formation et sensibilisation, (iv) l’appui aux survivant(e)s d’ EAS/HS, (v) l’appui au mécanisme de gestion de plaintes du projet et (vi) le suivi et l’évaluation des activités d’EAS/HS.

 

Les services prévus au titre de ces contrats sont répartis en deux (2) LOTS DISTINCTS constituant deux (2) MARCHES DISCTINCTS :

 

  • Lot 1 : Lubumbashi (Lubumbashi, Kipushi et Likasi) ; et
  • Lot 2 : Kolwezi (Kolwezi et Tenke Fungurume).

 

  1. Les Termes de Reference (TDR) de la mission peuvent être consultés sur le site web suivant : www.transforme.cd, ou peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

 

  1. L’UCP-TRANSFORME invite les candidats (Organisations Non Gouvernementales « ONG ») intéressés à présenter leur candidature en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les consultants intéressés doivent produire les informations sur leur capacité et expérience démontrant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour ces prestations.

 

 

 

 

 

Le Consultant doit répondre au profil ci-après :

 

  • Être une ONG et légalement constituée dans le pays (fournir tous les documents qui justifient de son établissement et fonctionnement légal en RDC) et être installée dans l’une des villes du lot choisi ;
  • Avoir une expérience générale d’au moins sept (7) ans, dont au moins cinq (5) ans dans les activités de prévention et réponse aux VBG, notamment : (a) Mobilisation communautaire et promotion du changement des comportements, et (b) Organisation des formations sur les VBG, le harcèlement sexuel (HS) et l’exploitation et abus sexuels (EAS) ; (c) Aménagement des espaces sûrs ou points d’écoute pour les femmes et les filles ;
  • Avoir au moins cinq (5) ans d’expérience dans les activités de réponse aux VBG, notamment : (a) Gestion des cas, soutien psychosocial et psychologique ; (b) Référencement médical et mise en place des conventions de collaboration avec les formations sanitaires compétentes ; et (c) Assistance juridique et judiciaire ;
  • Avoir une expérience dans la collecte éthique de données sur la prise en charge des survivant(e)s de VBG ;
  • Avoir un code de bonne conduite et une politique interne claire visant la prévention et la réponse du harcèlement, de l’exploitation et de l’abus sexuel, y compris un plan régulier de formation du personnel conforme aux standards minimums du projet ;
  • Avoir de l’expérience dans le renforcement des systèmes locaux de redevabilité, y compris la formation et la sensibilisation sur la prévention des VBG, EAS et HS ;
  • Fournir les preuves de la tenue d’une comptabilité et avoir été audité (audit financier) au moins une fois durant les deux dernières années par des cabinets d’audit reconnus ; et
  • Avoir une expérience prouvée dans la mise en œuvre des projets financés par les bailleurs de fonds internationaux (notamment la Banque mondiale, BAD, UE, USAID, UNICEF, etc).

 

NB :

  • Pour être acceptables, les références doivent être soutenues par des certificats de bonne fin de mission ou tout autre document pouvant attester de l’effectivité de la mission (ex : les lettres ou emails d’approbation du livrable final. Les extraits de contrat ne constituent pas les preuves de l’effectivité des prestations). Bien vouloir indiquer le Client bénéficiaire, l’année de réalisation, la personne de contact et le montant du contrat et le nombre des bénéficiaires des services de l’ONG.

 

La liste restreinte comprendra cinq (05) à huit (08) firmes. Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués à l’étape de la préparation de la liste restreinte. Les candidats peuvent s’associer pour renforcer leurs compétences respectives et augmenter leur chance de qualification mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l'association est sous la forme d'un groupement. Dans le cas d'un groupement, tous les membres sont conjointement et solidairement responsables de l’ensemble de contrat, en cas de sélection.

 

  1. Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions de la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de passation des marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement (FPI) (Edition de Septembre 2025) « Règlements de Passation des marchés »), relatives aux Règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêts sont applicables.

 

  1. Un Consultant sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection fondée sur les Qualifications du Consultant (SQC). Les critères d’éligibilité, l’établissement de la liste restreinte et la procédure de sélection seront conformes aux « Règlements de passation des marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projet d’Investissement FPI (Juillet 2016, révisée en Novembre 2017, Juillet 2018, Novembre 2020 et Septembre 2023) « Règlements de Passation des Marchés » et les « Lignes Directrices » de la Banque mondiale sur la Prévention et la Lutte contre la Fraude et la Corruption dans les projets financés sur les Prêts de la BIRD, et les crédits et les subventions de l’IDA (datant du 1er juillet 2016), ainsi que les dispositions stipulées dans l’Accord de financement applicables au projet.

 

  1. Les Consultants (Organisations Non Gouvernementales « ONG ») intéressés et remplissant les conditions requises, peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse ci-dessous et aux heures suivantes : de 
    9 heures à 16 heures (heure locale, TU+1) ou sur le site web « www. transforme.cd ».  

 

 

  1. Les manifestations d’intérêt (rédigées en langue française) doivent être envoyées par écrit à l’adresse ci-dessous (en version physique ou électronique « e-mail ») au plus tard le 27 novembre 2026 à 16 heures (heure locale, TU +1) et porter clairement la mention ci-après : AMI N° ZR-TRANSFORME-574830-CS-CQS « Sélection de deux ONG pour la Mise en œuvre des activités de prévention et réponse aux EAS/HS liés au Projet sur les villes du Lobito » (Tout en indiquant clairement le lot « ou les lots » de votre choix).

Unité de Coordination du Projet d’Autonomisation des Femmes Entrepreneures et mise à niveau des PME pour la Transformation Economique et l’Emploi « UCP/ TRANSFORME-RDC »

Téléphone (+243) 830 033 033

Email : transforme@transforme.cd (avec copie à cpm@transforme.cd)

à Kinshasa/Gombe, en République Démocratique du Congo.

State Institution "Projects Implementation Center for Tajikistan Digital Foundations" of the Executive Office of the President of the Republic of Tajikistan is implementing Tajikistan Digital Foundation Project (thereafter referred to as Project) co-financed by the World Bank and the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC). The total cost of the project is US$46.2 million, of which the IDA grant is $30M, SDC Trust fund is $14.8M and GoTJ share is $1.4M. and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the Advanced Digital Skills Trainings for 1,000 individuals

 

The consultant will have to perform the following tasks:

Tasks shall include, but not be limited to, the following: Program Design and Preparation

  1. Develop a time-bound implementation plan which includes target numbers of trainees to be trained, and description of monitoring mechanisms of the training program execution and quality of training offered
  2. Develop modular digital skills training programs or use off the shelf courses on AI, Cloud, Network, System Administration and Cybersecurity aligned with labor market relevance in Tajikistan and addressing language requirements, inclusivity considerations, infrastructure constraints, and applicability of skills.
  3. Develop of complementary business soft skills training modules, that will be delivered in Russian and Tajik to enhance participants’ readiness for employment and further skills development.
  4. Ensure blended and online delivery modalities through the Platform for Educational Needs, describing delivery options, sequencing, and implementation considerations to support regional equity of access and sustainability beyond the project period.
  5. Develop an inclusive outreach and participant selection framework, including eligibility criteria and targeting approaches, to support the participation of youth, NEET populations, women, persons with disabilities, and beneficiaries in line with the inclusion targets defined in the Objective section.
  6. Develop and adapt training curricula and learning materials in Russian, English, and/or Tajik, leveraging and contextualizing existing resources available in Tajikistan and identifying gaps where supplementary materials may be required.
  7. Develop and implement employer engagement mechanisms to facilitate internships and job matching for the course beneficiaries.
  8. The Consultant shall track employment outcomes for at least six (6) months following graduation.
  9. Collaborate with other training centers to achieve the objectives of this assignment.
  10. Develop an implementation plan with milestones, deliverables, and performance indicators.
  11. Coordinate with the PIC EOP and relevant stakeholders to ensure alignment with Component 2 objectives.
  12. Transfer full documentation, training materials (free of copyrights) to PIC EOP upon contract completion.

 

Duration

The total duration of the contract is 24 months.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1avZ1BiaGMRme-LLyzJU5MgukzT2-brdg/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=101229496586602350179&rtpof=true&sd=true

The Government of Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Preparation Grant for Georgia Water Supply, Sanitation, Wastewater, and Hazardous Waste Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise preparation of an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and associated environmental and social instruments for the hazardous waste management facilities proposed under the Feasibility Study (FS). These may include pre-treatment facilities (for example, segregation, dewatering and conditioning of oily sludges, contaminated soils and chemical residues); treatment facilities (such as physico-chemical treatment, neutralization and stabilization/solidification, thermal treatment); an engineered hazardous waste landfill; and associated storage, regional waste acceptance and temporary storage facilities, access roads, utilities and transport interfaces, as confirmed through the FS and agreed project scope. GREEN, RESILIENT AND TRANSFORMATIONAL TOURISM DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (GREAT-TDP)

SELECTION OF A GRANT MANAGEMENT FIRM TO IMPLEMENT THE MATCHING GRANTS AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM UNDER GREAT-TDP (SUBCOMPONENT 1.3)

PROJECT ID: P180337, IDA CREDIT NO. 73380-ZM

Background

The Government of the Republic of Zambia has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Green, Resilient and Transformational Tourism Development Project (GREAT-TDP), which is being implemented by the Ministry of Tourism (MoT) through a Project Implementation Unit (PIU). The Project seeks to enhance the sustainability, resilience, and competitiveness of Zambia's tourism sector while promoting inclusive economic opportunities and conservation outcomes in tourism destinations.

The GREAT-TDP comprises three components:

Component 1:      Strengthening Tourism Competitiveness and Destination Management;

Component 2:       Improving Access to Resilient Infrastructure; and

Component 3:      Project Administration and Management.

Under Component 1, Subcomponent 1.3, Expanding Economic Opportunities through MSMEs and Community-Based Tourism Support, the Project provides financial and technical support to tourism-related Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), Community-Based Enterprises (CBEs), Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), and Tourism Private Sector Associations (TPSAs) through a Matching Grants and Technical Assistance Program. The Program is designed to strengthen business capacity, improve competitiveness, support sustainable tourism development, and expand economic opportunities for participating beneficiaries.

Consulting Services

The Ministry of Tourism intends to apply part of the proceeds of the financing for consulting services ("the Services"), which include the engagement of a Grant Management Company (GMC) to support the implementation and administration of the Matching Grants and Technical Assistance Program under Component 1 of the GREAT-TDP.

Name of the Proposed Project: Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP)

Assignment Title: Development of Turtle Hatchery for conservation

Reference No.: S-12

Project ID No: P501274

The People's Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Development of Turtle Hatchery for conservation for the ultimate objective of this assignment is to facilitate hatchling production for conservation of sea turtles in Sonapara, Cox’s Bazar.

  1. The broad scope of consulting services (“the Services”) includes but not limited to:
  • Inception
  • Situational Report
  • Mid-Term Progress Report
  • Comprehensive Conservation Strategy Report
  • The final report consolidating all Deliverables

 

  1. Objectives

The ultimate objective of this assignment is to facilitate hatchling production for conservation of sea turtles in Sonapara, Cox’s Bazar. The specific objectives are to: (1) understand sea turtle nesting sites’ current situation, threats, and necessary conservation actions in Sonapara; (2) establish and operationalize turtle hatchery; and (3) conduct awareness raising activities.

 

  1. Scope of Work
  1. Conduct an assessment and year-round monitoring of sea turtle nesting at Sonapara Beach

The Consultant will identify and map sea turtle nesting sites and conduct focus group discussions (FGDs) with fishers to identify threats (including bycatch, predation, human disturbance, and habitat degradation). The Consultant will monitor nesting throughout the year to capture seasonal patterns and inform conservation actions. Develop a situational report which will cover: (i) identification and characterization of critical nesting habitats; (ii) migration and population studies using appropriate, ethical methods; (iii) development of an inventory of nesting events and hatching success; (iv) documentation of mortality, nesting frequency, and nest fate; and (v) identification and quantification of sources and levels of threats (including bycatch). The Consultant will prepare a comprehensive conservation strategy report summarizing findings and proposing a Conservation Management Plan (CMP) with actionable, long-term strategies, responsibilities, and a time-bound implementation schedule. The report also summarizes the results of all the activities conducted under this assignment.

 

  1. Establish and manage turtle hatchery

The Consultant will establish a turtle hatchery and guard shed with appropriate equipment and security measures. Nests will be managed for safe in-situ incubation and hatching; where in-situ protection is not feasible, the Consultant will implement ex-situ conservation (egg relocation) following accepted protocols and required permits. The Consultant will deploy guards as needed, control predators (e.g., dogs, crows, and other predatory animals), and prevent egg poaching consistent with legal and ethical standards. The Consultant will maintain records of nests managed, relocation activities, hatching success, and predator control actions.

 

  1. Conduct awareness raising activities

The Consultant will conduct awareness meetings with fisher communities on safe handling and release of entangled turtles. The Consultant will identify turtle egg collectors and hold dialogue with them to reduce poaching and promote stewardship. The Consultant will prepare and post informational signboards at key locations, develop and print a sea turtle information poster or leaflet (1,000 copies), and organize media campaigns around turtle hatchling releases and relevant observances (e.g., World Sea Turtle Day), in coordination with local authorities and community groups.

  1. The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) can be found at the following website: www.doe.gov.bd The ToR or any further information can be obtained at the address of the undersigned given below, during office hours from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm Bangladesh Standard Time (BST).

 

  1. The Department of Environment (DoE) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.  The shortlisting criteria are:

a)   General Experience of the Firm in providing services (core business and years in business);

b)   The Consultant must have at least 10 years of in-depth working experience on Development of Turtle hatchery in Bangladesh;

 

  1. Consultants are requested to submit, but not limited to, the following supporting documents in support of the above-mentioned criteria:

(i)  The Firm's Incorporation/Trade/registration documents from the country of the firm (ii) Firm’s brochures; (iii) description of similar consultancy contracts, including the scope, contract amount, name of Client, period of the contract (date of contract signing to date of completion), location/ country of the services, etc.

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the Section III, Para 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.
  2. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable) and/or a sub-consultancy (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant). In case of an association, the Consultant must explain in the EoI submission (a) the rationale/ justification for the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants; and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment. Failure to provide the above explanation in the EoI may risk the association not being shortlisted for the assignment. However, the qualifications/ experience of sub-consultants will not be considered by the Client in the evaluation of Expressions of Interest for Shortlisting purposes.
  3. A consulting Firm will be selected following the “Consultant Qualification Selection” method.

Improving Pre- and Primary Education Frontline Workers Performance and Management (US$15 million TBC)

Improving Health Frontline Workers Performance and Management (US$15 million TBC)

Component 3:

Cross-cutting support for frontline worker management (MOHA)

Component 4:

Project management and implementation arrangement (US$ 2 million TBC)

 

Scope of Work

 

Under the guidance and supervision of Project Manager, the Procurement Consultant supports development and updating of the procurement strategy and procurement plan; carry out the procurement processes of goods, consultancies, works, and non-consultancy services and contract management  for component 2 of the Improving Frontline Worker Performance in Education and Health Project, and maintains the procurement plan and inventory systems in full conformity with the procedures, rules and guidelines of the Ministry of Health (MOH), Ministry of Finance (MOF), and the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations.

 

 

 

Responsibilities

 

  1. Assist the Project Manager in updating the Project Procurement Strategy for Development (PPSD);
  2. Ensures that procurement plan is regularly updated as required to reflect the project needs and in line with the requirements from the World Bank;
  3. Liaise and coordinate with stakeholders, relevant divisions, departments, and agencies, including donors, to support effective procurement implementation.
  4. Undertakes procurement of the project in accordance with the legal agreement between the Government and the World Bank and the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations;
  5. Ensure the timely and regular provision of procurement information to the project management team to support decision-making at all levels.
  6. Ensure the accuracy of all procurement documents, including posting procurement notices, developing terms of reference, technical specifications and performance indicators by coordinating with the implementing agencies for the inputs, placing advertisements, and inviting Expressions of Interest for services required by the project.
  7. Prepare bidding documents, including letters of invitation, descriptions of goods/equipment to be procured, and packaging of items for procurement.
  8. Arranges dispatch of documents to prospective suppliers after receipt of concurrence/approval from IDA as required;
  9. Maintains the list and contact details of all consultancy firms and individuals that have provided an expression of interest, received invitations for quotation and/or bidding documents;
  10. Prepares necessary documentation for the MOH Procurement Committee review meetings, which involves ensuring the completeness of all documentation received from bidders/suppliers, checking references and referees provided by bidders/suppliers, and the preparation of comparative sheets;
  11. Prepares evaluation reports for consultancies, certifies and validates the bid evaluation report, and ensures that the Financial Manager and the Project Manager validate the reports prior to their review by IDA as necessary, and before contract preparation;
  12. Recommends the award of contracts and ensures the approval and endorsement of contracts by the responsible authorities;
  13. Maintains the confidentiality of all procurement processes and documents prior to the award of contracts, or the raising of purchase orders;
  14. Manage and ensure that all procurement activities are properly processed in the Bank’s STEP system and all relevant procurement information and documents are properly uploaded and recorded in this system in a timely manner.
  15. Monitors and supervises the performance of contracts according to the terms and conditions of contract;
  16. Managing the procurement filing/record and tracking form system in the office in a systematic and retrievable manner;
  17. Prepares quarterly procurement plans for goods and works which are to be submitted a month in advance to the Project Manager;
  18. Prepares monthly and quarterly procurement reports and ad hoc procurement reports as requested;
  19. Prepare and submit a monthly activity progress report to the Project Manager against the procurement work plan.
  20. Provide training and on-the-job training for procurement management to MOH staff and provincial and district-level personnel.
  21. Coordinate, plan, procure, and monitor procurement tasks related to health products, including but not limited to:
  • Liaise with relevant departments to develop an annual supply plan for health products, ensuring timely delivery and mitigating the risk of stock-outs.
  • Support the finance team in financial planning to ensure it aligns with procurement schedules and that funds are available when payments are due.
  • Execute procurement of health products as per the approved procurement plan.
  • Responsible for processing importation and shipping documents required for customs clearance.
  • Monitor procurement and budget/expenditure to identify savings and/or overspending.
  • Coordinate with the finance team to ensure that any revisions to the health products budget are reflected in the detailed budget.
  1. Perform other duties as may be requested by the Project Manager and Directors.

The consultant will work on a full-time basis at the DPF, Ministry of Health situated in Vientiane.  Adequate space and equipment will be provided to perform the work. The duration of the contracts is xxx years. However, the consultant performance will be reviewed annually and only upon satisfactory performance the continuation of the contract for the next year will be approved.

 

Reporting

The consultant will report to the DPF, DHP, and HPC will be responsible for monitoring the Consultant’s performance, reviewing deliverables, providing technical guidance, coordinating with relevant departments and stakeholders, and ensuring that the services are implemented in accordance with the contract requirements and the Terms of Reference.

  • A Bachelor’s degree in Procurement, Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Law, Engineering, or a related field. A Master’s degree or relevant professional certification in procurement will be an advantage.
  • At least 5 years of professional experience in procurement, including experience in procurement planning, preparation of bidding documents, evaluation of bids/proposals, contract management, and procurement monitoring.
  • Demonstrated experience in procurement activities for projects financed by international development partners, such as the World Bank, IDA, ADB, WHO, or other donor-funded projects.
