REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS)

 

Country: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

Project: Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase Two (LLRP-II)

Credit no/grand no:  7519-ET.

Assignment Title : Consultancy Services for Design Review and Construction Supervision of Awadi Geberoch Climate-Resilient Diversion Irrigation and Drainage Scheme in Argoba Woreda

Procurement Reference No.: ET-AFR-RPCU-569666-CS-QCBS

 

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase II (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include : ensure that the proposed irrigation and drainage infrastructure is properly designed, constructed, and completed in accordance with the approved engineering designs, technical specifications, contractual requirements, applicable standards, and environmental and social safeguards.

 

The service comprises :Review the completed detailed engineering design, verify construction readiness, supervise construction and administer the works contract, and provide completion, commissioning, handover and Defects Liability Period services. Protect the Client’s technical, financial, environmental and social interests while administering the works contract impartially and in accordance with its terms. To ensure the development of a reliable, efficient, and climate-resilient irrigation and drainage system at Awadi Geberoch Climate-Resilient Diversion Irrigation and Drainage Scheme in Argoba Woreda.

 

The implementation period is 10 (ten ) calendar months from the date of commencement.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

 

The Afar National Regional State, Office of the President, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria are:

a) Core business and years in business:

The Expression of Interest should focus on the firm’s corporate capability and comparable assignments, and should include, as applicable: A brief profile of the firm, including its legal status, year of establishment, ownership, organizational structure, core business areas and relevant technical capacity. Evidence of experience in irrigation and drainage infrastructure design review, construction supervision and/or contract administration, particularly diversion headworks, canals, hydraulic structures and on-farm irrigation development.

Details of comparable assignments completed and/or ongoing, including the assignment name and country/location, client, contract value (where disclosable), scope and relevance, commencement/completion dates, and the firm’s role.

Experience on projects financed by the World Bank, IFAD or other development partners, where applicable. Evidence of capacity to manage multidisciplinary engineering and ESHS supervision services, including environmental and social safeguards, occupational and community health and safety, land access/resettlement follow-up and stakeholder engagement.

Information on the firm’s availability and capacity to mobilize and maintain a resident supervision team in the project area.

For a joint venture or association, details of each member, the proposed form of association, the lead member and the respective roles and responsibilities. Relevant experience of each member should be clearly identified.

B) General experience: The Consulting Firm has extensive general experience in providing multidisciplinary engineering consultancy services, including feasibility studies, detailed engineering design, construction supervision, contract administration, and project management of irrigation, drainage, water resources development, and other related civil infrastructure projects.

C)   Specific experience: The Firm possesses relevant experience in the supervision and management of irrigation infrastructure development projects, including diversion weirs, river intake structures, irrigation canals, hydraulic structures, drainage networks, flood protection works, and associated civil engineering facilities. The Firm has experience in ensuring construction quality assurance and quality control, monitoring contractors' performance, supervising construction methodologies, reviewing and approving technical submissions, verifying work measurements, preparing progress reports, and ensuring compliance with approved engineering designs, technical specifications, contractual requirements, and applicable environmental and social safeguards.

D) Technical and managerial capability of the firm:  organizational capacity and has experience in ensuring construction quality assurance and quality control, monitoring contractors' performance, supervising construction methodologies, reviewing and approving technical submissions, verifying work measurements, preparing progress reports, and ensuring compliance with approved engineering designs, technical specifications, contractual requirements, and applicable environmental and social safeguards.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 7:00 A.M. to 6:00 P.M. ( EAT), on working days.

 

 Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, in hard copy) by  30 November  2026 at 9:00 A.M. East Africa Time (EAT).

The address referred above is:

 

                                                      Afar National Regional State, Office of the President,

                                                      Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II),

                                                     Afar Regional Project Coordination Unit (RPCU)

                                                    Attn: Procurement Officer , Tadesse Gebeyehu , Room No. 7

                                                     Tel: +251 33 666 0188, /  +251-912- 68- 90- 22/ +251- 933-80-62-

Systems Coordinator (Systematic Observations Financing Facility)

The Government of Samoa through the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Pacific Region Preparedness, Adaptation and Resilience (PREPARE) - Samoa Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include provision of overseeing activities funded by the Systematic Observations Financing Facility (SOFF) grant under the PREPARE-Samoa Project for the MNRE, while providing technical assistance to support the planning, coordination, implementation, management, monitoring, and review of activities funded under SOFF, with a focus on the key components and outputs that MNRE is responsible for delivering.

The assignment will be undertaken by an Individual Consultant (IC) on a full-time basis in Samoa for an initial period of 24 months, with a possible extension subject to performance appraisal and MNRE’s project needs. Hiring a Consulting Firm for Supervision of Development Works of Cyohoha Irrigation Scheme

The Government of Rwanda has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Commercialization and De-risking for Agricultural Transformation (CDAT) Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for hiring a consulting firm for supervision of development works of Cyohoha irrigation scheme.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is available on RAB’s website at www.rab.gov.rw.

The Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB), through the Commercialization and De-risking for Agricultural Transformation (CDAT) Project, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the above Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services including the firm’s core business and years in business, and evidence of relevant assignments of similar nature and complexity

The shortlisting criteria are:

  • General experience of at least 15 years in the design and/or construction supervision of pumped irrigation schemes,
  • Specific experience in successfully completed assignments of similar nature and complexity involving supervision of pressurized irrigation systems and associated infrastructure, including headworks, pumping stations, sedimentation basins, pipeline networks, and irrigation reservoirs. Consultants shall provide details of relevant assignments, including the client, assignment description, contract period, contract value, and evidence of successful completion.

The shortlist will contain five (5) to eight (8) firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers,” seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09h00 to 17h00 hours

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below in person, or by e-mail by November 30, 2026, at 12h00p.m. (Rwanda local time).

SPIU-RAB Head office

Attn: Stephen RWAMULANGWA/SPIU-RAB Coordinator

postal address and/or street address: Blue Star House 35 KG 7 Ave, Kigali

Kacyiru Sector, Gasabo District, City of Kigali-Rwanda

Tel: +250 738461866

E-mail: infospiu@rab.gov.rw

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN

CONNECTIVITY AND TRANSPORT SECTOR IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

Project ID: P509487

Assignment Title: Fit-gap analysis in the field of sustainable development, ESG reporting (SASB, IFRS 1/2), development of a decarbonization program, industrial safety, independent reporting certification, and obtaining an ESG rating

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): UZ-CTSI-1004-CS-QCBS-UTY-PM-05

The Republic of Uzbekistan has applied for financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) of the World Bank Group toward the cost of the Connectivity and Transport Sector Improvement Project (CTSIP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the enhancement of the Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) practices of JSC “O‘zbekiston temir yo‘llari” and its Group entities, comprising a Double Materiality Assessment (DMA); assessment of sustainability-related financial risks and opportunities, including climate-related physical and transition risks and opportunities; an integrated ESG diagnostic covering governance, strategy, risk management, data and internal controls, and readiness for IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 reporting; targeted implementation of both ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 management systems at three common operational sites, together with capacity transfer and tools for subsequent Group rollout; a Scope 1, Scope 2 and material Scope 3 GHG emissions inventory and an air pollutant emissions assessment for the 2024, 2025 and 2026 reporting years, and development of decarbonization and air pollutant emissions reduction programs; and preparation of a 2025 SASB-aligned Sustainability Report and a 2026 IFRS S1/S2-aligned Sustainability Report, together with strengthening of internal sustainability reporting readiness. The Services also include support for one initial engagement cycle with one ESG rating agency selected and contracted by the Client. The Client shall pay the agency’s fees; the Consultant shall not guarantee a particular rating outcome.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

JSC “O‘zbekiston temir yo‘llari” (the “Client”) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

1. At least 5 comparable assignments completed during the last 5 years involving the preparation and/or assurance of sustainability reports under SASB, IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards and/or GRI Standards for companies in transport, infrastructure, utilities, energy, extractives, manufacturing or other asset-intensive sectors. The demonstrated experience shall include direct preparation of sustainability reports.

2. At least 4 comparable ESG diagnostic assignments completed during the last 5 years for companies in the above sectors. The experience shall cover governance, management systems, data, internal controls and disclosure processes, including at least two assignments involving IFRS S1/S2 readiness, implementation or reporting.

3. At least 3 comparable assignments completed during the last 5 years involving climate-risk and opportunity assessments, scenario analysis and assessment of potential financial effects. At least 1 assignment shall involve infrastructure, industrial operations or other long-lived physical assets.

4. At least 5 comparable assignments completed during the last 5 years involving Scope 1, Scope 2 and material Scope 3 GHG inventories under the GHG Protocol and/or ISO 14064-1, including decarbonization measures, target pathways or transition-planning inputs.

5. At least 2 comparable double materiality assessment completed during the last 5 years using ESRS requirements and EFRAG guidance.

6. At least 3 comparable assignments completed during the last 5 years involving ISO 14001- and/or ISO 45001-aligned management systems. The combined experience shall cover both standards and include practical implementation, procedures and controls, training, internal audits, management review and corrective actions.

Experience providing ESG, sustainability, governance, climate or corporate transformation advice to state-owned enterprises, sovereign holding companies or public-sector entities will be considered a strong advantage. Railway-sector experience shall not be mandatory unless expressly specified for a particular role.

(Note: Consultants shall clearly describe relevant assignments, indicating the client, country, duration, scope of services, financing source, and role of the firm.)

The same assignment may satisfy more than one experience criterion where its scope, outputs and the relevant entity’s or expert’s role are clearly evidenced. Evidence may include completion certificates, acceptance acts, client references or equivalent contractual documentation. Anonymized evidence may be provided where confidentiality restrictions apply.

Relevant experience of joint venture members shall be assessed against their assigned roles. Specialized ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 experience may be demonstrated by a named sub-consultant where permitted by the procurement documents and supported by a substantive role and committed resources. Experience of an affiliated or network firm shall not be attributed automatically to the bidder; that entity’s formal participation, assigned responsibilities and committed resources shall be identified.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The shortlist will contain 5 to 8 firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method, as set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and as further detailed in the Request for Proposals (RFP).

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by November 30, 2026 12.00 o’clock (midday by Tashkent time). Late expressions of interest will be rejected.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

Consulting Services for the Reengineering and Standardization of INEFOP's Main Processes and Procedures

CONSULTING SERVICES – QUALITY AND COST-BASED SELECTION (QCBS)

2.2.14./C-2.2.14/COMP.2/CS/INEFOP-2026

The Government of Angola, through the Ministry of Public Administration, Labor and Social Security (MAPTSS), via the National Institute of Employment and Vocational Training (INEFOP) and with the support of the World Bank, received funding of US$250 million for the implementation of the Angola Youth Employment and Opportunities Project (AYEOP/JOVEM+, P505158), approved by the World Bank Board of Directors on March 20, 2025, and intends to apply part of this funding to the contracting of consultancy services for the reengineering and standardization of INEFOP's main processes and procedures.

This consultancy aims to hire a specialized company or consortium to diagnose, redesign, standardize, and validate 18 mission, management, and support processes, based on quality management standards. These include processes for financial management, asset management, human resources management, customer service and service center management, information technology (IT), communication, and document management and archiving, as well as capacity building and an institutional adoption plan.

The consultancy is expected to be completed within nine (9) months from the start date of services, which is considered to be the time required to complete these tasks. The terms of reference can be obtained at the email address indicated below.

The Employment and Opportunities Project for Young People in Angola (AYEOP/JOVEM+) hereby invite eligible companies ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services, submitting their expressions of interest, certificates/diplomas and other supporting documents deemed necessary for the application.

The consultant must possess the following qualifications: a. A minimum of 5 years of experience and three completed projects of a comparable nature. The experience must demonstrate, collectively, process reengineering, institutional modernization, procedures, and quality management, with at least two projects in public institutions or service delivery networks of comparable size. At least one project must include the application of quality management benchmarks, and at least one must cover employment, vocational training, social services, or public services directed at citizens. A single contract may demonstrate more than one area. The supporting documents must identify the subject matter, client, period, services actually provided, and results delivered. The experience of the consortium members will be related to the proposed distribution of responsibilities. Key personnel will not be evaluated at this stage of the expressions of interest assessment.

Consultants will be evaluated based on the World Bank's Procurement Standards and Regulations for Investment Project Finance Borrowers of September 2025, and should therefore pay attention to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of said Standards, which define the World Bank's policy on conflicts of interest. The document can be consulted at the following link:

https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/c84273d1b230aeb2b0b8134de5dc8cd7-0290012025/original/Procurement-Regulations-7th-Edition-Sep-2025.pdf

The consultant will be selected based on a quality and cost-based selection method in accordance with the current Procurement Standards and Regulations (September 2025).

Interested consultants may obtain additional information, including the TORs (Terms of Reference), at the address indicated below from Monday to Friday between 8:00 AM and 4:00 PM (Angola time).

Expressions of interest (and other relevant information) should be sent by email by November 30, 2026 at 3:30 PM (Angola time).

FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OF SOMALIA

MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT AND CIVIL AVIATION

(MoTCA)

Somalia Infrastructure Development for Access and Jobs, Phase 1

(STAIRS2JOBS) PROJECT

 EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES

PIU Project Coordinator

Country: Federal Government of Somalia

Project ID No: P513127

Project: Somalia infrastructure development for access and jobs, phase 1 (stairs2jobs) project

Consultant Service: MOTCA PIU Project Coordinator 

Individual/Firm: Individual

Duty Station: Mogadishu

Revised Deadline: November 30 2026

Ref: SO-MOTCA-567865-CS-INDV

 

ADDENDUM

This is an addendum to the Procurement Notice ref:- SO-MOTCA-567865-CS-INDV published on 10 November 2026. Please kindly take note of the new submission deadline of November 30th, 2026. All other aspects of the notice remain unchanged.

1.  BACKGROUND OF THE PROJECT

The Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation (MoTCA) is implementing the Somalia Infrastructure Development for Access and Jobs, Phase 1 (Stairs2Jobs) Project, financed by the World Bank under the Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA). The Project Development Objective (PDO) of Phase 1 is to increase access to resilient infrastructure and infrastructure sector jobs, and to improve the capacity of select institutions.

MoTCA is responsible for the overall management, coordination, supervision, and implementation of all project activities under the Ministry. This includes ensuring the timely implementation of civil works; the procurement of goods, works, and services; and compliance with applicable environmental and social requirements. The Ministry oversees contractors and supervision consultants to ensure that project activities are implemented in accordance with the required technical, quality, environmental, and social standards. It is also responsible for managing project financial activities in coordination with the EAFD, facilitating the timely processing of payments, and preparing periodic work plans, budgets, progress reports, and other required project documentation.

In addition, MoTCA is responsible for implementing the project’s Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), monitoring and evaluating implementation progress and results, addressing implementation challenges, and regularly reporting project performance, progress, and key issues to the World Bank.

To strengthen the effective management, coordination, and implementation of these responsibilities, MoTCA intends to utilise financing under the Stairs2Jobs Project to recruit a Project Coordinator to support the Ministry in the overall coordination and implementation of project activities.

2.  RESPONSIBILITIES

The PIU Project Coordinator for MoTCA will serve as the focal point for coordination and leadership in the effective planning, implementation, and monitoring of all activities under the Stairs2Jobs Project at the MoTCA level. The Project Coordinator will be responsible for overseeing cross-sectoral project activities, ensuring they are implemented in line with approved project objectives, timelines, and budgets. He or she will facilitate coordination and communication among key stakeholders to ensure smooth and efficient project delivery.

All specific duties and responsibilities are detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR), available on the Ministry’s website at https://motca.gov.so, or upon request via in-person submission or email.

3.  SELECTION CRITERIA

The selection shall be based on the qualifications, experience, and skills of the candidate, followed by an interview. The required qualifications, experience, and competencies include:

  • A master’s degree in transport or aviation management, engineering, infrastructure management, public administration, business administration, accounting, economics, or another discipline directly relevant to infrastructure project implementation, institutional coordination, or public-sector programme management, from a recognised university.
  • A minimum of ten (10) years of progressively responsible professional experience in project management, infrastructure implementation, transport, aviation, or public administration — of which at least four (4) years must be in transportation, aviation, or infrastructure development related roles, preferably within an FCV context and/or on donor-funded projects.
  • Certification in one or more of the following areas will be given preference: Transport Operations or Planning (TPP), Infrastructure Project Management, Consulting Engineering (FIDIC), Air Traffic Control (ATC), Aeronautical Information Management/Services (AIM), Communication, Navigation and Surveillance (CNS), Airport Management, or other relevant technical certifications from recognised institutions.
  • Demonstrated experience working with government ministries, departments, and agencies (MDAs), development partners, or multilateral institutions.

4.  REPORTING

The Consultant will report to the Director General of MoTCA and work under the overall guidance of the World Bank Task Team Leaders for the Stairs2Jobs Project.

5.  DURATION OF ASSIGNMENT

The MoTCA PIU Project Coordinator shall be contracted for an initial period of one (1) year, renewable subject to a satisfactory performance evaluation by the Ministry, approval by the World Bank, and the availability of project funds.

6.  SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

The Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation (MoTCA) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned services. Interested consultants must submit the following:

  • A Curriculum Vitae (CV) including three (3) referees.
  • Copies of certificates of academic qualifications.
  • Copy of passport or ID
  • A cover letter indicating that they are qualified to perform the services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing — Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, and September 2025) (the “Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

7.  DEADLINE AND ADDRESS FOR SUBMISSION

Expressions of Interest and CVs must be delivered to the address below — by hand, mail, courier, or email — on or before Monday, 30th November 2026 at 16:00 hours.

Interested applicants may obtain further information, including the detailed Terms of Reference, from MoTCA in person or by email at the address given below during office hours, from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Saturday to Thursday.

ADDRESS FOR SUBMISSION

Attention:  Abdirahman Mohamed

Acting PIU Coordinator, Stairs2Jobs Project

Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation (MoTCA)

Physical address: Shangaani District Corso Somalia Street

Email: to: stairs2jobs.procurement@motca.gov.so  

Cc: dg@motca.gov.so

Office hours: 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m., Saturday to Thursday.

Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh

Ministry of Social Welfare

Department of Social Services

Strengthening Social Protection for Improved Resilience,

Inclusion, and Targeting (SSPIRIT) Project

21/1 & 21/2 Bir Uttam A.N.M. Nuruzzaman Sarak,

Shyamoli Square (9th Floor), Shyamoli, Dhaka-1207.

   Memo No.41.01.0000.126.07.024.2026-413                                                   Date: 03 November, 2026

 

Request for Expression of Interest (REOI)

 

The World Bank is supporting the Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh to better serve the poorest and most vulnerable populations by expanding coverage and strengthening delivery of the national social protection system for the poor through an IDA Credit of USD 200 million for the “Strengthening Social Protection for Improved Resilience, Inclusion and Targeting (SSPIRIT)” project. Key features of the initiative include, i) establishment and roll out of a Dynamic Social Registry (DSR), which will act as a central platform to improve the accuracy and efficiency of identifying and supporting beneficiaries; ii) strengthening Institutional Capacity for service delivery; iii) enhancing benefits adequacy of allowance programs; iv) strengthening skills development and complementary services; and v) providing tailored livelihood support to vulnerable group.

 

DSS intends to utilize a part of this credit to hire a Safeguard Specialist as an individual national consultant to ensure effective management of the Project.   

 

  1. Safeguard Specialist (Package No. SD-03): 1 Position

 

Qualifications & Experience

  1. At least a Master’s Degree from a reputed university in Environmental Management, Natural Resource Management, Sociology, or other Social Sciences;
  2. At least Seven (07) years of relevant operational ES experience and proven track record in working on projects covering a broad range of environmental and social management and development issues.
  3. Experience with World Bank projects would be preferred.
  4. Ability to think strategically and conduct dialogue on environmental and social development policies and priorities, while maintaining a strong sense of realism with regard to context, conditions and competing demands for resources;
  5. Experience of working with field level and local Government officials and local NGOs is highly desirable;
  6. Excellent spoken and written Bengali and English skills.

 

  • SSPIRIT, DSS now invites eligible applicant(s) to indicate their interest in providing the services mentioned above. The Applicants are invited for providing information in detail including their qualifications to perform the service (complete CV along with a description of the similar assignment, experience in similar position and conditions, general qualification etc.)

 

  • A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants (SIC) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. The Procurement Regulations can be viewed at the World Bank’s external website: https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/178331533065871195-0290022020/original/Procurement Regulations.pdf

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn in particular to:

(i) Section III, paragraphs, 3.15, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Sixth Edition, February 2025setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest, and (ii) Section III, paragraphs, 3.20-3.25 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Sixth Edition, February 2025 setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Eligibility, including the specific pre-requisite conditions to be met for the eligibility, on exceptional basis of Government officials and civil servants of the Borrower’s country under consulting contracts in the Borrower’s country.

 

  • Individuals who are currently working as Safeguard Specialist/Environmental Specialist/Social Specialist on another World Bank-financed project may also compete in this selection process, but if they are selected, they will be required before signing the proposed contract to provide documentary evidence of having satisfactorily complied with their existing contract’s requirements with respect to early termination of the contract by the consultant, including advance notice period, to avoid disruption in implementation of that project.

 

  • Expression of Interest shall have to be submitted to the address mention below (in person, by mail or through email: procurement.sspirit.dss@gmail.com) by 30 November, 2026 by 4:00 pm and be clearly marked as "Expressions of Interest for the position of (………….……………………..………)” in the email’s subject line or on top of the envelope.

 

  • The client reserves the right to accept or reject any/all Expressions of Interest (EOI) or cancel the EOI process at any stage without assigning any reason whatsoever and without incurring any liability to the affected applicant(s).

 

  • TOR can be found at the following website: http://www.dss.gov.bd/; further information in this regard could be obtained from the undersigned during office hours (9:00 AM to 4:00 PM BST).

data.notice_text:
Country:          Federal Government of Somalia (FGS)

Name of the Project: Somalia Productive, Resilient, and Inclusive Growth (SPRING)

 

Assignment Title: Cybersecurity Expert for National Payment System (NPS)

Project ID:     P501662

Individual/Firm:   Individual Selection

Deadline for submission of EOI: November 30,2026 at 4:00pm

Ref No.   SO-MOF-576060-CS-INDV

 

1. Background: In May 2025, the Federal Republic of Somalia, through its Ministry of Finance (MoF) launched the Somalia Productive, Resilient, and Inclusive Growth (SPRING) project. The project development objective is to promote private sector-led growth and job creation by improving the business-enabling environment, strengthening the financial system, and enhancing access to finance.

The SPRING project is organized around four components (three mutually reinforcing and one supporting): (i) Component 1: Improving the enabling environment for the private sector; (ii) Component 2: Deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity; (iii) Component 3: Enhancing access to finance and resilience for MSMEs; and (iv) Component 4: Project Management. A wide range of activities will be implemented as part of this project to reach its development objective, such as improvements to regulatory/institutional frameworks, the rollout of the digital ID system, financial sector reforms, the creation of a risk-sharing mechanism, and the provision of business development services for micro, small and medium enterprises in select economic sectors, among others.

The MoF received US$105 million from the World Bank, including US$10 million from the Somalia Multi-Partner Fund to implement the SPRING project. As part of this initiative, deepening financial sector reforms and strengthening institutional capacity, MoF intends to apply part of the proceeds from the World Bank to finance the position of Cybersecurity Expert for National Payment System (NPS).

2. Responsibilities: The Cyber Security Expert will provide Cybersecurity Strategy, Governance & Function Establishment; Cyber Risk Management, Compliance & Assurance; Security Architecture, Engineering & Secure Development; Security Operations, Monitoring & Incident Response; Identity, Privileged; Vulnerability Management, Security Testing & Threat Management; Cyber Resilience, Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery; Participant, Third-Party & Supply-Chain Security; Security Awareness, Team Capability & Knowledge Transfer; All other specific tasks detailed in the Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website link:  https://sps.so/docs/TOR%20for%20Cybersecurity%20Expert%20Terms%20at%20NPS.pdf

3.Skills and qualifications

 Selection Criteria: The selection shall be based on the qualifications, experience and skills of the candidate and followed by an interview. The qualifications, experience and competencies include:

  • Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, Information Technology, Network Security, Computer Engineering, or a closely related discipline is required. A Master's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Security, Computer Networks and Security, Information Systems, Technology Risk, or a related discipline is strongly preferred.
  • Minimum 10 years of progressive professional experience in cybersecurity, information security, technology risk, IT governance, or security assurance, with substantial hands-on responsibility in regulated or high-availability environments.
  • At least 5 years of experience in a senior, lead, managerial, or consulting role responsible for information-security governance, cyber-risk management, security operations, or cybersecurity transformation.
  • Demonstrated experience establishing, materially uplifting, or leading an information-security or cybersecurity function, ISMS, SOC/security-monitoring capability, incident-response programme, or comparable enterprise security capability.
  • At least two recognized professional cybersecurity or information-security credential is required, such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, GIAC, ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Implementer/Lead Auditor or Senior Lead Implementer, or an equivalent recognized certification.

4. Duration: The proposed duration for the assignment is Twelve Months (12) calendar months from starts date.

5. The Ministry of Ministry of Finance now invites eligible consulting (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the above-mentioned Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services and furnish the Curriculum Vitae (CV).

6. Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14, 3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services dated in September 2023 (Procurement Regulations), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.    

7. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

8. Interested Consultant may obtain further information (in person or by e-mail) at the address below during office hours from 8.00 a.m. – 4.00 p.m. Saturday to Thursday except on public holidays.

9. Deadline for submission: Expressions of interest should be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by November 30, 2026, at 4:00pm (Somalia Local time)

Shangani District, Mogadishu, Somalia

data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

COUNTRY: Central Asia region (Republic of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Republic of Uzbekistan, Republic of Tajikistan)

NAME OF PROJECT: Central Asia Regional Electricity Market Interconnectivity and Trade Project (P509488)

                                                             Grant No.: D0247          

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services to Design, Implement, and Maintain Central Asia Pilot Short-Term Electricity Market

Reference No. UZ-CDC ENERGIA-CS1-QCBS

The CDC "Energia" intends to procure consultancy services  ("the Services") including the Design, Implement, and Maintain Central Asia Pilot Short-Term Electricity Market, financed under the World Bank’s Regional Electricity Market Interconnectivity and Trade (REMIT) Project.

Objective

The objective of this assignment is to prepare the necessary legal agreements and documents to govern the operation of the Central Asian pilot market, develop and implement a trading platform for running the Central Asian pilot market and a settlement solution, implement the market, and provide pilot market operation as a service for a period of 24 months after system is operationalized, with an option for subsequent yearly extension of service if requested by the Client.

The consultancy will cover a pilot market for all Central Asia participating countries. Provision needs to be made by the consultant for future market products, and expansion in participating countries and market participants.

 

The expected commencement date for the assignment is May 2027. The duration of the assignment shall be 18 months for implementation (Phase 1) from the date of contract signature, plus 24 months of services for Central Asia .pilot market live operation (Phase 2), with an optional yearly extension of service thereafter.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website link: https://udc.uz/request-for-expressions-of-interestconsulting-services-firms-selection/.

The Coordination Dispatch Center "Energia" (CDC "Energia") now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Core Business (Areas of Expertise). The Consultant must demonstrate extensive and in-depth experience in power market design and advisory, power exchange, market operation, electricity trading and settlement platform provision.
  • Years in Business – The Firm must be minimum 5 years of business related to the assignment.
  • Experience in Similar Assignments. The Consultant must demonstrate experience in the fields of (i) design of day-ahead or short-term markets, including market rules, price formation and clearing algorithm, and cross-border capacity allocation ; (ii) delivery and go-live of trading and settlement platforms (iii) operation of a market as a service. For each project performed, the Consultant shall provide the name and contact address of the client (office and e-mail address and telephone number), date(s) of execution, name(s) of lead and associate firms, contract amount, and financing sources.
  • Technical and Managerial Capability. The Consultant must demonstrate competencies in:
    • Electricity market concepts and industry trends
    • Power system economics
    • Power market operations
    • System operations of interconnected power systems

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank's "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" dated September 2025 ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Further, the experience of a parent company, subsidiary company, group of companies, or associates of the firm shall not be considered in the evaluation.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. The intended contract type with the selected Consultant for the 2 phases: Phase 1- lump-sum and Phase 2- time-based.

Further information can be obtained from CDC "Energia" at the address below.

Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport and Telecommunication

 

Terms of Reference

 

for

 

Project Manager

 

Micro Small Medium Enterprises (MSME) and Related Technical Assistance
World Bank / NRPB SPEAR Project – Sint Maarten

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Background and context

Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) constitute approximately 95% of all businesses in Sint Maarten and form the backbone of employment, entrepreneurship, and economic resilience. Recognizing their central role, the Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport and Telecommunication (MinTEATT), through the Department of Economy, Transport and Telecommunication (ETT), is undertaking a comprehensive update of four (4) interrelated MSME-related policies, and the MSME institutional strengthening support programs. These two projects are being implemented under The Sustaining Program Effectiveness and Advancing Resilience (SPEAR) Project, funded by the Government of the Netherlands through the Sint Maarten Reconstruction, Recovery, and Resilience Trust Fund (TF) administered through the World Bank and implemented through the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB)[1].   The Sustaining Program Effectiveness and Advancing Resilience (SPEAR) Project is a strategic initiative led by the Government of Sint Maarten and the National Recovery Program Bureau (NRPB), with support from the Sint Maarten Trust Fund. It aims to enhance the operational effectiveness of recovery efforts and build long-term institutional resilience. The Trust Fund is governed by a tripartite Steering Committee composed of representatives from Sint Maarten, the Netherlands, and the World Bank, which allocates resources to short-, medium-and long-term recovery and capacity-building initiatives.  SPEAR has the following objectives:

  • Enhance the operational capacity and effectiveness of the National Recovery Program Bureau, and
  • Strengthen the institutional and technical capacity of the Government of Sint Maarten to ensure sustainability of investments.

Scope of Work

This task falls within the second component of SPEAR.

  1. A Policy Consultant or firm is engaged to lead the development of four (4) policy documents: These policies form the foundation of Sint Maarten’s MSME business environment. Updating these policies is essential to reflect the current realities, economic conditions, and evolving dynamics of the local business climate—while also anticipating future needs. At the heart of these policy updates is the goal of fostering a supportive, enabling environment in which entrepreneurs and businesses can thrive and operate efficiently. These revisions aim to strike a thoughtful balance between encouraging economic activity and safeguarding the quality of life, ensuring that Sint Maarten remains a safe, vibrant, and sustainable place to live, work, and do business. The policies are:
  1. The National MSME Policy
  2. The Investment and Diversification Policy
  3. The Residential Economic Policy (REP)
  4. The Beach and Vending Policy

The policy revisions are intended to align and update these policies to reflect current day realities on Island. The update is expected to be informed by data-driven strategies including the proposed World Bank Enterprise Survey[2]. Such data along with the revised policy documents are essential to sustaining progress and achieving inclusive economic growth in the vital Medium Micro and Small Enterprise (MSME) sector in Sint Maarten.  Therefore, the updates, will be critical to ensure alignment between these operational aspects, policy development, MinTEATT priorities, and overall GoSXM priorities.

  1. In parallel to the policy revisions, MinTEATT has requested technical assistance from the ongoing Enterprise Support Project (ESP), funded by the same Trust Fund, to support the execution of the operational aspects of MSME programs. This assistance focuses on institutional strengthening of MSME related institutions including the Sint Maarten Entrepreneurship Development Center (SEDC) and the Chamber of Commerce (COCI). The MSME support areas are:  

 

  1. Governance and Oversight Framework: The objective is to strengthen the Ministry’s oversight and governance of MSME support
  2. Monitoring and Evaluation’ (M&E) framework: Development of an M&E framework for MSME support programs.
  3. Standard Operating procedures (SOPs): Establish SOPs for MSME support programs in key aspects to include basic business training, one-on-one business advisory, and business coaching.
  4. Funding mechanisms for MSME support programs.

Terms of reference for these activities are being developed.

Role of the Project Manager

The Project Manager will be responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the SPEAR Project policy development and the ESP MSME institutional strengthening support programs components. This responsibility includes coordinating with the Policy Consultant and other Consultants hired through ESP, managing project workflow, coordinating with Min TEATT/ETT, facilitating stakeholder engagement and ensuring compliance with all project requirements.   The Project Manager will also be responsible for overseeing the day-to-day execution of the project process; maintaining project timelines; ensuring compliance with Government of Sint Maarten requirements; and facilitating the successful delivery of all project outputs. In this role, the project manager shall organize and supervise the identification, formulation, approval, implementation and completion of all activities under the component and liaise with the Project Implementation Unit at the Ministry of Finance (SPEAR) and National Recovery Program Bureau (ESP). Functional responsibilities for the role include:

  1. Project Management and Coordination
  2. Communication with Relevant Stakeholders
  3. Reporting and Monitoring and Evaluation
  4. Oversight and Quality Management

Under the supervision of the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Finance for overall project coordination and administrative oversight, and of the Ministry of TEATT, through ETT, for policy direction and substantive technical oversight, the Project Manager is expected to perform the following tasks. ETT will guide the policy content, review and validate project outputs, and ensure alignment with the Ministry’s priorities, with final policy approval remaining with the competent authorities:

Project Management and Coordination

  • Oversee the execution of the policy development update process and the development of MSME Support Programs ensuring that activities, deliverables and timelines across both workstreams progress in line with approved plans
  • Coordinate with Policy Consultants to monitor the project’s progress, address challenges, and ensure alignment with project objectives and timelines.
  • Facilitate and participate in regular project meetings with MinTEATT/ETT, NRPB, Ministry of Finance, the Policy Consultant and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Work directly with project counterparts and relevant stakeholders to ensure deliverables fall within the applicable scope and budget. This will involve coordinating with departments within the Government as well as external counterparts, including NRPB, to ensure all aspects of each project are compatible and to clarify specific requirements of each project.
  • Ensure project milestones are achieved on-time and that deliverables meet the required quality standards.
  • Identify and manage project risks, developing mitigation strategies as needed.
  • Manage the project budget, track expenditures and ensure allocated resources are used in accordance with approved plans.
  • Participate as a member of the bid evaluation team during the contracting process.
  • Support the selection of new project staff or consultants as needed.
  • Support the revision process of operational project documents (e.g., project operations manual, procurement plan, and environmental and social management plan), as needed. Participate and/or lead technical meetings with agency counterparts and project participant
  • Regularly supervise and report on project execution progress and budget performance
  • Assist with the preparation of progress reports and actionable information as required by Government to support its reporting commitments to the Council of Ministers, the Trust Fund Steering Committee and the World Bank, as needed.
  • Any other task related to this function that will contribute to the objectives of the project

Communication with Relevant Stakeholders

  • Facilitate communication among government counterparts, NRPB/WB and private sector stakeholders
  • Provide contributions to press releases related to project activities, as needed
  • Consolidate and track feedback and recommendations from stakeholders and develop response matrices with the Policy Consultant.
  • Ensure timely reporting, briefing notes, and updates to the Ministry of Finance and other governing bodies as required.

Reporting and Monitoring and Evaluation

  • Monitor Policy Consultant’s deliverables and work quality, ensuring it adheres to the TOR, timelines and quality standards.
  • Prepare and submit progress reports to relevant stakeholders where applicable (MinTEATT/ ETT, Ministry of Finance World Bank)
  • Submit necessary reports on delays and mitigation strategies/ corrective actions to relevant stakeholders (MinTEATT/ETT, Ministry of Finance, World Bank).
  • With the applicable PIUs (MoF, NRPB) provide inputs to address any complaints submitted through the projects’ Grievance Redress Mechanism (https://nrpbsxm.org/complaints-procedure)
  • Prepare and provide input on SPEAR and Institutional strengthening project required reports.

Consultant Oversight and Quality Management

  • Review Policy Consultant’s inception reports, providing feedback and ensuring alignment with project objectives and MinTEATT/ETT priorities.
  • Review all Annotated Policy Outlines (MSME policy, REP, Investment & Diversification Policy, Beach & Vending Policy), coordinating feedback from MinTEATT and ensuring coherence across the four policies.
  • Review all annotated outlines for the MSME institutional strengthening program support documents to assess quality, identify gaps and ensure that they meet technical and operational standards
  • Conduct quality checks of all policy documents ensuring alignment with Governing Program and National Development Plans (and other applicable documents).
  • Facilitate review and approval processes for all consultant deliverables, coordinating feedback from the  Department Head of ETT, Secretary General, Minister TEATT and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Ensure deliverables submitted are timely and are of professional standard, and incorporate stakeholders input where necessary.
  • Work with the Policy Consultant to assess stakeholder feedback, address identified gaps and incorporate feedback agreed upon by TEATT into the final documents and capacity-building materials. Document the reasons for not incorporating substantive stakeholder comments
  • Verify that consultants’ invoices are supported by appropriate reports, deliverables documentation and evidence of work completed.  

Any other tasks related to the function that will ensure successful completion of the SPEAR Project policy development and the Institutional Strengthening components

 

  • Final Project Completion Report- Documentation of the project including activities, results achieved, challenges, lessons learned and recommendations for implementation and future work.
  • Transition report- Handover documentation including all relevant information for smooth transition and continued implementation.
  • Budget execution reports, stakeholder coordination logs
  • Policy Documents (4),
  • MSME Institutional Strengthening documents (3),

Contract Arrangements and Reporting

The contract duration will be twelve (12) months, from contract signing, with the possibility to extend until June 2028. The successful candidate is expected to reside in Sint Maarten/Saint Martin to support the effective organization and execution of the work and ensure continuous engagement with public sector agencies and local stakeholders.

The Project Manager will report to the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Finance for project administration, financial management and compliance and work in close collaboration with the Department of Economic Transportation and Telecommunication (ETT) for substantive technical oversight, policy direction and review of deliverables

Qualifications and Experience

Minimum Requirements

  • At least a bachelor’s degree in public policy, economics, business administration, project management, or another relevant field.
  • At least 5 years of experience in project management, preferably in the public sector or development projects.
  • Demonstrated skills in results-based project planning, monitoring, and management.
  • Experience coordinating multi-stakeholder processes and facilitating consultation workshops.
  • Prior experience working in Sint Maarten or the Caribbean region.

 

Preferred Requirements

  • A master’s degree in a relevant field is a plus.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent.
  • Experience with MSME development, private sector development, or economic policy projects is a plus.
  • Proficiency in Dutch (spoken and written) is a plus.

 

General Competencies

  • Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities simultaneously.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to anticipate challenges and develop effective solutions.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including report writing, presentation, and facilitation abilities.
  • Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills, with demonstrated ability to build relationships and coordinate across diverse groups.
  • Computer literate with high proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project) and project management software.

 

[1]   Which is supporting implementation of the Enterprise Support Project (ESP), funded by the Sint Maarten Recovery and Resilience Trust Fund. ESP’s objective is to support the recovery of and increase resilience of existing and new micro, small, and medium sized enterprises in Sint Maarten.

 

[2]   The Enterprise Survey (ES) is a nationally representative firm-level survey with top managers and owners of businesses in over 160 economies (to reach 180 in upcoming years) that measures businesses’ major constraints, performance (including job creation), and characteristics including innovation and technology, market linkages, access to finance, infrastructure, and more. ES’s comprehensive data and analytical reports enable easy comparisons across economies and time.

 

Deadline for submitting Expressions of Interest Monday, November 30, 2026 by 17h00 to:

Mr. Shervin Frederick,  Email address:  Shervin.Frederick@sintmaartengov.org     AND

Mrs. Avril Isaac,            Email address:  Avril.Isaac@sintmaartengov.org

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

Syrian Arab Republic

Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516)

Grant No.: E6410-SY

Assignment Title: Technical Lead for the Public Procurement Reform Sub-Component (Sub-Component 2.2)

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): SY-MOF-547078-CS-INDV

The Ministry of Finance of the Syrian Arab Republic (the “Employer”) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the services of a Technical Lead for the Public Procurement Reform Sub-Component (Sub-Component 2.2), who will provide high-level strategic leadership and policy direction to the Government of Syria in the design, sequencing, and oversight of the public procurement reform program under the Project, with a view to establishing a modern, transparent, and efficient procurement system aligned with international best practices.

The Technical Lead will lead and coordinate implementation of the procurement reform activities under Sub-Component 2.2 - the new public procurement legal and regulatory framework (replacing the Uniform System of Contracts Law No. 51 (2004)), standard bidding documents, the Single Procurement Portal (SPP), an independent procurement complaints and review system, and the national procurement professionalization and capacity-development program, advising the Ministry of Finance and relevant stakeholders, coordinating with government entities, development partners and the World Bank Task Team, overseeing implementation progress and risk management, and leading the results framework for procurement reform, including key performance indicators and milestones. The assignment will be for an initial period of one (1) year, with the possibility of extension based on satisfactory performance and project requirements (the contract may be extended to cover the full duration of the Project).

The Technical Lead will work under the overall guidance of the Project Coordinator and the Public Financial Management Reform Coordinating Unit (PFMRCU) within the Ministry of Finance, and will closely coordinate with relevant government entities, the Syria External Assistance Fiduciary Section (SEAFS) and the World Bank Task Team.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The Ministry of Finance (through the Public Financial Management Reform Coordinating Unit - PFMRCU) now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). Firms' staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process.

The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

  1. postgraduate qualifications in procurement, law, public administration, engineering, economics, or a related field, and at least ten (10) years of relevant professional management-focused experience;
  2. proven successful experience in leading and managing technical assistance projects financed by international donors;
  3. experience in public procurement, including demonstrated experience in procurement reform, development of legal and regulatory frameworks, and institutional strengthening (highly desirable);
  4. advanced leadership skills in organizational change and development, with the ability to introduce critical reforms in complex organizational and contextual structures, including in Fragile and Conflict-affected Situations (FCS);
  5. proven experience in coordinating, cooperating and negotiating with high-level government officials, donor partners and multiple local stakeholders; and
  6. fluency in Arabic and English.

 

The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers [insert correct title and date of applicable Regulations edition as per the financing agreement] (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the following email address: syriapfmprocurement@gmail.com by 5PM on 30 November 2026 Damascus time.

 

Attn: Project Coordinator

Ministry of Finance

Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project

Joul Jammal Street, P.O. Box 13136

Damascus, Syrian Arab Republic

E-mail: syriapfmprocurement@gmail.com

 

 

=======================================================================

 

Terms of Reference (TOR)

Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516)

Technical Lead for the Public Procurement Reform Sub-Component

 

Project Background

  1. Syria is making progress in its transition towards stabilization, recovery, and reintegration, while continuing to face major challenges after 14 years of conflict. More than one year after the December 2024 political transition, the new Syrian government under the leadership of President Al-Sharaa has maintained overall political stability. Modest economic growth is projected for 2025 and 2026, and Syria has benefitted from the lifting of major economic sanctions and renewed participation in international financial systems and investment discussions. At the same time, the security situation remains fragile, with occasional outbreaks of violence, and the country faces massive development challenges and continued humanitarian needs. Continued international engagement and financing will be critical to support Syria in its post-conflict transition. 
  2. Sound management of public funds and transparency about their use are prerequisites for the Syrian state to gain the trust of its citizens and the international community as it seeks to mobilize resources and deliver services to the population. Fourteen years of conflict and economic mismanagement have weakened the capacity and legitimacy of Syria’s state institutions. A disciplined and transparent approach to public financial management (PFM) will be a critical foundation for Syria’s path to recovery and development. The Ministry of Finance has identified support for PFM reforms as a priority, highlighting the immediate need to update the relevant legal framework, rebuild human capital for core government functions, advance digitalization, and establish accountability and transparency. Sound management of public funds will also be needed to mobilize external assistance for the country’s massive reconstruction needs, with expectations from the international community of adequate oversight of reconstruction investments, payroll, and the flow of funds to provide these resource flows.
  3. The Syrian Arab Republic has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Syria Public Financial Management Capacity Strengthening Project (P512516), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of the financing for services of a Technical Lead for the Public Procurement Reform Sub-Component. The project components/sub-components are shown in Table 1. Full details are available in the Project Appraisal Document (PAD).

Table 1: Summary of project components/sub-components

 

  1. Within this context, Component 2 of the Project focuses on improving the efficiency and effectiveness of essential PFM and procurement functions. A key sub-component (Sub-component 2.2) is dedicated to public procurement reform, which aims to establish a modern, transparent, and efficient procurement system aligned with good international practices. This includes the development of a new procurement legal framework, introduction of standard bidding documents, establishment of a Single Procurement Portal (SPP), strengthening of complaint handling mechanisms, and development of procurement professionalization programs.
  2. The current procurement system, governed by the Uniform System of Contracts Law No. 51 (2004), presents several structural gaps and limitations, including weaknesses in competition, transparency, complaints review, and the absence of modern e-procurement systems.

 

Objective of the Assignment

  1. The objective of this assignment is to provide high-level strategic leadership and policy direction to the Government of Syria in the design, sequencing, and oversight of the public procurement reform program under the Project, with a view to establishing a modern, transparent, and efficient procurement system aligned with international best practices.

The Technical Lead will guide the reform agenda at the institutional and policy level, ensure coherence across reform pillars, and support sustainable capacity development and ownership by government institutions.

Tasks and Responsibilities

  1. The Technical Lead for Public Procurement Reform Component will be responsible for leading and coordinating the implementation of the public procurement reform activities under the Project and providing advisory support to the Ministry of Finance and relevant stakeholders.

In particular, the Lead will undertake the following tasks:

  1. Strategic Leadership and Reform Direction:
  • Provide overall vision, leadership, and strategic direction for the public procurement reform program, ensuring alignment with national priorities and international good practices.
  • Define and guide the sequencing and prioritization of reform initiatives, taking into account institutional readiness and the FCV context.
  • Advise senior government leadership on policy options, reform trade-offs, and implementation risks.

 

  1. Procurement Legal and Regulatory Reform:
  • Lead the strategic design and oversight of the new public procurement legal and regulatory framework, ensuring coherence, applicability, and sustainability.
  • Oversee the work of technical teams responsible for drafting legislation and regulations and ensure quality assurance and policy consistency.
  • Facilitate high-level consultations and consensus-building among key stakeholders to support adoption of the reform framework.

 

  1. Digital Transformation and System Modernization
  • Provide strategic guidance on the development and implementation of the Single Procurement Portal (SPP) as a cornerstone for transparency and efficiency.
  • Ensure that digital solutions are aligned with broader public financial management systems and government digital strategies.
  • Oversee high-level design decisions to ensure sustainability, interoperability, and scalability of systems.

 

  1. Complaint Handling and Oversight Mechanisms:
  • Lead the strategic design of an independent and credible procurement complaints and review system.
  • Ensure that oversight mechanisms are aligned with principles of fairness, transparency, and due process, and are institutionally sustainable.

 

  1. Capacity Development and Professionalization Strategy
  • Provide strategic guidance on the development of a national procurement professionalization framework, including certification pathways and institutional arrangements.
  • Oversee the design of capacity development programs to ensure long-term institutional strengthening, rather than short-term training delivery.
  • Promote a culture of professionalism and ethical standards in the procurement function across government.

 

  1. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination
  • Act as a key interlocutor with senior government officials, development partners, and other stakeholders on procurement reform matters.
  • Ensure effective coordination across ministries, agencies, and donor-supported initiatives to avoid fragmentation and duplication.
  • Support the Government in articulating and communicating the reform agenda to build broad-based ownership.

 

  1.  Implementation Oversight and Risk Management
  • Provide strategic oversight of implementation progress, ensuring that reform activities remain aligned with objectives and timelines.
  • Identify key implementation risks and bottlenecks and advise on mitigation measures at the policy and institutional levels.
  • Guide pilot initiatives and scale-up decisions from a strategic perspective.
