REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-2.6--4-R – Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)

 

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

GPE TF0D0613

 

Assignment Title: Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)

No. LEARN-2.6--4-R

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of this assignment is to support the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) in aligning budget planning and public financial management processes with the strategic priorities of the education sector and the implementation of flagship national programmes and reforms. In particular, the assignment will contribute to the effective planning, prioritisation, financing, and coordination of key initiatives. The Consultant will support the development of effective planning and resource allocation approaches aimed at improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and transparency of public expenditure, strengthening evidence-based decision-making, and ensuring better alignment between strategic objectives, reform implementation, and available financial resources.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest. The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time December 01, 2026.

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

for Consulting Services (Individual Consultant)

Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert (Budget Planning)

Contract No. LEARN-2.6-CC-4-R

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project

GPE TF0D0613

I. Background

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the “New Ukrainian School” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The LEARN objectives are: (i) to improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system. The total LEARN financing amounts to US$737 mln  provides a combination of the World Bank financing instruments: Program for Results (PforR) – US$675.9 mln and Investment Project Financing (IPF) – US$61.1 mln.

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million. On June 9, 2026, a Loan Agreement (Third Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) was signed between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (Loan No. K019-UA) in the amount of $286 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

II. Objective

The objective of this assignment is to support the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) in aligning budget planning and public financial management processes with the strategic priorities of the education sector and the implementation of flagship national programmes and reforms. In particular, the assignment will contribute to the effective planning, prioritisation, financing, and coordination of key initiatives. The Consultant will support the development of effective planning and resource allocation approaches aimed at improving the efficiency, effectiveness, and transparency of public expenditure, strengthening evidence-based decision-making, and ensuring better alignment between strategic objectives, reform implementation, and available financial resources.

III. Scope of services

The Consultant shall provide the following services, including but not limited to:

  • Analyze the current system of budgetary and strategic planning within the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES), including the application of the program-based budgeting approach;
  • Analyze the alignment of budget programs with strategic objectives and national policy priorities in the education and science sector;
  • Develop recommendations for aligning strategic documents (strategies, operational plans) with MoES budget programs;
  • Ensure integration of strategic objectives and priorities into the budget process (including preparation of budget requests, budget program passports, and reporting);
  • Contribute to the improvement of the structure of budget programs, performance indicators, and effectiveness metrics;
  • Support medium-term budget planning in line with strategic documents;
  • Provide methodological support on the application of the program-based budgeting approach within MoES;
  • Coordinate with the Ministry of Finance of Ukraine on budget planning and alignment of budget programs;
  • Provide methodological and analytical support for public expenditure reviews in relevant MoES sectors;
  • Develop proposals for implementing recommendations from expenditure reviews and ensure their incorporation into future budget planning cycles;
  • Support the implementation of results-based management approaches in the budget process;
  • Assess the effectiveness of MoES budget programs;
  • Prepare analytical materials on the efficiency of public expenditure and achievement of results.

Expected Deliverables:

  • Regular reports on the progress of aligning budgetary and strategic planning;
  • Analytical notes on the effectiveness of budget programs and their alignment with strategic objectives;
  • Proposals for improving the MoES budget process:

consulting and practical support to the Ministry of Education and Science in implementing results-oriented management approaches;

conducting analysis and assessment of the efficiency and effectiveness of budget programs of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine;

  • Analyze the implementation of previously provided recommendations and their impact on MoES budget indicators in the medium term, including collection and systematization of recommendations provided by the Accounting Chamber, the State Audit Service, and expenditure reviews conducted during the previous three years, as well as assessment of their implementation status.

 

IV. Reporting

The Consultant shall report to the Project Coordinator/Project Co-Coordinator and work in coordination with the Deputy Ministers of Education and Science of Ukraine, relevant MoES directorates, and project managers involved in the implementation of Project activities. On operational matters, the Consultant shall cooperate with the Head of the World Bank Operations Management Team.

The Consultant shall submit monthly reports to Project coordinator / Project Co-coordinator in hard copy. The reports shall include a description of services provided during the reporting period.

 

V. Provided resources

 

MoES shall provide the Consultant with the information necessary to carry out his/her assignment in a timely manner. MoES may provide the Consultant with a workplace, including necessary equipment to carry out his/her functions (e.g. PC, communications and office equipment).

 

VI.  Qualification requirements

 

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

 

  • Master’s degree or higher in finance, economics, accounting, or taxation;
  • At least 5 years of professional experience in public financial management or related areas;
  • Experience in strategic planning and alignment of budget programmes with sectoral policies.
  • Fluency in Ukrainian;
  • Proficiency in English at a minimum level of B1.

 

Desirable skills and qualifications:

  • Experience in effective communication among different government authorities;
  • Experience working with reforms or policies in the education and/or science sector;
  • Skills in using analytical tools and basic data visualization tools;
  • Experience in drafting regulatory/legal acts;

 

VII.  Period and location of employment

The Consultant shall provide his/her services until October 30, 2027. The contract may be extended subject to satisfactory performance and mutual agreement between the Consultant and the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine during the Project financing period.

The Consultant is expected to provide services under this Agreement on an ongoing basis throughout its term at a level of engagement equivalent to full-time employment, to the extent necessary to properly perform the tasks specified in the Terms of Reference.

The Consultant shall provide services primarily in Kyiv, Ukraine, and may take business trips to other regions of Ukraine to support implementation of the Project.

The Consultant is expected to be able to provide services remotely, but at the MOES request must arrive and/or provide services at the MOES premises as soon as possible.

VIII. Application package

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org, maryna.chubenko@mon.gov.ua indicating the email subject: «LEARN-2.6-CC-4-R: Selection of the Cross-Functional Strategy and Alignment Expert 2 (Budget Planning): [NAME]».

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time December 01, 2026.

If the candidate fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the candidate’s application.

data.title: Consulting firm to design, develop, deploy and support the Data Controllers & Processors Registration and Complaint Management Portal (DRC Portal) for the Data Protection Authority (DPA)

data.notice_text:
COUNTRY:                                       Federal Republic of Somalia

NAME OF PROJECT:                    Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP)  

PROJECT ID:                                    P176181         

Assignment Title:                          Consulting Firm to Design, Develop, Deploy and Support the Data Controllers & Processors Registration and Complaint Management Portal (DRC Portal) for the Data Protection Authority (DPA)

Reference No.:                                 SO-MOCT-FGS-581535-CS-CQS

Place of assignment:                   Mogadishu, Somalia

Submission Date:                         December 1, 2026, 2.00pm (local time, Mogadishu, Somalia)

The Federal Republic of Somalia has received a grant from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Digital Integration Project (EA-RDIP), and the Ministry of Communications and Technology intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) are required to be undertaken by an external consulting firm supporting the client, Ministry of Communications and Technology (MoCT), FGS, on behalf of the beneficiary, the Data Protection Authority (DPA), to carry out the implementation of “Design, Development, Deployment and Support of the Data Controllers & Processors Registration and Complaint Management Portal (DRC Portal)”. The assignment aims to establish a centralized, secure, scalable and integrated regulatory information system that enables the DPA to register, manage and regulate data controllers and data processors under the Somalia Data Protection Act No. 005 of 2023. The portal will automate registration, certification, fee payment, compliance, data breach notification and complaint handling workflows; provide secure, user-friendly interfaces for data controllers, data processors and the public; centralize the management of certificates, entities, users, breaches, payments and financial transactions; and generate real-time dashboards and compliance and operational reports. The consulting firm will undertake all the tasks required for the assignment, including system design and technical requirements, development, testing, deployment, training, and post-deployment support and maintenance. The core design, development and rollout are expected to be completed within eighteen (18) weeks, followed by twenty-four (24) weeks of post-deployment support, for a total engagement period of forty-two (42) weeks from contract effectiveness.

The Ministry of Communications and Technology now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.).

The short-listing criteria are as follows:

  1. Core business of the firm and at least seven (7) years of demonstrated experience in the design, development, implementation and support of integrated information management systems or systems of similar scope and complexity, with evidence of the company registration certificate, business license or operational permit, and providing company profile indicating services offered and years in operation.
  2. The firm should demonstrate successful completion of at least three (3) comparable ICT or digital transformation assignments, preferably involving government institutions or regulatory bodies. Proven experience in systems architecture, software development, database management, API development, systems integration and web-based application development, and demonstrated knowledge and experience in data protection, privacy, cybersecurity, information security and secure data handling, is required.
  3. Demonstrate experience of relevant services implemented in Somalia, or in Africa, low-income, fragile/conflict-affected or institutionally complex environments similar to that of Somalia, including the capacity to provide post-deployment support and maintenance; and
  4. The technical and managerial organization of the firm. (Provide only with the structure of the Firm organization) Do not provide CVs of staff. Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services dated July 2016 and revised in November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023, (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint venture and/ or a Sub consultancy. In case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.  

Interested Consultant may obtain further information in a written communication to the address below during office hours from 9.00am to 4.00pm Mogadishu time (Excluding public holidays).

data.notice_text:
INVITACIÓN A PRESENTAR EXPRESIONES DE INTERÉS

República de El Salvador

Proyecto: “Proyecto Crecer y Aprender Juntos: Desarrollo Integral de la Primera Infancia en El Salvador

Convenio de Préstamo No. BIRF No. 9067-SV

Solicitud de Expresiones de Interés 

 

SBCC No. SBCC 39/2026 MINEDUCYT-BIRF

 

”DISEÑO E IMPLEMENTACIÓN DE UN CURSO ESPECIALIZADO CON METODOLOGÍA DE TALLERES PARA FORMADORES DE FORMADORES DE PRIMERA INFANCIA DE EDUCACIÓN SUPERIOR”
 

1. El Gobierno de la República de El Salvador ha recibido un préstamo del Banco Internacional de Reconstrucción y Fomento (BIRF), Convenio de Préstamo N° BIRF 9067-SV, para financiar el costo del Proyecto “Crecer y Aprender Juntos: Desarrollo Integral de la Primera Infancia en El Salvador” y se propone utilizar parte de los fondos para efectuar los pagos bajo el contrato de esta consultoría.

2. El Ministerio de Educación, Ciencia y Tecnología (ejecutor de dicho préstamo), a través de la Dirección de Compras Públicas (DCP), invita a firmas consultoras elegibles (“Consultores”), a indicar su interés en proporcionar los servicios de la ”DISEÑO E IMPLEMENTACIÓN DE UN CURSO ESPECIALIZADO CON METODOLOGÍA DE TALLERES PARA FORMADORES DE FORMADORES DE PRIMERA INFANCIA DE EDUCACIÓN SUPERIOR”, cuyo plazo de ejecución es de 180 días calendarios. Los consultores interesados deberán proporcionar información que indique que están cualificados para suministrar los servicios (folletos, descripción de trabajos similares, experiencia en condiciones similares, disponibilidad de personal que tenga los conocimientos pertinentes, etc.). Los consultores se podrán asociar con el fin de mejorar sus calificaciones. 

3. Los Términos de Referencia de la consultoría, se encuentran descritos en el Anexo 1, y pueden consultarse en el siguiente enlace: https://goo.su/5GRzN. Asimismo, pueden obtenerse de forma gratuita, por cualquiera de los procedimientos que se detallan a continuación:

a. Presentarse a la Dirección de Compras Públicas, Ministerio de Educación, Ciencia y Tecnología, Plan Maestro Centro de Gobierno, Edificio A-1 Segundo Nivel, San Salvador, El Salvador, teléfono: 2592-3038, los días hábiles a partir del 17 de noviembre al 01 de diciembre de 2026, en horario de 7:30 a. a 12:00 m. y de 13:00 a 15:30 horas (hora El Salvador GMT-6). 

b. Ingresar al sitio web del Ministerio de Educación, Ciencia y Tecnología: https//www.mined.gob.sv en la sección AVISOS o en el sitio electrónico de compras públicas. www.comprasal.gob.sv, para la descarga gratuita del documento, durante el período comprendido del 17 de noviembre de 2026, durante las 24 horas y hasta las 15.30 hora (Hora El Salvador GMT-6) del 01 de diciembre de 2026.
 

4. Las firmas consultoras interesadas deberán proporcionar información y documentación (Currículum de la firma y Constancias de trabajos realizados) que demuestren que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia pertinente para realizar esta Consultoría. Los criterios para la preselección son los siguientes:

Criterio de evaluación

Experiencia General de la Firma

1. Firma consultora con experiencia en proyectos de diseño curricular e instruccional, desarrollo de formaciones presenciales y virtuales de formación de formadores o programas formativos dirigidos a docentes como: cursos, diplomados, especializaciones o programas de formación. La gestión logística y despliegue territorial en la implementación de procesos formativos presenciales a nivel zonal o de país. 

Experiencia Específica de la Firma 

1. Experiencia comprobable a través de portafolio digital en el diseño curricular e instruccional, diseño de contenidos y materiales como: Objetos Virtuales de Aprendizaje (OVA), videos, separatas o folletos, presentaciones, piezas gráficas, infografías, recursos de gamificación, entre otros.

2. Experiencia comprobable en la implementación de proyectos formativos en modalidad presencial dirigidos a formadores de formadores de Instituciones de Educación Superior como: cursos, diplomados, especializaciones o programas de formación. 

3. Experiencia comprobable en el diseño y montaje de entornos virtuales de aprendizaje, sites web o plataformas para la gestión de recursos educativos, con énfasis en usabilidad, accesibilidad y experiencia de usuario para adultos.

Para la conformación de la lista corta, se seleccionarán a las firmas que acrediten la mayor experiencia en los servicios requeridos, mediante contratos, constancias, órdenes de compra, certificaciones, referencias u otros medios probatorios. Esto hasta alcanzar el mínimo o máximo de firmas consultoras requeridas en el numeral 7.
 

5. Este proceso se efectuará en el marco de la modalidad expresión de interés, Selección Basada en Calidad y Costo (SBCC) detallada en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, sexta edición (Febrero de 2025.), y está abierta a todos los interesados de países elegibles, según se definen en dichos lineamientos. Adicionalmente, se solicita a los interesados referirse al numeral 3.14, de la Sección III. Gobernanza, relativo al Conflicto de Intereses, que textualmente establece lo siguiente: “El Banco exige que las empresas o los individuos que participan en las adquisiciones correspondientes a operaciones de financiamiento para proyectos de inversión no tengan conflictos de interés” y a los numerales 3.16 y 3.17, que establecen las referidas regulaciones en materia de conflicto de interés para los Servicios de Consultoría.

6. Las firmas consultoras (Consultores) pueden conformar asociaciones temporales con otras empresas nacionales o extranjeras para mejorar sus calificaciones y capacidades y pueden ser de largo plazo (independientes de un proceso de adquisición en particular) o conformarse para participar en un proceso de adquisición específico, pero deberán indicarlo claramente a través de documento impreso. (Ver numeral 5.38 de las referidas regulaciones).

7. Del conjunto de firmas que hayan presentado expresión de interés, se conformará una lista corta de entre 5 y 8 las empresas elegibles entre las que se postulen y se les invita a presentar sus propuestas, para elegir a la firma ganadora se tendrá en cuenta el Método “Selección Basada en Calidad y Costos (SBCC)”, establecido en las Regulaciones de Adquisiciones para Prestatarios en Proyectos de Inversión del Banco Mundial, sexta edición (febrero de 2025.).

8. Las firmas interesadas pueden obtener información adicional sobre este proceso solicitándola, hasta el día 23 de noviembre de 2026, dirigidas a la Arquitecta Carolina Astrid Ortiz Jiménez, Coordinadora para Adquisiciones de la DCP-BIRF, en horario de 7:30 a las 12:00 horas y de 13:00 a 15:30 horas (Hora El Salvador GMT-6) en la dirección o correo electrónico detallados en el numeral 10.  

9. Asimismo, se les informa que se realizará una reunión virtual informativa con el objetivo de ampliar el alcance o alguna inquietud de los ofertantes. Esta reunión se llevará a cabo el día 20 de noviembre de 2026, de las 9:00 a 10:00 horas (hora de El Salvador), por medio de este link: meet.google.com/itp-vxzf-rba o marcar el:(SV) +503 2113 9520 PIN:  286 882 122 6655#. El documento cual será enviado de forma editable a las firmas que lo soliciten por medio del siguiente correo electrónico: christian.villalta@mined.gob.sv

10. Las expresiones de interés deberán hacerse llegar por escrito a más tardar a las 15:30 horas (Hora El Salvador GMT-6) del día 01 de diciembre de 2026, a la siguiente dirección: Ministerio de Educación, Ciencia y Tecnología, Dirección de Compras Públicas, Plan Maestro, Centro de Gobierno, Edificio A-1, Segundo Nivel, San Salvador, El Salvador, Centro América Dirigidos  Licenciada María Guadalupe Moran de Albergue, o vía correo electrónico christian.villalta@mined.gob.sv  con copia a carolina.ortiz@mined.gob.sv

11. Todos los documentos deberán estar escritos en el idioma Castellano. En caso los instrumentos estén redactados en idioma extranjero, se podrán presentar traducciones simples.

12. Las Firmas Consultoras deberán remitir la siguiente documentación:

a. Carta de Expresión de Interés (según modelo del Anexo 2).

b. Información general de la firma (según modelo del Anexo 3).

f. Fotocopia simple de contratos, constancias que indiquen la experiencia de la firma.

g. Fotocopia simple del Documento constitutivo de la empresa.

h. Fotocopia simple del Documento de Identidad de la persona que funge como Representante Legal. 

i. Fotocopia simple de la Credencial de Elección del Representante Legal o su equivalente en el país de origen.

j. Carta compromiso anticorrupción para proveedores y contratistas (socios de negocios) [ISO 37001:2025 SGA 8.5] (Anexo 6)

 

Los documentos antes mencionados, pueden ser consultados en el siguiente enlace: https://goo.su/5GRzN 

 

San Salvador, 17 de noviembre de 2026

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – SELECTION OF INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS)

 

Republic of Uzbekistan

Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project

Credit No.: 7425-UZ

 

Assignment Title: AI and Technology Ecosystem Adviser – International Individual Consultant

Reference No.: UZ-DIP-582910-CS-INDV

 

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the International Development Association toward the cost of the Uzbekistan Digital Inclusion Project. “Administration of Technology Park of Software and IT” LLC (IT Park), as the Implementing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds to engage an individual consultant as AI and Technology Ecosystem Adviser to the CEO of IT Park Uzbekistan, under Subcomponent 1.1 of the Project.

Under Subcomponent 1.1, the Project supports IT Park Uzbekistan’s AI and technology ecosystem agenda, including the implementation of AI strategy, priority AI initiatives, international technology partnerships and the commercialization of innovations, in line with Uzbekistan’s Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies until 2030.

The Adviser will support the CEO of IT Park in prioritising, designing and delivering
AI ecosystem initiatives, partnerships and programmes, and in strengthening IT Park’s internal capacity to manage its AI agenda. Results are expected to contribute to the Project Development Objective through the creation of digital jobs, growth of AI-enabled IT services exports and inclusion of women, youth, persons with disabilities and the regions.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include, but are not limited to:

  • assessment of existing AI initiatives, capabilities and AI-readiness, and recommendation of priorities for a 12-month AI ecosystem work plan;
  • advice on strategic AI-related decisions, including decision papers on proposed AI programmes, centres, partnerships and investment initiatives;
  • identification and engagement of international technology partners, and support for cooperation proposals and authorised negotiations;
  • support for applied AI initiatives and the commercialisation of innovations developed by local startups and IT Park residents;
  • advice on mechanisms to attract AI talent and strengthen IT Park’s institutional capacity, including working sessions for IT Park staff;
  • support to the CEO across IT Park’s strategic directions (startups and venture investment; export and international positioning; Uzbekistan as a regional technology hub; support to IT Park residents and their AI adaptation; and R&D, data and robotics).

The assignment is proposed for a period of 12 months. The Adviser will work in a hybrid format, under a time-based contract.

To obtain the Terms of Reference for the assignment, please send your request to the following e-mail address: udip@it-park.uz.

“Administration of Technology Park of Software and IT” LLC now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services: a curriculum vitae in the English language, and contact details of references.

The evaluation criteria are:

1) General Qualifications

  • University degree in technology, engineering, economics, management or a related field;
  • Fluent professional English;
  • Availability to work in person in Tashkent, Uzbekistan for at least 5 working days per month throughout the assignment.

2) Professional Experience

  • At least 8 years of experience in technology businesses, innovation, digital transformation or technology ecosystem development, including at least 5 years in leadership or strategic roles;
  • At least 3 years of substantive experience in managing AI projects or programmes, and at least one completed AI initiative with verifiable results and a clearly identified personal contribution;
  • Demonstrated experience in advising senior decision-makers, developing programmes involving companies, startups, universities, investors and public institutions, and supporting technologies through pilots, deployment, licensing, investment or entry into overseas markets;
  • Experience in international technology projects, negotiations with organisational leaders and cooperation with government bodies or development institutions;
  • Active professional relationships with AI companies, technology centres, customers and investors, supported by examples of collaboration.

3) Advantages

  • Russian or Uzbek proficiency;
  • Experience with recognised technology clusters or AI centres;
  • Experience working on MDB-financed projects (e.g., World Bank, ADB);
  • Experience in developing or transition economies, preferably in Central Asia/CIS, including AI ecosystem or policy development;
  • Knowledge of responsible AI and data governance frameworks.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Fifth Edition, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest, and to paragraph 3.21 on eligibility.

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection procedures set out in the Procurement Regulations, based on an evaluation of qualifications and experience against the criteria above and of the brief approach to the assignment. The three top-ranked candidates will be invited to an interview (in person or online) with the participation of the CEO of IT Park.

Assignment Title: ECPE Model Diversification Expert

Reference No. LEARN-IC-ECEDO-05-R

In 2024, Ukraine, together with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank), signed the agreements for the Operation “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as LEARN or the Operation).

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The Operation focuses on supporting the priorities “1. Early Childhood and Preschool Education” and “2. Reform of the New Ukrainian School” stipulated in the Strategic Plan.

The objective of this assignment is to support hromadas during the first phase of the implementation of the “First Steps Forward” program in selecting and developing diversified service delivery models in the field of preschool education (ECE) that best respond to local needs. The Expert will ensure that the diversified service delivery models are feasible for implementation, comply with national legislation, are child-centered, and are suitable for further scaling at the national level. The Expert will provide support to hromadas in identifying appropriate options for diversification of preschool education services, as well as ensure technical guidance on service delivery models and develop recommendations for their practical application.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 November 17, 2026

The Government of Montenegro (the Recipient) has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development – ‘’World Bank’’ toward the costs for implementation of ‘Waste Management Reform Project (WMRP), (the Project)’’. The Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development, and Northern Region Development -MESDNRD (the Client) as the lead implementing agency for the project, intends to apply part of these proceeds to the payments for Consulting services.

The Waste Management Reform Project (WMRP) aims to enhance the Country’s waste management capacity and sector performance, supporting Montenegro’s progress toward EU accession. The objective of the WMRP project adopts an integrated approach through three main components (i) strengthen institutional capacity for solid waste management, (ii) improve the performance of solid waste services in selected municipalities, and (iii) enhance environmental conditions at targeted waste disposal site. The Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development, and Northern Region Development (MESDNRD) (the “Client”) is seeking to engage an experienced and qualified Consultancy firm (the “Consultant”) to support of the Montenegro Waste Management Reform Project (the “Project”).

The objective of this particular assignment is to establish a statistically robust, nationally representative and seasonally differentiated baseline on the quantity and composition of municipal waste generated in Montenegro, including a technically defensible basis for estimating plastic packaging waste contained in municipal waste and for supporting future Chapter 33 reporting and projections while the Scope of services and deliverables are clearly defined within the ToR.

The (MESDNRD) through the Technical Service Unit (TSU) now invites eligible Consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consult-firm (Legal entity) should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services in subject, with demonstrated experience in waste composition studies, statistical sampling and analysis, and waste management data assessment. The Consultant will work closely with relevant stakeholders ensuring compliance with Montenegro’s relevant policies, EU regulations, and international best practices.

* It is anticipated that the Consultant should complete the work over a maximum duration of 10 months.

The qualification and evaluation criteria are:

The Consultant (Firm) should meet the following qualification criteria:

1. General experience: At least five (5) years of professional experience in waste management studies, waste characterization, waste data analysis or related environmental consulting services ---------------------------15.

2. Relevant assignment experience: Successful completion of at least two (2) comparable assignments within the last seven (7) years involving municipal waste composition analysis, waste characterization studies or statistically representative waste sampling and analysis –--------------------------------------------------------- 40.

 

3. Statistical and methodological capacity: Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing statistically representative sampling methodologies, including data processing, statistical analysis and preparation of analytical reports ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------20.

4.. Waste packaging and EU reporting experience: Demonstrated experience in at least one assignment involving packaging waste data, recycling statistics, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) systems or EU waste reporting requirements -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------15.

5. Field implementation capacity: Demonstrated experience in organizing and supervising field sampling campaigns, waste sorting operations and associated quality assurance and quality control procedures----10.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Total Scores 100

Experience in EU Member States, EU candidate countries or Western Balkan countries shall be considered an advantage but shall not constitute a mandatory eligibility requirement. Documented experience in Chapter 33 plastic own resource data or EU plastic-packaging waste calculation and reporting, and in applying SWA-Tool or an equivalent statistically justified waste composition methodology, shall also be considered an advantage.

The Consultant may demonstrate compliance with the above requirements through the combined experience of the members of a joint venture, where applicable

It is expected that the interested Consultant’s company within the submitted ‘’EoI’’ shall prepare and present a table listing (reference list) which will provide the following information: Contracting authority/client data and contact information to whom the consultancy service was performed, (contract-project detailed description, contract value for performed services and contract implementation period). (name, e-mail, phone numbers for verification purposes).  The Consultant firm may also submit other documents and which are not listed above in order to justify general qualifications and qualifications relevant to the assignment it considers relevant, such us indicative list of the key staff/key personnel (team) that is generally available for this kind of work.

*CVs or biodata for Key Expert’s- (staff) are not required and will not be evaluated at this stage.

Consultants may associate to enhance their qualifications. The associations should clearly indicate the form of the association (Joint-venture, Consortium, sub-consultancy; member in charge; other member/s and or sub- consultants). Joint ventures should submit letter/confirmation, indicating their intent to form a joint venture if awarded the contract and shall provide the above-mentioned information for each member of the joint venture. *Consultant may only submit one expression of interest. If a consultant submits or participates in more than one Expression of Interest, such expression will be disqualified. However, sub-consultants, including individual experts, may participate in more than one expression of interest only in the capacity of sub-consultants.  Qualifications and experience of the sub-consultants will not be considered for evaluation purposes.

The objective of the Project is to improve the delivery of digitally-enabled public services and to enhance the digital skills of the population. The Project development objective is to expand access to and usage of selected digital public services and enhance digital skills of the population. The project consists of two main components designed to leverage digital technologies for both social objectives (i.e., inclusive access to public services) and economic objectives (job creation and economic growth), as follows:

The African Union has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Africa Centres for Disease Control Support Program to Combat Current and Future Public Health Threats Project. The Project Development Objective is to enhance the capacity of Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) to support AU Member States in preventing, detecting, and responding to current and future public health threats and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), an autonomous institution of the African Union, is mandated to strengthen public health systems across Africa through coordinated disease prevention, preparedness, and response. In line with this mandate, Africa CDC is establishing Five (5) Regional Coordinating Centres (RCCs), including the Eastern Africa RCC. On 27 April 2025, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between the Government of Kenya and Africa CDC, under which the Government of Kenya allocated 10 acres of land for the establishment of the Eastern Africa Regional Coordinating Office and Regional Training Centre.

The proposed EARCC Hub will involve ground-clearing, earthworks, civil construction, installation of utilities (water, electricity, sanitation, medical waste systems), and fit-out of specialized laboratory and emergency operations facilities. These activities entail significant environmental and social risks during the construction and operational phases, necessitating a comprehensive ESIA prior to any physical work. To guide evidencebased decisionmaking, Africa CDC seeks to commission a consultant to conduct a PreFeasibility Study, Feasibility Study, and a full Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) that complies with both Kenyan law and AU/Africa CDC standards.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include to assess environmental and social risks and impacts of the proposed project, ensure compliance with applicable standards, and develop mitigation and management measures that support sustainable, inclusive, and climate-resilient implementation. It is expected that the consultancy will be undertaken within a period of 12 weeks. The expected start date of the assignment is January 2027.
