REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST
(Consultant Services – Individual Consultant)

Country: Republic of Kosovo
Project Name: Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening (KOMPAS)
Project ID: P179831
Loan No.: IDA 75410
Assignment Title: Legal Specialist – Digital Health Governance & IHIS Regulatory Framework
Reference No.: XK-MOH-A1.01-CS-INDV
Issued on: 18 November 2026

Background

The Government of Kosovo has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening Project (KOMPAS) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include providing legal and regulatory expertise to develop a legally sound and actionable regulatory framework for the implementation of the Integrated Health Information System (IHIS) within the Ministry of Health, under Component 2 of the KOMPAS Project. The Consultant will determine the appropriate legal pathway for each required change; review the existing legal framework and draft the necessary laws, Administrative Instructions and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs); propose legal provisions and mechanisms to mandate the use of IHIS by public and private health care providers and health professionals; map the rights, responsibilities, accountability and liability of all key actors in the IHIS ecosystem; and develop the legal framework for health data analytics at the National Institute of Public Health (NIPH).

The expected level of effort is up to 120 working days over a period of 12 months. The assignment is expected to commence in December 2026, with the exact start date to be confirmed upon contract signature.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

The Ministry of Health now invites eligible individual consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested candidates should submit:

  • A Letter of Expression of Interest
  • A detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Copies of diplomas and relevant certifications
  • References for similar assignments (if available)

 

Selection Method

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultants (IC) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

Qualifications and Experience Requirements

The Consultant shall meet the following minimum qualifications:

  • Education: University Degree in Law; a Master’s degree in Law is preferred.
  • Minimum of 10 years of professional legal experience, with a strong focus on health legislation, labor law, or public administration in Kosovo.
  • Proven experience in drafting administrative instructions, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and regulatory frameworks within the public sector.
  • Experience in data protection, digital health or ICT law, or alignment with the EU acquis is an asset.
  • Experience in projects financed by international financial institutions or donors, preferably the World Bank, is an advantage.
  • Fluency in Albanian and English is required. Working knowledge of Serbian is an asset.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09:00 to 16:00.

Expressions of Interest must be delivered electronically (by e-mail) to the address below no later than 03 December 2026 at 4:00 PM local time. Expressions of Interest received after the deadline will not be considered. Incomplete Expressions of Interest, which do not include all the documents requested above, may not be considered.

Ministry of Health

Project Coordination Unit Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening (KOMPAS)
Pristina, Kosovo

Attn: Fanol Duli, Project Coordinator

Email: fanol.duli@rks-gov.net

CC: Blerim Çerkini, Procurement Specialist

Email: blerim.cerkini@rks-gov.net

 

 

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

 

Country: Kosovo                           

World Bank Loan/Credit Name: Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening- KOMPAS

Project ID: P179831

Ref. No.: XK-MOH-A1.01-CS-INDV

Assignment name:  Legal Specialist – Digital Health Governance & IHIS Regulatory Framework

 

  1. Background

Referring to the Financing Agreement between the Republic of Kosovo and the International Development Association for the Kosovo Comprehensive Approach to Health System Strengthening Project (KOMPAS), the KOMPAS Project (P179831) was approved on 07 May, 2024. The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to strengthen institutional capacity and governance for quality of care in the Kosovo health system.

The Project has three components: Component 1 (strengthening key health system building blocks for Quality of Care), Component 2 (developing an Integrated Health Information System) and Component 3 (project management, monitoring and evaluation). The elements most relevant to this assignment are summarised below:

Component 1: Strengthening key health system building blocks for Quality of Care (QoC)

The objective of this component is to support aspects of public health/Pandemic Preparedness and Response (PPR), service delivery, and health financing (strategic purchasing), that will help unblock the bottlenecks in the structural and process of care. Of particular relevance to this assignment is Subcomponent 1.2:

Subcomponent 1.2 Developing and implementing strategic purchasing for quality. This subcomponent will support the development and implementation of key strategic purchasing elements which are not in place in Kosovo but are critical for both structural and process aspects of quality care. The IHIS is expected to supply the claims, reimbursement and performance data on which strategic purchasing by the Health Insurance Fund (HIF) will depend.

Component 2: Developing an Integrated Health Information System (IHIS): The objective of this component is to support the design, development, and implementation of an integrated digital health ecosystem that is critical for the functioning of the entire health system. The foundational and key strategic IHIS building blocks will set the digitized health data environment to support health service delivery and decision-making.

This activity is informed by the “Kosovo eHealth Feasibility Study,” which was completed under the Kosovo Emergency COVID-19 Project (P173819). The planned system will include Primary Health Care (PHC) facilities and hospitals, as well as laboratories and the National Institute of Public Health (NIPH), and will allow for the seamless transmission and sharing of health information among all authorized individuals. Based on globally recognized best practices and experience with previous health information systems development in Kosovo, the approach will be to not build one monolithic system but rather an ecosystem of cooperating information systems built on common governance, standardization, and technical foundational building blocks. Such a system will also require robust patient confidentiality and data privacy protocols to ensure that only authorized users can access patient data.

This component will include three sub-components, outlined below:

Subcomponent 2.1: Establishing foundational building blocks of IHIS. This subcomponent will support the establishment of critical elements of foundational environment (Enterprise Architecture) for digital health systems implementation, including: (i) the legal and regulatory framework for transformed health services delivery through digital systems utilization; (ii) the assessment and design of Master Data Management standards and systems, such as foundational registries and common coding and classification systems; (iii) design and implementation of the Health Information Exchange services; and (iv) upgrade of hardware platforms on central locations and in health facilities.

Subcomponent 2.2: Digital health support for improvement in QoC. Implementation of Component 1 will require finalization of the implementation and upgrade of the basic health information system (BHIS). Currently, the BHIS is not fully implemented in all Primary Health Care (PHC) facilities and with full functionality. This subcomponent will support: (i) rolling out the BHIS to all PHC facilities (including finalization of patient empanelment and zoning); (ii) upgrading the BHIS functions (automatic update of codes from key registries and allowing dashboard and smart reporting on facility level); and (iii) upgrading the integration with eReferrals system and introduction of eAppointments.

Subcomponent 2.3: Implementation of IHIS strategic systems. The eHealth Feasibility Study envisages full digitalization of the health sector in Kosovo to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of service delivery, clinical decision support, health financing, pandemic preparedness and public health functions, supply chain for pharmaceuticals and nutraceuticals, health workforce management, and health system management and policy making.

  1. Objective of the Assignment

The primary objective of this assignment is to develop a legally sound and actionable regulatory framework to support the implementation of the Integrated Health Information System (IHIS) within the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Kosovo, under the World Bank–financed KOMPAS Project.

In line with the Project Appraisal Document (PAD) and the Digital Health Blueprint, the Ministry is advancing the digital transformation of the health sector, with a particular focus on establishing an enabling legal and regulatory environment for the use of digital health systems. A key priority is ensuring that IHIS becomes an integral and mandatory component of healthcare service delivery.

The assignment will therefore include determining the appropriate legal pathway for each required change, and the drafting of legal provisions and mechanisms to mandate the use of IHIS by public and private health care providers and health professionals, as well as the development of the necessary legal texts and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to support system implementation and enable health data analytics at the National Institute of Public Health (NIPH).

  1. Scope of Work

The Legal Specialist will work closely with the Project Coordination Unit (NJKP/PCU), digital health working groups, and MoH legal departments to execute the following tasks:

The Legal Specialist is responsible for the legal and regulatory aspects of the tasks below. The design of technical governance arrangements, interoperability and data standards, system architecture and security controls remains the responsibility of the MoH, the IHIS technical teams and the SDHP. The Legal Specialist will work with these teams, and with the Agency for Information Society and the Information and Privacy Agency, to ensure that the technical arrangements have a sound legal basis and are reflected in the proposed legal and regulatory texts.

  • Legal Pathway and Instrument Mapping (first step): As the first task of the assignment, determine for each required change whether it needs primary legislation (new law or amendment), an Administrative Instruction or other secondary act, SOPs, amendments to job descriptions or other employment-related instruments, contracts, or other acts. For each change, identify the responsible institution, the legal basis, the adoption procedure (including Government and Assembly procedures where primary legislation is needed), the sequencing and dependencies between instruments, and the likely timeline. The resulting map, once agreed with the MoH, will determine the form and sequencing of the drafts prepared under the other tasks.
  • IHIS Legal Framework Review (Activity A1.01): Conduct a comprehensive review of the existing legal framework governing the IHIS. In line with the agreed legal pathway, draft and finalize the necessary legal and regulatory texts (e.g., laws, administrative instructions) to support the secure, interoperable rollout of digital health systems. The review and the draft texts shall address, at a minimum, the following areas:
    • Governance and institutional mandates: a clear legal definition of IHIS ownership and governance, including system ownership, the data controller and processor roles for each IHIS component, and the respective mandates of and relationships between the MoH, the NIPH, the HIF, the Agency for Information Society and the Information and Privacy Agency.
    • Health Insurance Fund and strategic purchasing: the role of the HIF in the IHIS, its lawful access to data, and the legal link between IHIS records and claims, reimbursement and performance-based payment.
    • Patient identification and record linkage: the legal basis for patient identification, unique patient identifiers, record linkage and the master patient index.
    • Patient rights: consent models, patient access to their own records, rectification, audit trails of who has accessed a record, and complaint and redress channels, consistent with Law No. 06/L-082 and the EHDS.
    • Secondary use of health data: the lawful basis and governance for the use of health data for research, planning and policy, including anonymisation and pseudonymisation standards and the body responsible for approving data access.
    • Commercial use of health data: what private actors may and may not do with health data (for example marketing, insurance underwriting and the sale of data), and the terms on which health technology innovators may access data, to the extent this is not already covered by Law No. 06/L-082.
    • Digital instruments: the legal validity of electronic signatures and electronic prescriptions in the health sector, the legal status of electronic records compared with paper records, and telemedicine, together with the regulatory provisions governing their mandatory use.
    • Cybersecurity and continuity: security standards for the IHIS platform, incident notification and business continuity requirements, cross-checked against the national cybersecurity and critical infrastructure framework.
    • Hosting, cloud and cross-border exchange: hosting location, use of cloud services, processing by foreign vendors, and cross-border exchange of health data with EU systems.
  • Private Sector Scope and Connection Obligations: Working with the SDHP, prepare a mapping of the actors who must connect to the IHIS, who may connect and who are exempt, covering at least private clinics and hospitals, private laboratories, pharmacies, diagnostic centres, individual health professionals in private practice and private health insurers (if any). Because private providers are not bound by civil service instruments, propose the legal mechanisms that will apply to them, such as mandatory connection and reporting duties, conditions for licensing and accreditation, links to contracting with the HIF, and incentives for connection.
  • Technology Vendors, Procurement and Contracting: Propose the legal and regulatory requirements for IHIS technology vendors and IT suppliers, including certification of vendors and software, initial and ongoing conformance testing against interoperability standards, data processing agreements, source code and data escrow, exit and data portability clauses, and liability for defects. Where the IHIS involves outsourced hosting, managed services or public-private arrangements, assess the related public procurement and contract law implications.
  • Data Privacy & Security Compliance: Ensure all drafted legal frameworks, AIs, and SOPs strictly adhere to Kosovo’s Law No. 06/L-082 on Protection of Personal Data, establishing secure protocols for electronic patient records and the NIPH data warehouse.
  • NIPH Health Data Analytics & "One Health" Governance (Activity A3.08): Review and draft specific legal and regulatory texts—including Administrative Instructions (AIs) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)—required for redesigning and implementing NIPH health data analytics. This includes providing the legal frameworks for data warehouses, system interfaces, smart reporting mechanisms, and establishing data-sharing protocols to support "One Health" initiatives (ensuring legal interoperability with veterinary or environmental health data).
  • Legal Gap Analysis for Personnel: Review the Law on Health, Law on Labor, Law on Civil Service, and current administrative instructions governing health professionals to identify legal and regulatory gaps related to the mandatory use of IHIS in healthcare service delivery. The review shall assess whether existing legal provisions adequately define the responsibilities of healthcare professionals for electronic data entry, digital record management, and compliance with IHIS-related requirements, and propose necessary amendments where required. The review shall also cover the professional licensing and regulatory framework that applies to health professionals in private practice.
  • Professional Duties and JD Provisions: Propose legally appropriate provisions and mechanisms, including, where appropriate, amendments to job descriptions (JDs), employment-related instruments, administrative instructions or other relevant acts, explicitly defining "Digital Record Management" and real-time IHIS data entry as core professional responsibilities.
  • Mapping of Rights, Responsibilities, Accountability and Liability across the IHIS Ecosystem: Map the legal rights, responsibilities, accountability and liability of all key actors in the IHIS ecosystem, including at least: the MoH, the NIPH, the HIF, public and private health care providers and health professionals, system administrators, non-clinical users, data controllers and data processors, technology vendors and service providers, and entities accessing health data for secondary use. For each actor, the mapping shall identify the applicable legal obligations, the accountability and liability for breaches or misuse, and any gaps in the current legal framework, and shall propose the provisions needed to address them.
  • Accountability & Compliance Framework: Formulate a legal strategy defining compliance mechanisms and accountability measures for all IHIS actors identified in the mapping above, including the legal definition of "digital negligence" regarding patient registration, electronic prescribing, and clinical coding within the IHIS. The Consultant shall assess whether the proposed sanctions, disciplinary routes and incentives are proportionate and workable, and shall propose reciprocal obligations on the system provider and the MoH (such as system availability and uptime, technical support and training) as conditions for enforcing user obligations.
  • Stakeholder Consultation: Present the legal strategies, drafted texts, and SOPs to key stakeholders, including the NIPH, Chamber of Doctors, Chamber of Nurses, Chamber of Pharmacists, Chamber of Dentists, the HIF, the Agency for Information Society, the Information and Privacy Agency, representatives of private health care providers, and MoH leadership, incorporating feedback to ensure sector-wide alignment.
  • EU Alignment: Review relevant EU digital health and health data governance requirements, including the European Health Data Space (EHDS), and ensure that the proposed legal and regulatory framework supports progressive alignment with applicable EU standards and interoperability requirements, including for patient rights, secondary use of data and cross-border exchange.
  1. Deliverables

The Consultant is expected to deliver the following:

  1. Inception & Legal Gap Report: Identifying current legal barriers for both IHIS utilization and NIPH data analytics, and including: (i) the legal pathway and instrument map (primary legislation, AIs, SOPs, employment-related instruments, contracts and other acts), with responsible institutions, adoption procedures, sequencing and an indicative timeline; and (ii) the private sector connection mapping (must connect, may connect, exempt); and (iii) the mapping of rights, responsibilities, accountability and liability of all key IHIS actors. Once approved by the MoH, this report will confirm the form and scope of Deliverables 2 to 5.
  2. Draft Regulatory Texts for IHIS (A1.01): Comprehensive drafts of required legal/regulatory texts supporting the broader digital transformation of health services (Sub-component 2.1). The drafts shall cover the areas listed in Section 3, including governance and institutional mandates, patient rights, secondary and commercial use of data, private sector obligations and vendor requirements, in the form of instrument determined in Deliverable 1.
  3. NIPH Data Analytics Legal Framework (A3.08): Drafted AIs and SOPs governing the data warehouse, interfaces, and smart reporting for the NIPH.
  4. IHIS Professional Obligations Package: Proposed provisions making IHIS use mandatory, for integration, where appropriate, into the JDs, employment contracts and other employment-related instruments of public sector health professionals, together with the equivalent licensing, accreditation or contracting mechanisms for private providers.
  5. Draft Compliance Instrument(s): Draft MoH Administrative Instruction(s) or other instrument(s), in the form determined in Deliverable 1, establishing the compliance and accountability mechanisms, including the reciprocal obligations of the system provider and the MoH.

Language Requirement for Deliverables: All final, publication-ready legal texts (Laws, Administrative Instructions, SOPs) must be delivered in both official languages (Albanian and Serbian), alongside English versions for World Bank review and clearance. The MoH/PCU will arrange translation into Serbian; the Consultant shall support the legal validation of the Serbian versions.

  1. Qualifications and Experience Requirements
  • Education: University Degree (Preferred Master’s) in Law.
  • Professional Experience: Minimum of 10 years of professional legal experience, with a strong focus on health legislation, labor law, or public administration in Kosovo.
  • Specific Expertise: Proven experience in drafting administrative instructions, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and regulatory frameworks within the public sector. Experience in data protection, digital health or ICT law, or alignment with the EU acquis is an asset.
  • Language: Fluency in Albanian and English is required. Working knowledge of Serbian is an asset.

 

  1. Reporting, Clearances, and Duration
  • Reporting: The Consultant will report directly to the KOMPAS Project Coordinator within the NJKP/PCU. The General Secretary of the MoH will provide strategic and technical oversight, including clearance of deliverables.
  • Duration: The expected level of effort is up to 120 working days over a period of 12 months.
  • The Consultant will submit monthly progress reports outlining activities undertaken, deliverables produced, and progress against the agreed work plan.
  • The Consultant shall perform his/her duties in accordance with the terms and conditions of the contract, the applicable legislation of the Republic of Kosovo, and the World Bank Procurement Regulations and implementation procedures.

Client Contribution

Consultant will be based and work in the MoH premises in Pristina. The MoH will provide office space and equipment required.

Selection process

Experienced and qualified individuals will be selected in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing (IPF) Borrowers (“the Regulations”), as updated in February 2025, based on an open call for Individual Consultants (IC) Selection.

The consultant will be selected based on:

  • General qualifications (education, legal competencies, analytical and drafting skills) – 30%
  • Specific professional experience relevant to the assignment (health legislation, regulatory and legal drafting, digital health governance, data protection, development of Administrative Instructions and SOPs) – 40%
  • Experience in similar assignments/projects (public sector legal advisory roles, regulatory framework development, donor-funded projects, preferably World Bank–financed projects) – 30%

CONSULTANCY SERVICE TO ASSESS THE ECONOMIC IMPLICATIONS AND PUBLIC PERCEPTIONS OF THE FREE MOVEMENT OF PERSONS PROTOCOL.

 

REF: ET-AUC-569896-CS-QCBS

 

 

  1. Background

The African Union (AU), through Agenda 2063 and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), has positioned regional integration as a cornerstone of Africa’s economic transformation. The Free Movement of Persons (FMP) and labour mobility are critical enablers of this vision, facilitating trade in services, investment, skills mobility, tourism, and the development of regional value chains across the continent.

To advance these objectives, the AU adopted the FMP Protocol in 2018 (African Union, 2018), with the aim of progressively removing barriers to mobility among Member States. Effective implementation of the Protocol is expected to enhance productivity, competitiveness, employment opportunities, and broader economic integration. However, progress towards ratification and implementation has remained limited, largely due to concerns related to security, labour market impacts, migration governance, and national sovereignty. As of September 2026, 32 Member States have signed the Protocol and four (Mali, Niger, Rwanda, and São Tomé and Príncipe) have ratified it, against the 15 ratifications required for entry into force; no new signature or ratification has been recorded since 2019 (ICMPD and AUC, 2025; Mo Ibrahim Foundation, 2026). Existing analytical work has documented the expected benefits of free movement and the reasons for slow ratification (AUC and IOM, 2018; Hirsch, 2021; ECA and AUC, 2023; ICMPD and AUC, 2025), but has not yet quantified the incremental economic effects of the Protocol against a counterfactual, nor the distribution of its costs and benefits across Member States (UNCTAD, 2018; Maskus, 2023).

In contrast, several Regional Economic Communities (RECs), particularly ECOWAS, have implemented the right of entry (Phase 1 of the FMP Protocol) for their citizens, while the rights of residence and establishment remain only partially implemented, and border closures, deportations and re-introduced formalities have at times reversed progress (ECA and AUC, 2023; ICMPD and AUC, 2025; AfDB and AUC, 2025). The differing levels of acceptance and implementation between regional and continental mobility frameworks present an important policy question for the African Union and highlight the need for a better understanding of both the economic opportunities and the socio-political factors influencing support for free movement.

This study is financed under the World Bank-supported Building Institutions and Systems to Harness and Realize Agenda 2063 (BIASHARA) project (P180117), which supports the AUC and the AfCFTA Secretariat in advancing three Agenda 2063 flagship commitments – the AfCFTA, the Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM) and the FMP Protocol – and which includes performance-based conditions on the alignment of Member State and REC legal and regulatory frameworks with all three instruments (World Bank, 2023). The study is therefore expected to treat the FMP Protocol as one pillar of an integrated market-access, connectivity and mobility agenda, and its outputs will feed the BIASHARA results framework and the AU scorecards on AfCFTA, SAATM and FMP implementation.

Against this backdrop, the African Union Commission (AUC) seeks to undertake a comprehensive study that integrates the following two complementary lines of inquiry:

  1. Phase 1 (economic implications) will assess the prospective economic implications of implementing the FMP Protocol, including its potential impact on trade, tourism, labour markets, investment, and regional economic integration.
  2. Phase 2 (public and stakeholder perceptions) will examine public perceptions of mobility and labour movement across Africa, identifying the factors that shape acceptance, resistance, trust, and concerns regarding regional and continental mobility initiatives. Drawing on comparative regional experiences, observed mobility practices, and selected country case studies, the study will generate evidence-based insights and practical recommendations to support effective implementation of the FMP Protocol and strengthen Africa's regional integration agenda.

The two phases will be delivered by a single consulting firm (or consortium) as parallel workstreams under one inception report, one steering committee and one integrated final report, so that the economic evidence generated in Phase 1 informs the communication and advocacy outputs of Phase 2.

Phase 1: Assessment of the Economic Implications of the Free Movement of Persons Protocol and Comparative Analysis of Regional Mobility Regimes in Africa

This assignment integrates two complementary analytical components:

  • Study A: Assessment of the economic implications of the Free Movement Protocol on trade, tourism, and labour markets (economic impact)
  • Study B: Comparative analysis of regional mobility regimes and exploratory case studies of first-mover countries (comparative analysis)

Together, these analyses will provide practical, evidence-based insights to support AU Member States in advancing the implementation of the FMP Protocol and maximizing its economic benefits.

  1. Objectives of the Assignment

The overall objective of this consultancy is to generate policy-relevant, forward-looking evidence and strategic guidance to support the implementation of the AU Free Movement of Persons (FMP) Protocol.

Specifically, the assignment aims to:

  • Provide a quantified, scenario-based assessment of the incremental economic effects of implementing the FMP Protocol – relative to a baseline of continued unilateral and REC-level visa liberalisation – covering trade, tourism and air travel, labour markets, regional value chains, public finances and broader economic growth, and reporting both benefits and costs.
  • Quantify how benefits and costs are distributed across Member States (countries of origin and destination; income groups; skilled and less-skilled workers; women and men), and identify the fiscal implications for Member States, including visa and permit revenue foregone and the tax and social contributions of mobile workers.
  • Demonstrate the contribution of labour mobility to AfCFTA implementation, particularly in relation to trade in services (Mode 4), productivity, and regional economic integration, and the complementarity between the FMP Protocol, the AfCFTA and the Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM).
  • Generate comparative, evidence-based insights from existing regional mobility regimes and first-mover countries, highlighting enabling conditions, practical implementation approaches, and early outcomes, including the reasons why the rights of residence and establishment have lagged behind the right of entry and the lessons of reversal episodes.
  • Deliver actionable, policy-oriented recommendations and strategic guidance to inform:
    • AU policy dialogue and advocacy
    • AfCFTA-aligned economic integration strategies
    • Member States’ implementation of the FMP Protocol
    • BIASHARA programme monitoring and the AU scorecards on AfCFTA, SAATM and FMP implementation
  1.  Scope of Work

The consultant will undertake the following tasks:

  1. Conduct a comprehensive review of literature, policy frameworks, and existing studies on the economic impacts of migration, mobility, and labour movement in Africa, including AfCFTA-related dynamics. The review shall take the existing evidence base as its starting point and state explicitly what the present study adds; at a minimum it shall cover AUC and IOM (2018), UNCTAD (2018), OECD and ILO (2018), World Bank (2020), Hirsch (2021), Bisong (2022), ECA and AUC (2023), Chime et al. (2023), Maskus (2023), IOM and AUC (2024), ICMPD and AUC (2025), ECA and AUC (2025), the Africa Visa Openness Index series (AfDB and AUC, 2025), Mo Ibrahim Foundation (2026) and Afrobarometer (2026).
  2. Assess the economic impact of implementing the FMP Protocol under explicit scenarios corresponding to the Protocol's three phases (right of entry; right of residence; right of establishment) and to variable-geometry coalitions of ratifying States, against a baseline that reflects existing unilateral and REC-level liberalisation, focusing on:
  1. Trade (including intra-African trade and services)
  2. Tourism flows, business travel and intra-African air passenger traffic
  3. Labour markets (employment, skills mobility, productivity)
  4. Investment and business mobility
  5. Public finances (visa and permit revenue foregone; tax and social contributions of mobile workers; public service costs)
  6. Informal and small-scale cross-border trade, with gender-disaggregated analysis
  7. Remittances and diaspora investment
  8. Implementation costs (civil registration and identity systems, border management, recognition of qualifications) and labour-market adjustment risks in destination countries
  1. Analyze the linkages between mobility and AfCFTA, including:
  1. Trade in services and movement of service providers (Mode 4 commitments in Member States' schedules under the AfCFTA Protocol on Trade in Services, and movement of key personnel under the Protocol on Investment)
  2. Labour mobility and regional value chains
  3. Economic integration and competitiveness
  1. Analyse the integration linkages between the FMP Protocol, the AfCFTA and the Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM), in the broader context of the Agenda 2063 flagship projects supported under BIASHARA, including:
  1. Mapping the FMP Protocol's three phases against the mobility-dependent provisions of the AfCFTA (Mode 4 commitments under the Protocol on Trade in Services, movement of key personnel under the Protocol on Investment, and the operational needs of the Guided Trade Initiative) and identifying where the absence of mobility rights constrains AfCFTA implementation
  2. Including intra-African air passenger flows as an outcome variable in the quantitative analysis, using AFCAC/IATA data and the SAATM Continental Study route dataset (AUC and IATA, 2021), to estimate the interaction between visa openness (Africa Visa Openness Index) and air service liberalisation (SAATM Solemn Commitment and implementation status)
  3. A three-flagship status snapshot for each case-study country – AfCFTA (ratification, tariff and services schedules), SAATM (commitment, implementation, intra-African seat capacity) and FMP (signature/ratification, visa openness score, work-permit regime) – identifying sequencing complementarities and joint quick wins, consistent with the Africa Regional Integration Index, which already measures visa openness and intra-regional flight connections jointly (UNECA, AU and AfDB, 2019)
  4. A short set of joint advocacy messages for Ministers of Finance, Trade, Transport and Interior, delivered as an Integration Linkages Note (maximum 15 pages plus the snapshot matrix) and incorporated as a chapter of the final report and reflected in the policy briefs
  1. Undertake a comparative analysis of regional mobility regimes (e.g., ECOWAS, EAC, SADC), examining:
  1. Institutional and legal frameworks
  2. Implementation practices and governance models
  3. Economic outcomes, measured with quantified indicators (migrant stocks and flows, cross-border trade, tourism arrivals, remittances), including the reasons why the rights of residence and establishment have lagged the right of entry, the effects of the January 2025 withdrawal of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger from ECOWAS, and reversal episodes (re-introduced visa requirements, electronic travel authorisations, border closures)
  1. Conduct exploratory case studies of 4–6 countries selected against explicit criteria – ratifying States; unilateral first movers (e.g., Rwanda, Kenya, Ghana, Benin, The Gambia, Seychelles); pivotal non-signatories (e.g., South Africa, Nigeria, Egypt); and at least one North African and one lusophone Member State –, focusing on:
  1. Early implementation approaches
  2. Enabling policy and institutional conditions
  3. Emerging economic benefits and challenges
  1. Identify key enabling factors and constraints affecting the economic impact of free movement, including regulatory, institutional, and political economy dimensions.
  2. Engage key stakeholders (AU institutions, RECs, Member States, private sector, tourism actors, and academia) to validate findings and ensure policy relevance.
  3. Develop policy recommendations and strategic guidance to:
  1. Maximize economic benefits of the FMP Protocol
  2. Align mobility frameworks with AfCFTA objectives
  3. Support Member States in implementation efforts
  4. Prepare a country-by-country readiness assessment of signatory States that have not yet ratified (a 'pathway to 15 ratifications'), presented in a traffic-light format compatible with the AU scorecards on AfCFTA, SAATM and FMP implementation
  1. Produce high-quality analytical outputs, including a final report and policy briefs tailored to AU decision-making processes. Outputs shall include the datasets, model files and code in reproducible form, a technical annex documenting methods, data and assumptions, and executive summaries in English and French, with Arabic and Portuguese versions of the policy briefs.
  1. Proposed Methodology

The study will adopt a mixed-methods analytical approach, combining quantitative and qualitative techniques to generate robust, policy-relevant, and forward-looking insights. The quantitative component shall, at a minimum, comprise: (i) gravity-model estimates of the effect of visa and permit restrictions on bilateral trade, tourism and intra-African air passenger flows, using a visa-restrictions index derived from the Africa Visa Openness Index (AfDB and AUC, 2025); (ii) event studies of the liberalisation and reversal episodes already observed (e.g., Rwanda 2013, Seychelles, Kenya 2024, Ghana 2025, Benin 2025, the ECOWAS decision of 2024 to abolish the 90-day limit); (iii) a labour-mobility scenario model (computable general equilibrium or a calibrated partial-equilibrium model) reporting results by phase of the Protocol and by country of origin and destination, extending the benefit-cost approach of Maskus (2023) beyond skilled labour; and (iv) fiscal incidence analysis for the case-study countries following the approach of OECD and ILO (2018). Data sources shall include the Africa Visa Openness Index series, UN DESA international migrant stocks, the AU Report on Labour Migration Statistics in Africa (STATAFRIC), AFCAC/IATA air traffic data and the SAATM Continental Study dataset (AUC and IATA, 2021), UN Tourism arrivals, World Bank/KNOMAD remittance data, COMESA and EAC small-scale cross-border trade surveys, the Freemove Project regime dataset (Acosta and van der Baaren, 2024), and national statistics.

This will be complemented by qualitative research, including key informant interviews with AU institutions, RECs, Member State representatives, private sector actors, and technical experts. A comparative case study approach will be applied, focusing on a targeted sample of regional mobility regimes and selected first-mover countries (approximately 4–6 cases) to ensure analytical depth while maintaining geographic representation.

The analysis will be structured around a comparative framework examining institutional arrangements, policy environments, and observed mobility practices. Findings will be validated through stakeholder consultations to ensure accuracy, relevance, and alignment with policy needs.

This approach is designed to balance analytical rigor, depth, and feasibility within the assignment timeline, while avoiding overly broad or non-implementable coverage.

Phase 2: A Continental Study on Public Perceptions of Free Movement of Persons in Africa: Comparative Analysis of Regional and Continental Mobility Dynamics

The study will answer a central analytical question:

  • What factors explain differences in public and stakeholder perceptions of regional and continental mobility frameworks, including their perceived feasibility, benefits, risks and implications for free movement? ?

Understanding how and why perceptions of regional and continental mobility frameworks differ is important for advancing continental integration. These perceptions may be shaped by a range of economic, social, political and institutional factors, including concerns around employment and job competition, irregular migration, security, migration governance and national sovereignty. The study will examine how these factors influence both public attitudes and stakeholder positions on the ratification and implementation of the FMP Protocol.

Continental survey evidence shows majority public support (56 per cent) for free movement within regions, alongside a widespread perception that crossing borders to work or trade is difficult and divided views on the economic effects of immigration (Afrobarometer, 2026). Paradoxically, the hesitation documented to date is largely at State level – sovereignty, security, revenue and the institutional separation between trade and interior ministries (ECA and AUC, 2023). No survey has yet asked citizens about a continental protocol as distinct from their regional regime. The analysis shall therefore distinguish government and elite positions from public attitudes, and shall include a continental-versus-regional comparison by design.

In this context, the African Union Commission seeks to undertake a comprehensive study to assess public perceptions of mobility across Africa, identify key drivers of fear and resistance, and generate evidence-based policy recommendations. The study will inform policy design, advocacy strategies, and labour mobility frameworks aligned with AfCFTA implementation, thereby strengthening the AU’s capacity to advance regional integration, intra-African trade, and economic transformation.

  1. Objective of the Assignment

The overall objective of this consultancy is to:

  1. Assess public perceptions of mobility, migration, and labour movement across Africa, with particular focus on concerns related to security, employment, and migration governance.
  2. Analyze the comparative dynamics between regional and continental mobility frameworks, testing the hypothesis that regional mobility regimes are perceived as more feasible and manageable than continental initiatives, and distinguishing public attitudes from government and elite positions.
  3. Identify key socio-political, economic, and security-related drivers of fear, resistance, and acceptance influencing public attitudes toward free movement.
  4. Develop actionable, evidence-based recommendations to inform:
    1. Ratification and implementation of the Free Movement of Persons Protocol
    2. AU public communication and advocacy strategies
    3. Labour mobility frameworks aligned with AfCFTA implementation
  1. Scope of Work

The consultant will undertake the following tasks:

1. Literature and Policy Review: Conduct a structured review of existing literature, AU policy frameworks, REC protocols, and empirical studies on migration, mobility, and labour movement in Africa, including AfCFTA-related mobility dynamics. The review shall include political-economy analyses of African migration governance (Hirsch, 2021; Zanker, 2019; Bisong, 2022; Chime et al., 2023; Maunganidze, 2022) and the perception evidence in Afrobarometer (2026).

2. Mapping and Analysis of Public Perceptions: Map and analyze public perceptions across a selected sample of AU Member States and RECs focusing on:

  • Security concerns (e.g., terrorism, cross-border crime)
  • Employment and labour market competition
  • Migration governance and irregular migration

Data sources will include:

  • Existing datasets (Afrobarometer Round 10, 2024/25, and earlier rounds; national and regional perception surveys)
  • Key informant interviews (government, AU/REC officials, private sector, academia)
  • Focus group discussions and a survey experiment in 6–8 Member States testing framing effects (continental versus regional versus bilateral mobility; skilled versus less-skilled workers; reciprocity), with the sample, countries and instruments to be specified in the inception report against the budget envelope
  • Media and digital narrative analysis
  • Message testing of candidate advocacy narratives, to inform the strategic communication guidance
  • All primary data collection shall comply with research ethics approval, informed consent and applicable data protection requirements, to be set out in the inception report

3. Comparative Assessment of Regional Mobility Regimes: Using the same case set as Phase 1 (Task 4) to avoid duplication, undertake a comparative assessment of selected regional mobility regimes (e.g., ECOWAS, EAC, SADC), examining:

  • Levels of public acceptance and trust
  • Implementation practices and governance models
  • Perceived economic and social benefits and risks

4. Analysis of Divergence Between Regional and Continental Mobility Frameworks: Analyze the divergence between regional and continental mobility frameworks, focusing on:

  • Differences in public trust and political acceptance
  • Perceived risks versus benefits at the continental level
  • Structural, institutional, and narrative factors influencing resistance

This analysis will draw on comparative evidence and stakeholder insights to explain why regional mobility regimes are often perceived as more feasible than continental initiatives.

5. Analyze Public Perceptions of Labour Mobility and Economic Opportunity: Examine how labour mobility and its perceived linkages to economic opportunity are understood by different stakeholder groups, focusing on:

  • Perceptions of job competition versus job creation
  • Public attitudes toward movement of workers and service providers
  • Perceived benefits and risks of skills mobility
  • Trust in national and continental institutions to manage labour mobility

This analysis will focus on perceptions, narratives, and attitudes, rather than measuring actual economic outcomes, and will complement the economic implications study.

6. Identify key narratives, misinformation trends, and political economy dynamics shaping public perceptions of free movement.

7. Engage key stakeholders (AU institutions, RECs, Member States, private sector, civil society, and academia) to validate findings and ensure policy relevance.

8. Develop policy recommendations and provide strategic guidance to:

  1. Address public fears and misconceptions
  2. Strengthen AU communication and advocacy strategies
  3. Align mobility policies with AfCFTA labour market needs
  4. Support Member States in advancing ratification and implementation of the Free Movement of Persons Protocol

9. Produce high-quality analytical outputs, including a final report and policy briefs tailored to AU decision-making processes.

  1. Proposed Methodology

The study will adopt a mixed-methods approach combining quantitative and qualitative techniques to ensure robust and policy-relevant findings. It will draw on existing datasets (such as Afrobarometer and national perception surveys), complemented by primary data collection (a survey experiment, focus group discussions and elite interviews with parliamentarians, immigration and labour officials) in a targeted sample of 6–8 Member States across the five AU regions, including at least one North African Member State.

Qualitative methods will include key informant interviews with government officials, AU/REC representatives, private sector actors, civil society, and academia, as well as focus group discussions where feasible.

The study will also incorporate media and digital narrative analysis to capture prevailing public discourse, misinformation trends, and framing of mobility issues. A comparative analytical framework will be applied across selected regions and countries to identify patterns of perception, drivers of resistance or acceptance, and variations between regional and continental mobility narratives. Findings will be validated through stakeholder consultations to ensure accuracy, representativeness, and policy relevance.

  1. Schedule for Completion of Tasks

The assignment is expected to be completed within 30 weeks from the date of contract signature. The two phases will run as parallel workstreams under a single joint inception report; the milestones below are expressed as weeks from contract signature. A validation workshop with Member States, RECs, the AfCFTA Secretariat and AFCAC will be held between the interim and final reports (week 18).

A revised final report incorporating feedback from the AUC, along with policy briefs tailored to Heads of State, Ministers of Finance, Trade, Transport and Interior, the Pan-African Parliament and the RECs; the 'pathway to 15 ratifications' readiness assessment; the strategic communication guidance; and the datasets, model files and code.   1. Data, Services, and Facilities to be Provided by the Client

The African Union Commission will provide:

  1. Relevant AU policy frameworks (FMP Protocol, Agenda 2063, AfCFTA documents)
  2. Access to key stakeholders within AU, RECs, and Member States
  3. Introduction to respective stakeholders, where need be
  4. Existing studies and data related to mobility and economic integration
  5. AFCAC data on SAATM implementation status and the SAATM Continental Study dataset (AUC and IATA, 2021); AfCFTA Secretariat schedules of specific commitments in services and Guided Trade Initiative data
  6. Facilitation of access to Member State immigration entry/exit statistics, work and residence permit data, customs and small-scale cross-border trade data, and STATAFRIC labour migration statistics
  1. Consultant’s Qualifications, Experience Requirements and Team Composition

The assignment will be undertaken by a consulting firm or consortium (for example, an economics firm partnering with a survey research organisation) with demonstrated expertise in conducting research on migration, regional integration, economic analysis, free movement of persons, and public perception research. The firm should meet the following requirements:

A. Firm Qualifications and Experience

  • Proven track record (minimum 10 years) in conducting research on migration, mobility, labour movement, or regional integration in Africa
  • Demonstrated experience in public perception studies, socio-economic research, or political economy analysis
  • Experience in delivering policy-oriented research and advisory services to governments, regional organizations, or international institution
  • Proven ability to conduct multi-country and comparative studies
  • Demonstrated experience in quantitative impact assessment (gravity, computable general equilibrium or micro-simulation modelling) and in survey-based or experimental perception research

B. Key Experts (Team Composition)

The firm is expected to propose a multidisciplinary team including, at a minimum:

1. Team Leader / Lead Expert

  • Advanced degree (master’s or PhD) in migration studies, economics, political science, international relations, or related field
  • At least 10 years of relevant experience
  • Proven experience leading similar regional or continental studies
  • Strong expertise in migration governance, regional integration, and policy analysis

2.  Public Perception/Social Development Research Expert

  • Advanced degree in sociology, political science, or related field
  • At least 7 years of experience in public perception or behavioral research
  • Experience in survey design, qualitative analysis, and socio-political assessments

3. Economist - Labour Mobility / Economic Integration Expert

  • Advanced degree in economics, labour economics, or related field
  • At least 7 years of experience in labour mobility, trade in services, or AfCFTA-related work

4. Data Analyst / Statistician

  • Degree in statistics, data science, economics, or related field
  • At least 5 years of experience in quantitative and qualitative data analysis

5. Quantitative Modeller (Trade and Migration)

  • Advanced degree in economics or a quantitative discipline
  • At least 7 years of experience in gravity, computable general equilibrium or micro-simulation modelling of trade or migration, with published or client-delivered applications

6. Strategic Communications Expert

  • Advanced degree in communications, public policy or a related field
  • At least 7 years of experience in evidence-based public communication, message testing and advocacy campaigns, preferably with AU, REC or national institutions

7. Legal and Institutional Expert (part-time)

  • Expertise in AU and REC legal frameworks on free movement, trade in services and air transport (Yamoussoukro Decision and SAATM)

C. Additional Competencies

  • Strong analytical and report-writing skills
  • Experience working with AU institutions, RECs, or similar regional bodies is an added advantage
  • Ability to deliver high-quality outputs within tight timelines
  • Working proficiency in French is required within the team; Arabic and Portuguese are an advantage. Deliverables shall be produced in English and French, with executive summaries and policy briefs also in Arabic and Portuguese
  1. Clients Assignment Management Arrangement

The assignment will be managed by the African Union Commission (Department of Health, Humanitarian Affairs and Social Development) in coordination with relevant divisions. A Steering Committee comprising the Department of Health, Humanitarian Affairs and Social Development, the Department of Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry and Minerals, the AfCFTA Secretariat, AFCAC and the World Bank (as financier under BIASHARA) will provide technical oversight; the AUC and the World Bank will provide consolidated comments on each deliverable within ten working days of submission.

  • The consulting firm will report to the designated AU focal point
  • All deliverables will be subject to review and approval by the AUC, following technical review by the Steering Committee and the World Bank
  • Regular progress updates will be required
  • Validation meetings may be organized to review draft findings
  • Payment milestones will be linked to the acceptance of the inception report, the interim report, the final report and the final policy package
  • The AUC will own the data, models and outputs; the consultant shall deliver them in editable and reproducible formats

Projet de Développement de la Capacité Statistique Pour Améliorer la Prise de Décision « DECIDE »

 

Recrutement d’un(e) Coordonnateur(trice) Adjoint(e)

 

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

N° 02/ZR-MINPLAN-576296-CS-INDV/DECIDE/2026

 

Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC) a adressé à la Banque Mondiale une requête relative au financement du Projet de Développement de la Capacité Statistique pour Améliorer la Prise de Décision (DECIDE) et à l’intention d’utiliser une partie du financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché de recrutement d’un(e) Coordonnateur(trice) Adjoint(e).

L’objectif est d’assurer sous l’autorité du Coordonnateur de l’UGP, le leadership opérationnel de la coordination et de la mise en œuvre du projet DECIDE, en garantissant la réalisation dans les délais impartis de l’objectif de développement du projet DECIDE, conformément à son accord de financement, à son document d’évaluation, à son manuel des opérations, aux exigences fiduciaires, environnementales, sociales et de reporting de la Banque mondiale, ainsi qu’au plan de travail et budget annuel approuvé. 

Sous l’autorité du Coordonnateur, il est chargé, pour le projet DECIDE, des tâches spécifiques ci-après :

  • Coordonner la mise en œuvre et le suivi des activités du projet DECIDE ;
  • Assurer la représentation du projet DECIDE vis-à-vis des instances internes et externes ainsi que des tiers ;
  • Appuyer le Ministère du Plan et de la Coordination de l’Aide au Développement dans le cadrage administratif, juridique et institutionnel du projet DECIDE ;
  • Assurer la gestion de fonds, de moyens humains et matériels mis à la disposition de l’UGP par le Gouvernement et les bailleurs de fonds pour l’exécution du projet DECIDE ;
  • Elaborer les Plans de Travail et Budget Annuel du projet DECIDE dans les délais prescrits ;
  • Veiller à la qualité des relations avec les bailleurs de fonds et au respect des procédures ;
  • Assurer l'intérim du Coordonnateur au sein de la Commission de passation des marchés, pour les marchés du projet DECIDE, en cas d'absence ou d'empêchement de celui-ci, dans le respect des règles de prévention des conflits d'intérêts du Règlement de passation des marchés et des Directives anticorruption ;
  • Suivre les travaux des commissions d’analyse et de coordination en liaison avec la commission des marchés ;
  • Assurer le suivi général de la qualité, des délais et des budgets de l’exécution du projet DECIDE ;
  • Etablir les mécanismes étroits de coordination avec les entités de mise en œuvre du projet DECIDE (INS, BCR, CAID, FNUAP) et les entités bénéficiaires ;
  • Préparer les réunions du Comité de Pilotage du projet DECIDE et suivre la mise en œuvre de leurs recommandations ;
  • Préparer les missions de supervision, de revue des portefeuilles et de dialogue des bailleurs de fonds et suivre la mise en œuvre des recommandations ;
  • Assurer le suivi de la mise en œuvre du plan de contingence du RGPH2, notamment le suivi des mesures d’atténuation, des responsabilités, des échéances et des principaux risques, en coordination avec l’INS, le BCR et les autres parties prenantes concernées ;
  • Assurer le suivi de l’exécution financière du projet DECIDE, avec pour objectif un taux de décaissement annuel d’au moins 25 % ;
  • Promouvoir et contribuer à garantir un environnement de travail collégial, respectueux, inclusif et sûr pour l’ensemble des membres de l’UGP, notamment à travers la prévention et le traitement approprié de toute forme de harcèlement ou de comportement inapproprié, en complément des dispositions relatives au code de conduite et à la prévention de l’EAS/HS.

Les Termes de Reference (TDR) et le modèle de CV sont joints à cette demande de manifestation d'intérêt de la mission ou peuvent être trouvés sur le site web suivant : https://www.cepo.cd/.

La CEP-O invite les candidats intéressés à présenter leur candidature en vue de fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les consultants intéressés doivent produire les informations sur leur capacité et expérience (lettre de motivation datée et signée, curriculum vitae suivant le modèle à télécharger, attestations de service rendu ou tout autre document faisant foi de l’expérience acquise, copies légalisées du ou des diplômes par les autorités compétentes et autres supports) démontrant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour les prestations.

Les critères de qualification sont les suivants :

SADC SECRETARIAT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY:                             Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT:            SADC REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:            INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANCY TO ASSESS AND IMPLEMENT TISSTAT FOR TRADE IN SERVICES DATA PERTAINING TO STATISTICAL DATA OF 2 MEMBER STATES IN SADC REGION. BW-SADC-563174-CS-INDV

 

 

REFERENCE NUMBER: SADC/5/2/478

 

DATE OF ISSUE: 17 November 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the SADC Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

 

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services to assess and implement TISSAT for Trade in service data pertaining to statistical data of 2 member states in SADC region in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

 

The SADC Secretariate invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested individual consultants to conduct the training, recruited as individual consultants following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title                 :  Individual Consultant to assess and implement TISSAT for Trade in service data pertaining to statistical data of 2 member states in SADC region (1 Position)

 

Accountable:  Senior Officer, Research and Statistics 

 

Duration of Assignment:  8 months

 

  1. The Objectives of the Assignment

 

The overall objective of this exercise is to capacitate two Member States in the region towards production of disaggregated trade in services (TIS) statistics to support regional integration priorities on trade policies.

 

  1. Specific objectives

 

The specific objective of this assignment is to undertake a comprehensive scoping and assessment exercise within the respective national statistical systems (NSSs) of 2 Member States and to implement TISSTAT tool for production and dissemination of detailed TIS statistics in one Member State.

 

  1. Expected results

 

The consultant is expected to achieve the following results in the following chronological order:

  • Scoping and Assessment Reports for 2 Member States (one for each) on statistical and institutional matters; and
  • Findings Report of TISSTAT in one Member State for collection of TIS statistics based on pilot exercise pertaining to statistical matters.

 

 

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

 

This assignment is expected to be carried out by a consultant with in-depth knowledge in trade in services statistics and TISSTAT tool management.  The specific profile is provided below:

Qualifications and Skills

    • A minimum of a Degree in statistics, economics or related field. A Masters degree and above shall be an advantage.

 

General Professional Experience

    • The Consultant must have at least 15 years of specific experience in production and dissemination in economic statistics, in particular on external sector statistics such as Balance of Payments and TIS statistics.

 

Specific Professional Experience

    • Demonstrated experience of doing a scoping and assessment of countries for implementation of TISSTAT on statistics and institutional factors in at least 2 countries;
    • Demonstrated experience in providing training to developing countries on TISSTAT tool pertaining to core statistical matters in at least 2 countries; and
    • Demonstrated experience in implementation of TISSTAT tool with validated results in at least 2 countries as technical assistance.

 

  1. Duration of the assignment

 

The Individual Consultant will be recruited for 8 months. Note: the 8 months is the duration of the assignment and not the number of days required to undertake it. It caters for coordination of work to be done by recipients of the assignment and to a certain extent, flexibility for the consultant to deliver on the outputs.

 

  1. Facilities to be provided by the Client

 

For the expert working on this consultancy, the Contracting Authority shall facilitate visa entry in the member states hosting the workshop, if required.

 

  1. Location of Employment

 

The assignment will involve traveling to 2 Member States and shall also be done remotely by the Consultant.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

  1. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

  1. Mode of Application

 

Interested Individuals Consultants meeting the stated requirements should submit their Expressions of interest including updated detailed curriculum vitae (CVs) and copies of professional certificates must be delivered in a written form using a drag and drop electronic tender box by Friday, 4th December 2026 on or before 00:00 hours, Botswana local time. No public opening will be held.

Kindly note that only highly technically scored bidder will be contacted for negotiations meeting.

Your Technical proposal should be valid for a period of 120 days from the date of deadline for submission.

SADC SECRETARIAT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY:                       Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT:                 SADC REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:       INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANCY TO ASSESS AND IMPLEMENT TiSSTAT FOR TRADE IN SERVICES PERTAINING TO INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) OF 2 MEMBER STATES IN SADC REGION. BW-SADC-563160-CS-INDV

 

 

REFERENCE NUMBER: SADC/5/2/479

 

DATE OF ISSUE: 17 November 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the SADC Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

 

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services to assess and implement TiSSTAT for Trade in services pertaining to information technology (IT) of 2 member states in SADC region in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

 

The SADC Secretariate invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested individual consultants to conduct the training, recruited as individual consultants following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title             :  Individual Consultant to assess and implement TiSSTAT for Trade in services pertaining to information technology (IT) of 2 member states in SADC region (1 Position)

 

Accountable:  Senior Officer, Research and Statistics 

 

Duration of Assignment:  7 months

 

  1. The Objectives of the Assignment

 

The overall objective of this exercise is to capacitate two Member States in the region towards production of disaggregated trade in services (TIS) statistics to support regional integration priorities on trade policies.

 

  1. Specific objectives

 

The specific objective of this assignment is to undertake a comprehensive scoping and assessment exercise pertaining to IT within the respective national statistical systems (NSSs) of 2 Member States and to support as IT expert for pilot implementation of the TISSTAT tool for production and dissemination of detailed TIS statistics in 1 Member State.

 

  1. Expected results

 

The consultant is expected to achieve the following results in the following chronological order:

  1. Scoping and Assessment Reports for 2 Member States (one for each) on IT matters describing the readiness of each Member State assessed against agreed criteria.
  2. Findings Report of TiSSTAT in one Member State for collection of TIS statistics based on pilot exercise pertaining to IT matters and TiSSTAT installed and technically operational in one Member State. Designated users trained and able to perform assigned functions.

 

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

 

This assignment is expected to be carried out by a consultant with in-depth knowledge in TISSTAT IT tool deployment and management.  The specific profile is provided below:

 

Qualifications and Skills

    • A minimum of a Degree in IT or related field. A Masters degree and above shall be an advantage.

 

General Professional Experience

    • The Consultant must have at least 10 years of specific experience in IT development.

 

Specific Professional Experience

    • Demonstrated experience of doing a scoping and assessment of countries for implementation of TISSTAT on IT  factors in at least 2 countries;
    • Demonstrated experience in providing training to developing countries on TISSTAT tool pertaining to IT matters in at least 2 countries; and
    • Demonstrated experience in implementation of TISSTAT tool with validated results in at least 2 countries as technical assistance.

 

 

  1. Duration of the assignment

 

The Individual Consultant will be recruited for 7 months. Note: the 7 months is the duration of the assignment and not the number of days required to undertake it. It caters for coordination of work to be done by recipients of the assignment and to a certain extent, flexibility for the consultant to deliver on the outputs.

 

  1. Facilities to be provided by the Client

 

For the expert working on this consultancy, the Contracting Authority shall facilitate visa entry in the member states hosting the workshop, if required.

 

  1. Location of Employment

 

The assignment will involve traveling to 2 Member States and shall also be done remotely by the Consultant.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

  1. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

  1. Mode of Application

 

Interested Individuals Consultants meeting the stated requirements should submit their Expressions of interest including updated detailed curriculum vitae (CVs) and copies of professional certificates must be delivered in a written form using a drag and drop electronic tender box by Friday, 4th December 2026 on or before 00:00 hours, Botswana local time. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA

LOWLANDS LIVELIHOOD RESILIENCE PROJECT – PHASE II (LLRP-II)

Credit No.: 7519-ET

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Route Selection and Survey, Feasibility Study, Detailed Engineering Design, ESIA and Tender Document Preparation for a Package of Six (6) Gravel Access Roads and Four (4) Medium Span Bridges in Hararey, El-Ogaden, Dambal, Mubarek, Shilabo, Guradamole, Aware, Qubi, Hadagala and Hamaro Woredas, Somali Regional State

Reference No.: ET-SOM-RPCU-570309-CS-QCBS

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank toward the cost of the Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project – Phase II (LLRP-II), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include route selection and survey, feasibility study, detailed engineering design, Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and preparation of tender documents for six (6) gravel access roads and four (4) medium span bridges in Somali Regional State, as follows: Gravel access roads: (1) Duhun–Garasley–Hararey (49 km), Hararey Woreda, Nogob Zone; (2) Adaley–El-Ogaden (23 km), El-Ogaden Woreda, Korahey Zone; (3) Dulcad–Dambal–Araabi (35 km), Dambal Woreda, Siti Zone; (4) Kukubanya–Buurfuley (50 km), Mubarek Woreda, Dawa Zone; (5) Shilabo–Higloley (50 km), Shilabo Woreda, Korahey Zone; and (6) Berdo–Adeley (15 km), Guradamole Woreda, Liban Zone (total about 222 km). Medium span bridges: (7) Falfal Bridge (120 m), Aware Woreda, Jarar Zone; (8) Erer River Bridge (80 m), Qubi Woreda, Erer Zone; (9) Habaqo Bridge (65 m), Hadagala Woreda, Siti Zone; and (10) Af-dhagah Bridge (70 m), Hamaro Woreda, Erer Zone.

The Services will be carried out in two phases, following the latest Ethiopian Roads Administration (ERA) design manuals, standard specifications and Quality Manual, the LLRP-II environmental and social instruments (ESMF, RF, SEP, SA, LMP and GBV Action Plan), the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and the World Bank Environmental, Health and Safety (EHS) Guidelines:

(a)  Phase I – Route Selection and Survey, and Feasibility Study: identification and comparison of at least three alternative routes in technical, economic, environmental, social and strategic terms; site reconnaissance and investigation; stakeholder consultation; classified traffic counts and axle load surveys; full topographic survey and 3D Digital Terrain Model; preliminary design; ESIA of the selected route; preliminary cost estimates (80–85% accuracy) and preliminary bill of quantities; and economic evaluation (EIRR, NPV and sensitivity analysis, using HDM-4 or a similar package).

(b)  Phase II – Detailed Engineering Design, ESIA and Preparation of Bidding Documents: materials and site investigation; geometric, drainage, pavement, geotechnical and bridge/structural design; road safety design and audit, including “Green Road” measures; utilities, private accesses and right-of-way demarcation; climate and natural hazard vulnerability assessment and climate-resilient design; risk assessment; estimate of the construction contract period; final ESIA and Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP); and preparation of bidding documents based on the World Bank Standard Procurement Documents, including technical specifications, drawings, bills of quantities and the Engineer’s cost estimate.

The implementation period is three (3) months from the date of commencement, and the assignment is expected to start in December 2026.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Somali Regional State, Office of the President, Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP-II) Regional Project Coordination Unit now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

(a)  Core business and years in business: the firm’s core business shall be in road/highway engineering consultancy services. Provide the company profile, certificate of registration and number of years in business.

(b)  General experience: experience in civil engineering consultancy services (studies, design and/or construction supervision of roads, bridges or other civil infrastructure) during the last ten (10) years.

(c)  Specific experience: experience in assignments of similar nature and complexity, i.e. route selection, feasibility studies and detailed engineering design of roads (new construction, rehabilitation or upgrading, including gravel/low-volume roads) and of bridges (medium span bridges and major drainage structures), covering topographic surveys, traffic and economic evaluation, hydrology and drainage, geotechnical and structural design, ESIA and preparation of bidding documents, preferably in arid, semi-arid or pastoral lowland areas and under projects financed by the World Bank or other international development partners. For each assignment, indicate the client, location, road length and/or bridge span, contract value, duration, scope of services and the firm’s role, supported by contract or completion certificates.

(d) Technical and managerial capability of the firm: organizational structure, survey equipment (e.g. survey-grade GPS and total stations), access to soil, materials and geotechnical testing laboratories, road design software (e.g. MX Road, InRoads or Eagle Point), hydrological and structural analysis software, economic evaluation software (e.g. HDM-4), quality assurance systems, and capacity to mobilize multidisciplinary field teams to remote and geographically dispersed areas of Somali Region.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.
