REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

 

Country: Lebanon

Project Name: GFPP for Lebanon Digital Acceleration Project (LDAP)

GFPP Grant No.: TF0C8895

Project No.: P181954

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Development of a Government Cloud Policy Framework for Lebanon

Reference No.: LB-OMSAR-537761-CS-INDV

The Republic of Lebanon represented by the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform (OMSAR) has received a Grant (# TF0C8895) from the World Bank’s Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this grant for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include establishing the foundations of Lebanon's government cloud policy framework through three connected outputs: (i) a Statement of Policy Principles, grounded in international good practice and validated with Lebanese stakeholders; (ii) a draft Government Cloud Policy, prepared as a binding policy instrument in a form suitable for formal adoption; and (iii) a Cloud Policy Framework Architecture and Institutional Responsibility Matrix that position the Policy within the wider framework, assign ownership of each element, and identify the follow-on workstreams required to complete it.. The assignment is expected to be completed in approximately 14 weeks from the Contract’s Commencement Date.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest – Annex I.

The Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform (OMSAR) now invites eligible individual consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide:

  1. A curriculum vitae (CV) demonstrating the required qualifications and relevant experience, and
  2. A brief Methodology and Work Plan (not exceeding 5 pages) outlining the proposed technical approach and logical sequencing of activities to fulfil the scope of work.

Minimum Qualifications and Experience

The Consultant must meet the following minimum requirements:

  • An advanced degree in public policy, law, ICT, digital government, information systems, or a related field;
  • At least ten (10) years of professional experience in digital government, digital transformation, ICT policy, or cloud strategy and governance;
  • Demonstrated experience drafting government cloud policies or comparable binding digital-government policy instruments (e.g., policies, directives, decrees, or regulations) that were subsequently adopted by a government or public institution;
  • Demonstrated comparative knowledge of government digital policy frameworks across multiple jurisdictions, including their approaches to relevant areas such as data classification, security standards, provider assurance, and enforcement.
  • Good familiarity with public financial management, public budgeting, and public procurement, preferably in Lebanon;
  • Experience working in developing countries and/or fragile and conflict-affected contexts is desirable; experience in the Middle East and North Africa region is an advantage;
  • Oral and written proficiency and ability to draft policy instruments in either English or Arabic; knowledge of both languages is an advantage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (September 2025) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (09:00 AM to 04:00 PM Beirut Time).

Expressions of interest (including CV and a methodology/work plan not exceeding 5 pages) must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by COB December 4, 2026.

Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform (OMSAR)

Technical Unit – Preparation Grant for Lebanon Digital Acceleration Project

Attn: Ms. Mirvat Hammoud – Procurement Specialist

Omar Daouk Street, Mina El Hosn Sector,

STARCO Building, Bloc A, 5th Floor, Room 505a

Beirut, Lebanon

Tel: +961 (1) 371 505; ext. 160

E-mail: mhammoud@omsar.gov.lb

 

Annex I

 

Terms of Reference

PREPARATION GRANT FOR LEBANON DIGITAL ACCELERATION PROJECT (P181954)

Consultancy Services for the Development of a
Government Cloud Policy Framework for Lebanon

1. Background

Lebanon is facing a protracted, multidimensional crisis that has impaired state institutions and public service delivery. Fragmented digital systems, reliance on paper-based processes, and limited trust in electronic transactions continue to hinder efficiency, transparency, and accountability across the public and private sectors. These challenges are compounded by gaps in digital governance, incomplete regulatory activation, and limited institutional capacity to operationalize key digital enablers.

In response, the Government of Lebanon, with support from the World Bank, is undertaking a strategic investment aimed to modernize Lebanon's public sector through digital transformation, stimulate private sector growth, and accelerate the development of a robust digital economy. The Lebanon Digital Acceleration Project (the “Project”) will establish secure, scalable, and resilient digital infrastructure including cloud services, data platforms, and cybersecurity systems that are essential for attracting investment and fostering innovation. By strengthening digital ID, e-signature capabilities, and the legal framework for digital transactions, the Project will improve the ease of doing business and enable trusted, efficient engagement between the public and private sectors. In parallel, the Project will advance key regulatory reforms in telecom, data protection, cybersecurity, e-signature, artificial intelligence (AI) and other areas, while investing in Lebanon's digital talent pool. Together, these measures will lay the foundation for a more competitive, dynamic, and inclusive economy.

The World Bank's Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) has been extended to the Government of Lebanon to support early implementation of the Project. The GFPP grant is being implemented by a Technical Unit (TU) housed within OMSAR.

An important enabler of digital government transformation is the adoption of modern, secure, resilient, and cost-effective cloud technologies to support the delivery of digital public services and the modernization of government ICT environments. Realizing the benefits of cloud computing requires a coherent policy framework that provides clear governance arrangements, establishes common principles and requirements, guides cloud adoption decisions, and promotes consistent approaches to cloud service acquisition, management, security, and oversight across government entities.

In Lebanon, digital transformation initiatives have progressed across multiple institutions and sectors. However, infrastructure environments, hosting arrangements, and cloud adoption practices remain fragmented, with varying levels of maturity across public institutions. Government entities continue to rely on diverse hosting models, legacy infrastructure, and institution-specific approaches to technology management, resulting in inefficiencies, duplication of investments, and challenges in achieving interoperability, scalability, resilience, and effective cybersecurity management.

In 2024, the World Bank provided to the Government of Lebanon Technical Assistance that reviewed Lebanon's data hosting ecosystem and developed recommendations for a government cloud and data hosting strategy, covering aspects related to governance, legal and institutional frameworks, cloud deployment models, cybersecurity, data classification, migration planning, procurement, and implementation priorities (the 2024 Assessment).

In addition, in June 2026, a project aiming to develop a National Data Classification Policy Framework has been launched under the GFPP grant and is ongoing. Other ongoing assignments under the GFPP grant include an assessment of the legal, regulatory, policy, institutional, and governance framework relevant to digital transformation, including cloud adoption, cloud service management, and data hosting across government (“Cloud Framework Assessment”); as well as a technical assessment of the current state of data hosting and cloud readiness in government, across a sample of representative ministries (“Data Hosting Assessment”). In parallel, complementary reform workstreams are underway or planned in related areas, including the revision of Lebanon's legal framework for personal data protection.

International experience shows that a mature government cloud policy framework is not a single document but a family of complementary artifacts and governance mechanisms, including, depending on the jurisdiction, elements such as a cloud strategy; a cloud policy; a data classification scheme; associated security controls; standards and assurance arrangements for cloud service providers; specialized procurement vehicles and public financial management arrangements; non-binding implementation guidance; and/or dedicated private or community cloud environments dedicated to public sector users.

This assignment is deliberately scoped as a first phase in the elaboration of such a holistic cloud policy framework: it will deliver the foundational elements of the eventual policy framework alongside a clear mapping of the remaining elements to be developed under parallel and follow-on workstreams.

2. Objective of the Assignment

In this context, the TU at OMSAR intends to recruit a qualified Individual Consultant to establish the foundations of Lebanon's government cloud policy framework through three connected outputs: (i) a Statement of Policy Principles, grounded in international good practice and validated with Lebanese stakeholders; (ii) a draft Government Cloud Policy, prepared as a binding policy instrument in a form suitable for formal adoption; and (iii) a Cloud Policy Framework Architecture and Institutional Responsibility Matrix that position the Policy within the wider framework, assign ownership of each element, and identify the follow-on workstreams required to complete it. Specifically, the Individual Consultant will:

  • Conduct an international benchmarking of government cloud policy frameworks and distill a concise Statement of Policy Principles relevant to the Lebanese context, to be validated with key stakeholders;
  • Draft the Government Cloud Policy in a form suitable for formal adoption by the Government of Lebanon as a binding policy instrument; and
  • Map the target architecture for the wider Cloud Policy Framework, including its constitutive elements and the institutional responsibilities required to implement and maintain them, while identifying dependencies on existing framework elements and defining  implementation roadmap for parallel and follow-on work needed to complete framework development.

This assignment shall take into account and, when relevant, build on previous and parallel policy work and related technical assistance, which will be provided to the Consultant by OMSAR, including the 2024 Assessment, ongoing work to define the National Data Classification Policy Framework as well as analytical work related to data hosting and cloud computing. Throughout the assignment and its phases, continuous and iterative consultations with relevant stakeholders shall be conducted.

3. Detailed Scope of Work and Deliverables

The Consultant shall undertake the following activities:

Phase 1: Inception

The Consultant shall:

  • Conduct kickoff meetings with OMSAR and relevant stakeholders;
  • Review the outputs of previous and ongoing assignments and other relevant documents; and
  • Prepare the methodology, work plan, and stakeholder engagement plan for all phases of the assignment, and validate these with OMSAR.

Deliverable D1: Inception Report, including methodology, work plan, and stakeholder engagement plan.

Phase 2: International Benchmarking and Statement of Policy Principles

The Consultant shall conduct a structured comparative review of government cloud policy frameworks in a sample of relevant jurisdictions, selected to reflect a range of regions, income levels, and institutional capacities, with an eye to integrating approaches and perspectives that could be relevant to the Lebanese context. The review shall cover, at a minimum, the following dimensions:

  • The scope of application of the cloud policies and their framing, e.g. cloud-preference-based framings such as “cloud first” versus structured-choice framings such as “cloud smart”;
  • The types of policy instruments and related artifacts making up the cloud policy framework, their legal basis, and the institutional governance arrangements for their issuance, maintenance and enforcement;
  • The linkage between cloud policy and ancillary policy instruments such as national data classification schemes, data protection legislation, cybersecurity frameworks, and any inherited constraints and security controls that apply;
  • Approaches to defining standards, requirements and security controls;
  • Assurance arrangements for cloud service providers, including who assesses standards compliance, what evidence is required, who takes the resulting decision, and how that evidence is kept current;
  • Enforcement models, such as spend controls and similar enforcement mechanisms, alongside their institutional prerequisites, and strengths and weaknesses of different approaches;
  • Procurement enablers, such as framework agreements, central brokers, and cloud marketplaces;
  • Administrative and financial enablers, such as budgetary treatment of operational and consumption-based expenditure, multi-year commitments, payments in foreign currency, and potential billing arrangements between public entities;
  • Institutional enablers, including the mandates, business units, and technical capacities on which each model depends; and
  • The role of government-specific private or community cloud infrastructures alongside commercial cloud infrastructures as part of a hybrid cloud adoption model.

For each dimension, the Consultant shall assess applicability to Lebanon's legal, institutional, technical, fiscal, and market context, drawing on the 2024 Assessment, the Cloud Framework Assessment, and the Data Hosting Assessment rather than repeating them, and shall identify which enforcement and compliance mechanisms are realistically available to the Government in the short term under existing mandates, processes, and capacities, as distinct from those requiring new legal authority, institutions, or sustained technical capability.

On the basis of this review, the Consultant shall prepare a Statement of Policy Principles: a concise (two to three pages) statement of policy intent setting out the high-level orientations proposed to govern cloud adoption in Lebanon. Each principle shall be a clear, affirmative statement of policy direction, traceable to the benchmarking findings, and formulated at a level of generality that allows stakeholders to align on it before detailed drafting begins. The Statement of Policy Principles precedes, and will guide, the drafting of the Government Cloud Policy under Phase 3; it is not itself a binding instrument. The Consultant shall present the draft Statement to relevant stakeholders and revise it to reflect the feedback received.

Deliverable D2: International Benchmarking Report and validated Statement of Policy Principles.

Phase 3: Government Cloud Policy and Framework Architecture

The Consultant shall prepare a coherent package of three artifacts, drafted so as to be suitable for validation with stakeholders and, should the Government so decide, submission to the Council of Ministers for approval and issuance:

3.1 Draft Government Cloud Policy. A binding policy instrument giving effect to the validated Statement of Policy Principles. The Policy shall include those elements identified as relevant in the international review of best practice and validated in the Principles, and shall include at least:

  • Prefatory text (preamble or recitals) recording the purpose, context, and drafting intent of the Policy;
  • The scope of application, specifying the government entities, systems, and workloads covered;
  • The nature and orientation of the obligations created and any linkages to the national data classification framework;
  • The cloud deployment and service models permitted, relying on internationally recognized definitions;
  • Security and assurance requirements established, including any references to recognized international standards and certification schemes;
  • Exception handling mechanisms to deal with policy waivers, specifying who decides, on what evidence and criteria, on what authority, etc.;
  • Governance, oversight, and reporting obligations of government entities; and
  • Transitional provisions.

The Consultant shall also recommend the legal or administrative instrument through which the Policy should be issued (e.g., a decree) and the competent issuing authority. The Consultant may rely on complementary legal analyses conducted under parallel workstreams in doing so.

3.2 Cloud Policy Framework Architecture. Definition and mapping of the complete target cloud policy framework for Lebanon, including the Cloud Policy itself but also including other complementary artifacts and elements required to ensure its effective implementation, with a descript of each element and its role in the framework, showing how the Cloud Policy relates to, depends on, relies on, or informs each element. Each element in the architecture shall be classified according to whether it already exists, requires revision, is being developed in a parallel workstream, or is flagged for future development work. The Framework Architecture shall include a matrix or matrices mapping dependencies and complementarities between framework elements, including between legal, institutional and policy elements as well as other constituent artifacts.

Deliverable D3: Government Cloud Policy and Cloud Policy Framework Architecture, validated with relevant stakeholders.

Phase 4: Implementation Roadmap and Final Presentation

The Consultant shall prepare the following

  • 4.1 Institutional Roles and Responsibility Matrix. A matrix assigning each element and function of the framework (for example aspects related to standards, provider assurance, supervision, enforcement, procurement, and other areas as relevant) to existing or future institution(s), identifying where existing capacities suffice and where new or additional institutional mandates, units, or capabilities would be required.
  • 4.2 Implementation Roadmap. Prepare a sequenced Implementation Roadmap for the follow-on workstreams identified in the Framework Architecture (for example: selection and adoption of security standards and the mapping of controls to classification tiers; operationalization of provider assurance arrangements; design of procurement vehicles; development of implementation guidance; and migration planning support), specifying for each workstream an outline of scope, dependencies, indicative duration, and suggested institutional owner, in sufficient detail to inform the preparation of future terms of reference; and
  • 4.3 Final Presentation. Deliver a presentation slick deck, in PowerPoint format, to relevant government stakeholders summarizing methodology, findings, deliverables, and recommendations.

Deliverable D4: Implementation Roadmap, Institutional Roles and Responsibilities Matrix, and Final Presentation, validated with relevant stakeholders.

4. Duration of the Assignment

The duration of the assignment shall be approximately fourteen (14) weeks from the Commencement Date. The Commencement Date shall be the contract signature date or the date of a written notice to proceed issued by OMSAR, as specified in the contract.

5. Consultant Qualifications

The Individual Consultant shall demonstrate the following qualifications:

  • An advanced degree in public policy, law, ICT, digital government, information systems, or a related field;
  • At least ten (10) years of professional experience in digital government, digital transformation, ICT policy, or cloud strategy and governance;
  • Demonstrated experience drafting government cloud policies or comparable binding digital-government policy instruments (e.g., policies, directives, decrees, or regulations) that were subsequently adopted by a government or public institution;
  • Demonstrated comparative knowledge of government digital policy frameworks across multiple jurisdictions, including their approaches to relevant areas such as data classification, security standards, provider assurance, and enforcement.
  • Good familiarity with public financial management, public budgeting, and public procurement, preferably in Lebanon;
  • Experience working in developing countries and/or fragile and conflict-affected contexts is desirable; experience in the Middle East and North Africa region is an advantage;
  • Oral and written proficiency and ability to draft policy instruments in either English or Arabic; knowledge of both languages is an advantage.

6. Compliance Requirements

The selected Consultant must adhere to all applicable World Bank regulations and guidelines, including but not limited to the World Bank's Guidelines on Preventing and Combating Fraud and Corruption in Projects Financed by IBRD Loans and IDA Credits and Grants, and must disclose any actual or potential Conflict of Interest (COI).

In addition, the Consultant must comply with the following Environmental and Social (E&S) requirements aligned with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and the Lebanon Digital Acceleration Project (LDAP) commitments:

1. Code of Conduct (CoC)

The Consultant must sign and follow a CoC covering data confidentiality, respectful conduct, non-discrimination, and zero tolerance for SEA/SH.

2. Labor and Working Conditions

The Consultant shall perform the assignment in accordance with applicable labor and working condition requirements under the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESS2), including maintaining safe and healthy working practices, professional conduct, and respect for applicable occupational health and safety standards.

The Consultant shall have access to the Project's Grievance Mechanism for raising any work-related concerns or complaints arising during the assignment.

3. Data Security, Privacy, and Cybersecurity

All data handled under this assignment must be securely stored, accessed only by authorized staff, and managed using privacy-by-design and cybersecurity best practices. Any data breach must be immediately reported.

4. Stakeholder Engagement and Grievance Redress

Any targeted technical consultations conducted as part of policy development shall inform participants about the Project's Grievance Mechanism and how complaints can be submitted.

5. SEA/SH Prevention

The Consultant shall comply with zero-tolerance requirements for SEA/SH and adhere to appropriate professional conduct and reporting procedures when engaging with stakeholders, in line with the Project's CoC and World Bank requirements.

6. Environmental Considerations for ICT (ESS3)

Any ICT equipment or data storage devices used must be managed responsibly, including secure data wiping and environmentally sound disposal.

7. Deliverables and Payment Schedule

The engagement will be completed in approximately fourteen (14) weeks from the Commencement Date, with key phases and deliverables structured as follows. Weeks are expressed in terms of time after the Commencement Date:

Commencement and Payment Terms:

  • Commencement Date: The Commencement Date shall be the contract signature date or the notification date (written notice to proceed) issued by OMSAR to start the assignment.
  • Invoice Requirements: Each payment will need to include an official invoice along with the formally accepted deliverable.
  • Payment Date: Payments will be processed within thirty (30) days after the submission of the invoice and accepted deliverable.

8. Reporting and Governance

Project Oversight and Management Structure

A Technical Working Group (TWG) will be convened by OMSAR to provide strategic direction, oversight, and effective management of the engagement. Chaired by the Grant Coordinator and composed of members from OMSAR, OMSTAI, and other relevant ministries, as applicable, the TWG serves as the primary governing body responsible for reviewing the Consultant's progress and ensuring alignment with national digital transformation goals and applicable institutional mandates.

Reporting Obligations

The Consultant will report directly to the Grant Coordinator. In addition to the contractual deliverables, the Consultant, upon request, shall participate in progress meetings with the TWG team to ensure methodological alignment.

Deliverable Acceptance and Payment Clearance

  • Deliverable Review: All deliverables listed in the TOR are subject to review by the World Bank (WB) and the TWG to ensure methodological alignment and quality, with input from all participating entities. Consolidated review comments will be communicated to the Consultant within ten (10) business days of submission of each deliverable; the delivery schedule shall be adjusted to reflect any longer review period.
  • Formal Acceptance: A deliverable is considered formally accepted upon written notice (via email or formal letter) from the Grant Coordinator, following review by the WB and the TWG, confirming that the output meets the required standards.
  • Administrative Requirements for Payment: To initiate payment processing, the Consultant shall submit an Invoice Package to the Grant Coordinator, including: the Official Invoice for the specific milestone; a copy of the written acceptance notice from the Grant Coordinator, reflecting the TWG's validation; and evidence of deliverable submission. Payments will be processed within thirty (30) days of submission of a complete Invoice Package.

Nothing in this TOR shall be construed as establishing, modifying, or superseding the legal mandates, roles, or decision-making authority of any participating public entity under applicable laws and regulations.

9. Intellectual Property & Confidentiality

Intellectual Property Rights

Confidentiality Obligation

The Consultant shall maintain strict confidentiality of all information accessed during the assignment and shall ensure that no information is shared, disclosed, or used outside the scope of this contract.

10. Technical Proposal Requirements

The Consultant shall submit a technical proposal comprising the following:

Consultant Profile and Relevant Experience

  • CV/Resume demonstrating relevant qualifications and experience;
  • Description of relevant experience in cloud computing, cloud governance, enterprise architecture, digital government, digital transformation, ICT policy, or related fields; and
  • Description of similar assignments completed within the last five (5) years involving cloud policy development, cloud governance frameworks, cloud strategy, digital government, digital infrastructure, or related advisory services, including at least one example of a binding policy instrument drafted by the Consultant.

Methodology and Work Plan

  • The proposed approach to delivering the assignment;
  • Understanding of the assignment objectives and scope;
  • Proposed methodology for the international benchmarking, policy drafting, and stakeholder consultations;
  • Work plan and implementation schedule aligned with the phases and deliverables of the assignment; and
  • Quality assurance and deliverable review arrangements.

References

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

     Kingdom of Eswatini      

 

Country: Kingdom of Eswatini

Client: Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology (MICT)

Name of Project: Digital Eswatini Project

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: P508948

Assignment Title: Consulting Services for Provision of Independent Verification Agency (IVA) Services

Reference No. SZ-MICT-581805-CS-CQS

The Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Digital Ewatini Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include independently verifying, and confirming to MICT-PIU and the World Bank, whether the evidence submitted shows that each PBC (or PBC tranche/increment, where scalable) has been achieved as claimed, so that the World Bank can authorize disbursement. The IVA shall also assess the reliability of the data submitted, flag risks to remaining PBCs early, and help the responsible entities generate audit-ready PBC evidence. The assignment will run for approximately 4.5 years, covering Period 4 results (June 2030) and the Electronic Communications Act 2013 revision (Results Framework end-date September 2030). The assignment is expected to commence by June 2027.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: (1) Firm: at least 7 years of independent verification, results-based financing verification or third-party monitoring for World Bank or other MDB-financed operations, including at least 2 assignments verifying PBCs, DLIs or similar, (2) experience verifying SOE financial or governance performance and regulatory or legislative reform milestones, preferably in telecommunications.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, amended September 2025, Seventh Edition (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: Fairness and transparency in the selection process require that Consultants, or their affiliates, competing for a Consulting assignment do not derive a competitive advantage from having provided Consulting Services related to it. To that end, the Borrower shall make available to all short-listed Consultants, together with the request for proposals document, all information that would give a Consultant a competitive advantage

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualification-Based Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 09:00 to 17:00 hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) by 4 December 2026 at 17:00 hours Local Time.

The Principal Secretary

Attn: Mr. Joshua Banda, Procurement Specialist

P.O Box 642, Office No. 203, Swazi Plaza

H100, Mbabane, Kingdom of Eswatini

Tel: +268 2404 5109/+268 7669 9318

E-mail: procurement_digitaleswatini@gov.sz, copy joshuabanda02@yahoo.co.uk, ndlangamandlabo@gov.sz, dlaminisak@gov.sz

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

1. Background

The Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini, through the Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology (MICT), is advancing the Digital Eswatini Project (P508948) with World Bank financing to expand access to, and use of, affordable broadband connectivity and digital public services. Part of the financing is linked to Performance-Based Conditions (PBCs), under which funds are disbursed against independently verified achievement of agreed milestones. The Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at MICT would like to engage an Independent Verification Agent (IVA), to verify achievement of all PBCs report its findings to MICT-PIU and the World Bank. Further details on the PBCs and the evidence sources will be provided.

2. Objective

The IVA shall independently verify, and confirm to MICT-PIU and the World Bank, whether the evidence submitted shows that each PBC (or PBC tranche/increment, where scalable) has been achieved as claimed, so that the World Bank can authorize disbursement. The IVA shall also assess the reliability of the data submitted, flag risks to remaining PBCs early, and help the responsible entities generate audit-ready PBC evidence.

3. PBCs to be Verified

The IVA shall verify the following, as defined in the Legal Agreements and the Project Implementation Manual, which prevail over these ToR in case of discrepancy for, Years 1–4, i.e., June 2027 to June 2030.

  • PBC 1 – Financial stabilization (EPTC): external actuarial assessment of pension liabilities and an approved pension transition plan.
  • PBC 2A – Business turnaround plan (EPTC): plan prepared and approved by the EPTC Board.
  • PBC 2B – Revenue increase (EPTC): 8% cumulative target over the June 2026 baseline, released in 25% increments (about 2% a year).
  • PBC 2C – Cost optimization (EPTC): 20% cumulative reduction in operating costs as a percentage of revenue from the June 2026 baseline, released in 25% increments.
  • PBC 2D – Governance and institutional reform (EPTC): (i) new technical leadership (Board advisor, key five Board positions, CEO); (ii) separation of telecom and postal accounts.
  • PBC 3A – Open access and infrastructure sharing guidelines (ESCCOM): issuance, and annual implementation compliance.
  • PBC 3B – Price glide path directive (ESCCOM): issuance, and annual implementation compliance.
  • Electronic Communications Act 2013 revision (MICT; market-reform disbursement condition under Sub-component 1.1): removal of EPTC's exclusivity in wholesale services.

4. Scope of Services and Tasks

Task 1: Inception and Methodology

  • Review the Legal Agreements, PIM and related documents to confirm definitions, baselines, targets, scales and evidence requirements for every item in Section 3; develop a verification protocol and data-request templates for each, and agree them with MICT-PIU, EPTC, ESCCOM, MICT and the World Bank;
  • Verify the baselines: EPTC's June 2026 revenue and operating cost-to-revenue ratio, and wholesale prices before the price glide path.

Task 2: PBC 1 – Pension Stabilization

  • Verify that a certified external actuarial firm completed the assessment (liabilities as of September 2025, and transition costs under pessimistic, neutral and optimistic scenarios), and review its methodology;
  • Verify the pension transition plan (timelines; payments to pensioners and active members; based on the assessment and one round of negotiations with those affected) and its approval by the EPTC Board and FSRA;
  • Monitor adherence to the plan in payments and processes: the insurer payment for pensioners and the two active-member payment phases, reporting deviations promptly.

Task 3: PBC 2A – Business Turnaround Plan

  • Verify the plan includes current and forward-looking growth and cost projections and details on management, leadership and governance, and that the EPTC Board approved it (Board minutes).

Task 4: PBCs 2B and 2C – Revenue and Cost

  • Verify EPTC's annual audited financial statements (to be audited by an international audit firm) against the June 2026 baselines, measuring revenue and operating costs (including the wage bill) on the Protocol definitions and consistently with the baseline;
  • Test the four revenue levers (new products, new fiber-to-premise customers, wholesale growth, collections) and the wage bill by sampling underlying records, and flag reclassification, one-off items, or the effect of wholesale price cuts on revenue;
  • Confirm the scale increment achieved each year and the amount due.

Task 5: PBC 2D – Governance and Institutional Reform

  • Verify leadership appointments from contract details, Board records and EPTC's organogram;
  • Verify separation of telecom and postal accounts in the audited financial statements and accounting policies.

Task 6: PBCs 3A and 3B – Regulatory Instruments

  • Verify the open access guidelines and the price glide path directive were issued by ESCCOM, gazetted and published on the ESCCOM website, and are binding on operators (a descending wholesale price schedule in the case of the glide path);
  • Verify annual implementation compliance through ESCCOM's annual reports and, for the glide path, operators' price reports year on year against the baseline and glide path steps.

Task 7: Electronic Communications Act 2013 Revision

  • Verify that the gazetted Act submitted by MICT is the public text and, in substance, removes EPTC's wholesale exclusivity as the Legal Agreement requires, and give a verification opinion to MICT-PIU and the World Bank.

Task 8: Reporting, Risk Flagging and Capacity Support

  • Issue a verification report for each PBC or tranche with a verified / partially verified / not verified opinion and an evidence log; keep a consolidated PBC tracker;
  • Issue semi-annual risk notes flagging data gaps and risks to remaining PBCs; advise EPTC, ESCCOM, MICT and the PIU on data and controls; present findings at Bank missions and Project Steering Committee meetings.

5. Deliverables and Timeline

#

Deliverable

Indicative Timing

1

Inception Report (methodology, protocols, templates, work plan) and baseline verification

Within 6 weeks of contract signing

2

Verification Report and payment-monitoring reports: PBC 1

On EPTC notification (Year 1); at each payment phase

3

Verification Reports: PBC 2A; PBC 2D (leadership, Year 1; accounts, Year 4)

On EPTC notification

4

Annual Verification Reports: PBCs 2B and 2C

Within 6 weeks of audited statements (Years 1–4)

5

Verification Reports: PBCs 3A and 3B (issuance, Year 2); annual compliance reports (to Year 4)

On ESCCOM submission; annually

6

Verification Report: Electronic Communications Act 2013 revision

On MICT submission of the gazetted Act

7

Semi-annual Progress and Risk Notes

Every 6 months

8

Final Assignment Report

Within 4 weeks of the final verification

 

6. Duration and Reporting

The assignment will run for approximately 4.5 years, covering Period 4 results (June 2030) and the Electronic Communications Act 2013 revision (Results Framework end-date September 2030), on a time-slice basis tied to EPTC's and ESCCOM's reporting calendars. The IVA reports simultaneously to MICT-PIU and the World Bank, and is contracted by the PIU under Component 3. It must remain independent of EPTC, ESCCOM and MICT.

7. Qualifications

Firm: at least 7 years of independent verification, results-based financing verification or third-party monitoring for World Bank or other MDB-financed operations, including at least 2 assignments verifying PBCs, DLIs or similar; experience verifying SOE financial or governance performance and regulatory or legislative reform milestones, preferably in telecommunications, experience in Sub-Saharan Africa or in the Southern Africa region or countries sharing the same landscape with Eswatini is required.

Key experts (alternatives may be proposed if all competencies are covered):

  • Team Leader / PBC Verification Specialist – 10+ years leading verification or performance audits for MDB-financed projects; responsible for all items. Minimum of university level qualifications, in relevant field of studies with at least seven years’ progressive working experience and at least two similar nature and complexity assignments successful completion within the last recent years. Thirty (30) indicative expert-months required.
  • Pension and Actuarial Specialist – qualified actuary experienced in defined-benefit to defined-contribution transitions and insurance transfers of pensioner liabilities; independent of the external actuarial firm (PBC 1). Minimum of university level qualifications, in relevant field of studies with at least seven years’ progressive working experience and at least two similar nature and complexity assignments successful completion within the last recent years. Twenty-Six (26) indicative expert-months required.
  • Corporate Finance / SOE Audit Specialist – professional accounting qualification (CA, CPA, ACCA) and 8+ years in financial statement and payroll analysis or SOE turnaround (PBCs 2A–2C, accounts separation). Minimum of university level qualifications, in relevant field of studies with at least seven years’ progressive working experience and at least two similar nature and complexity assignments successful completion within the last recent years. Twenty-Six (26) indicative expert-months required.
  • Governance and Institutional Specialist – SOE board and leadership appointment and institutional reform verification (PBC 2D). Minimum of university level qualifications, in relevant field of studies with at least seven years’ progressive working experience and at least two similar nature and complexity assignments successful completion within the last recent years. Twenty-Six (26) indicative expert-months required.
  • Telecommunications Regulatory and Pricing Specialist – 8+ years in telecom regulation, wholesale price regimes, and open access (PBCs 3A, 3B). Minimum of university level qualifications, in relevant field of studies with at least seven years’ progressive working experience and at least two similar nature and complexity assignments successful completion within the last recent years. Twenty-Six (26) indicative expert-months required.
  • Legal and Legislative Specialist – qualified lawyer with 8+ years in telecom/ICT law and legislative reform, able to analyse Acts, gazettes and licensing frameworks (Electronic Communications Act, PBCs 3A and 3B). Minimum of university level qualifications, in relevant field of studies with at least seven years’ progressive working experience and at least two similar nature and complexity assignments successful completion within the last recent years. Twenty-Six (26) indicative expert-months required.
  • M&E / Data Verification Specialist – data quality assurance and risk-based sampling; operator price data and the PBC tracker. Minimum of university level qualifications, in relevant field of studies with at least seven years’ progressive working experience and at least two similar nature and complexity assignments successful completion within the last recent years. Twenty-Six (26) indicative expert-months required.

One Hundred and Eighty-Six (186) total indicative expert-months will be required for this assignment.

8. Client Inputs

MICT-PIU, EPTC, ESCCOM and MICT will provide the Legal Agreements, PIM and PAD; EPTC's audited statements, Board minutes, actuarial report, transition plan and payment records, leadership contracts and organogram; ESCCOM's gazetted instruments, annual reports and operator price reports; MICT's gazetted Act; and focal points. The IVA works from its own premises with in-country missions as needed.

9. Selection

The firm will be selected by Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) under the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2025, Seventh Edition) and the Anti-Corruption Guidelines (July 1, 2016), on a time-based or output-based contract to be confirmed in the Request for Proposals.

10. Confidentiality and Independence

The IVA shall not have taken part in preparing any evidence it verifies, including the actuarial work, the business plan, the regulatory instruments or the Act, and shall not be affiliated with the external actuarial firm, EPTC's auditor, or consultants supporting ESCCOM or MICT. It shall keep EPTC and operator data confidential and disclose only to MICT-PIU, EPTC, ESCCOM, MICT and the World Bank, and shall disclose any conflict of interest before signing and promptly if one arises.

data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

Country: Republic of Kazakhstan

Partnership for Market Implementation Project

Grant No. TF0B9097                          

Assignment title:      Comprehensive climate vision (long-term and short-term) defining ETS evolution

Contract No. KZPMI-QCBS-02 (as per the Procurement Plan)

The Republic of Kazakhstan has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (“the World Bank”), acting as agency of the Partnership for Market Implementation Multi Donor Trust Fund, toward the cost of the Partnership for Market Implementation Project (“the Project”), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for consulting services to be procured under this project.

The executive agency is the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources of the Republic of Kazakhstan (MENR).

Project’s objective is to enhance Kazakhstan’s Emissions Trading System (ETS) through the design of an allowance auctioning mechanism, complementary market-stability and the Carbon Fund. These measures will strengthen Kazakhstan’s carbon pricing architecture, improve price discovery and liquidity.

MENR intends to apply a part of the proceeds for consulting services on Comprehensive climate vision (long-term and short-term) defining ETS evolution.

The objective of this assignment is to develop a set of Climate Vision options for Kazakhstan for 2030-2060, grounded in an integrated assessment of the ETS, carbon pricing, economy-wide and sectoral decarbonization pathways, climate finance and Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. The Climate Visions shall provide a coherent analytical basis for the update of Kazakhstan’s LT-LEDS (Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategies) and future NDCs (Nationally Determined Contributions), while supporting decisions on carbon-pricing reform, sector transformation, resource mobilization and investment.

The specific objectives include:

  1. Establish a common analytical and decision-making framework, building on the LT-LEDS Roadmap and existing Government modelling tools.
  2. Assess Kazakhstan’s existing climate policies, strategies, models, data and analytical gaps, and establish a common set of scenarios covering current policies, NDC achievement and 2060 carbon neutrality, with common milestone years through 2060.
  3. Develop a classification system for Kazakhstan's emitting activities by responsiveness to carbon pricing and, on this basis, develop quantified economy-wide and sectoral decarbonization pathways.
  4. Assess the performance and evolution of Kazakhstan’s ETS and broader carbon-pricing framework, including alternative options for coverage, cap trajectories, auctioning, compliance flexibility, domestic crediting and complementary carbon-pricing instruments, and develop prioritized recommendations for post-2030 evolution.
  5. Assess the potential role of Article 6.2 and 6.4 in supporting Kazakhstan’s NDC and LT-LEDS.
  6. Integrate the results of the ETS, carbon-pricing, sectoral, climate-finance and Article 6 analyses into a concise set of Climate Vision options.
  7. Develop a prioritized implementation roadmap for Climate Vision and carbon pricing.

Expected duration of assignment: 12 months from the date of Contract signing. 

Scope of services includes the following:

Task A - Baseline Assessment, Diagnostics and Scenario Framework

Task B - Development of the Climate Visions and Updated Integrated Modelling Framework

Task C – ETS Reform and Carbon Pricing

Task D - Sectoral Decarbonization Pathways, Climate Finance and Resource Mobilization

Task E - Article 6 Strategy

Task F - Climate Visions Synthesis and Final Report

The Terms of Reference for the assignment can be found at the following website https://www.gov.kz/org/ecogeo/documents/details/1102902?lang=en

The Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources of the Republic of Kazakhstan (“the Client”) now invites the eligible consulting firms (“the Consultants”) to express their interest in provision of the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (but not biographical details of individual experts).

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank policy on the conflict of interest. Consultants shall meet the eligibility requirements and shall comply with the World Bank’s policy on fraud and corruption as set forth in the Procurement Regulations, including Annex IV.

Consulting firms may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture (JV), consortium or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. The type of association must be clearly stated in the expression of interest. In case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

Consultants will be selected through the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Regulations and in accordance with the following criteria:

The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

The Consultant shall demonstrate a combination of suitable international experience and adequate subject matter and operational capacity in Kazakhstan, including qualified national expertise and the ability to provide sustained in-country coordination and stakeholder engagement throughout the assignment.

Requirements for the consultant or proposed consortium, taken as a whole:

        • at least 10 years of relevant international experience in analytical and advisory work on climate policy, long-term decarbonization, ETS or carbon pricing;
        • demonstrated experience applying energy-system and GHG-emissions models to climate-policy scenarios, with access to macroeconomic or distributional analysis capability; 
        • demonstrated experience in ETS design or reform, carbon-pricing options, sector transition and investment implications; 
        • demonstrated experience in Article 6 or international carbon markets and associated institutional, MRV, accounting or regulatory readiness; 
        • operational capacity in Kazakhstan demonstrated by the proposed team or association, including qualified national expertise and the ability to provide sustained in-country coordination, Russian/Kazakh-language engagement and stakeholder support throughout the assignment; and 
        • capacity to manage multidisciplinary workstreams, editable analytical tools, quality assurance, translation and knowledge handover. 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during business hours from 09:00 to 18:00 (Astana time).

The Expressions of Interest (EOI) should include a brief company profile, description of relevant assignments, client references where available, and information on association arrangements, if any

Expressions of interest signed by an authorized person, in PDF format must be sent to the email address kz_pmi@yahoo.com or delivered to the address below no later than 18:00 (Astana time) on December 4, 2026.

Requests for clarification may be submitted in writing to the email address indicated below.

data.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – SELECTION OF CONSULTING FIRMS)

 

 

Country: Republic of Uzbekistan

 

Implementing Agency: National Agency for Social Protection (NASP) under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan.

 

Project Name: “Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable Populations” (INSON, P504420)

 

Financing Agreement (IDA Credit No. 7555-UZ) / Grant Agreement No. TF C4589-UZ

 

Assignment Title: “Expertise in Prosthetic Devices and Rehabilitation Equipment”.

 

Package Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): UZ-INSON-CS-CQS-2.1.11.

 

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank for the implementation of the project “Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable Populations” (INSON) and intends to apply part of the proceeds towards payment for consulting services under this assignment.

 

The consulting services (the “Services”) include: analysis and revision of the Assistive Products List (APL), including classification and criteria for product selection and prioritization; development of draft and final technical requirements and specifications for priority prosthetic and orthotic devices and rehabilitation equipment, including equipment planned for procurement for rehabilitation centres; development of a short-term rental and reuse model for assistive products, including assessment of service-delivery models, financial and institutional arrangements, operational procedures, model contracts, inventory management and monitoring tools; preparation of documents and recommendations for subsequent implementation of the rental scheme, including a pilot-ready implementation package. The assignment also includes stakeholder consultations, training of 14 regional trainers (30 hours of in-person training), followed by training of 208 district-level specialists (20 hours online in two groups using a cascade model). The Terms of Reference provide for limited operational testing of the proposed pilot approach, where feasible within the assignment timeframe.

 

The overall duration of the assignment is seven (7) months. The international key experts shall spend a cumulative minimum of 40 person-days in Uzbekistan, including field visits to at least two regions.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) are available at the following link:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RJ5N9KGvqRp_M5HlMzSaoXShuIk7jk8d/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104755491226149341341&rtpof=true&sd=true

 

The National Agency for Social Protection (NASP) under the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan invites qualified consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested firms shall provide information on their institutional experience and similar completed assignments, indicating the client, country, contract value, start and completion dates, scope of services performed, and the firm’s role, as well as information demonstrating their capacity to perform the assignment. In the case of a joint venture (JV), it shall be specified which JV member performed each similar assignment cited. The criteria for the firm’s qualifications and relevant experience are as follows:

 

  • At least five (5) years of institutional experience in prosthetic and orthotic devices, rehabilitation equipment, assistive technology or rehabilitation service delivery.
  • At least two (2) assignments completed within the last ten (10) years in the above fields, carried out at national level or for an international client.
  • At least one (1) assignment completed within the last ten (10) years involving the development, revision or technical assessment of an assistive products list (APL), product selection and prioritization, or technical/quality assessment of assistive products.
  • At least one (1) assignment completed within the last ten (10) years involving rental, reuse, loan-pool arrangements, refurbishment or maintenance of assistive products, or comparable equipment service-delivery arrangements.
  • At least one (1) completed assignment involving the design and delivery of a structured training/capacity-building programme in two or more locations.
  • Ability to mobilize a qualified team with expertise in prosthetics and orthotics, rehabilitation, assistive technology, APL development, financing and training, with capacity to work in Uzbek and Russian.
  • Experience in Central Asia, the CIS or comparable middle-income health systems is an asset.
  • Experience performing assignments for UN agencies, international financial institutions or national ministries of health or social protection is an asset.

 

At the expressions of interest stage, the qualifications and relevant experience of the firm will be evaluated. Key experts and their curricula vitae (CVs) will not be evaluated at this stage; the relevant information will be requested from the selected firm together with its technical proposal.

 

Interested Consultants are referred to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (September 2023) (the “Procurement Regulations”) concerning conflict of interest. (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)

 

Country:                                             Independent State of Samoa

Name of Project:                              Samoa Finance Sector Resilience and Development Project (SFSRDP) 2025 – 2029 (World Bank Financed Project P181456)

Loan No./Credit No./Grant No.:      IDA – E3780

Assignment Title:                              Diagnostic assessment for a National Retail Payment Switch

Reference No.:                                   CBS/CS/004

 

1. Introduction:

The Government of Samoa has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the SFSRDP P181456 and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Central Bank of Samoa invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing consulting services to conduct a diagnostic assessment for a national retail payment switch.

The objective of this assignment is to undertake a diagnostic assessment of Samoa's retail payments ecosystem and evaluate the need, feasibility, and potential design options for establishing a National Retail Payment Switch.

Interested consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.

This REOI is being issued for the purpose of establishing a shortlist of qualified consulting firms who will subsequently be invited to submit detailed technical and financial proposals under the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method.

 

2. Background:

The Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) is the monetary authority responsible for maintaining financial stability, managing currency issuance, and overseeing the payment systems in Samoa.

Under the Samoa Finance Sector Resilience and Development project supported by the World Bank, the CBS is pursuing initiatives to strengthen the national payments ecosystem, increase digital financial inclusion, improve payment efficiency, and support the country's broader digital transformation agenda. As electronic payment channels continue to expand across banks, mobile money operators, government agencies, merchants, and consumers, the need for more efficient interoperability arrangements has become increasingly important.

Currently, retail payment transactions may be processed through bilateral arrangements, proprietary networks, or international payment schemes, resulting in potential inefficiencies, higher transaction costs, limited interoperability, and constraints on innovation. A National Retail Payment Switch could provide a shared infrastructure enabling seamless, secure, and real-time interoperability among payment service providers.

Before making investment and policy decisions, CBS seeks the services of a consultancy firm to conduct a comprehensive diagnostic assessment to determine whether a National Retail Payment Switch is necessary, feasible, and economically viable, and if so, to identify the most appropriate implementation model for Samoa

 

3. Objective of the Assignment:

The objectives of the assignment include:

  1. Assess the current state of retail payment systems and interoperability arrangements.
  2. Identify gaps, inefficiencies, and constraints within the existing payment ecosystem.
  3. Evaluate current and future demand for interoperable retail payment services.
  4. Assess the business, technical, operational, regulatory, and financial viability of a National Retail Payment Switch.
  5. Examine alternative interoperability models and determine whether a national switch is the most appropriate solution.
  6. Provide recommendations and an implementation roadmap, if deemed necessary.

 

4. Scope of Services:

The Consultant will be expected to undertake activities including, but not limited to:

Task 1: Inception Phase and stakeholder consultation

Task 2: Assessment of the current payment ecosystem

Task 3: Gap Analysis

Task 4: Assessment of the Need for a National Retail Payment Switch

Task 5: Evaluation of Alternative Models

Task 6: Design Considerations (If a Switch is Recommended)

Task 7: Implementation Roadmap

 

5. The detailed Terms of Reference for the Assignment is provided in the Annex of this document.

 

6. The Central Bank of Samoa now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

7. A consulting firm is allowed to submit the expression of interest alone if it considers itself to be fully qualified on its own for the assignment, as it is not mandatory for consultants to associate with any other firm(s), whether foreign or local. Alternatively, if consultants themselves choose to associate to enhance their qualifications and capability for the assignment, then such associations may either be as a Joint Venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally responsible) and/or Sub-consultants (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant). In case of an association, the Consultants must explain in the EOI submission

(a) the rationale for forming the association and

(b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each subconsultant for carrying out the assignment, to justify the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants in the association.

Failure to provide the above explanation in the Expression of Interest may risk the association not being shortlisted for the assignment. Please note that in the evaluation of EOIs of associations for shortlisting purposes, only the qualifications of the JV members will be taken into account whereas the qualifications of proposed sub-consultants will not be considered.

 

 

8. The shortlisting criteria are as follows, in which specific experience of the Consultant relevant to the assignment will be considered of paramount importance:

    1. Demonstrated experience in assignments of comparable scope, specifically in conducting diagnostics and advisory services for national or regional payment systems, with a focus on retail payment switch design, implementation, or assessment within the last 10 years.
    2. Proven track record in supporting the modernization of payment systems to enhance efficiency, security, and interoperability of digital financial services, including experience with regulatory and supervisory frameworks for payment systems in developing country contexts.
    3. Experience advising central banks, financial sector regulators, or payment system operators on the development, evaluation, or integration of payment infrastructure, including interoperability standards (e.g., API, QR) and digital financial services ecosystems.
    4. Familiarity with financial inclusion strategies and demonstrated capacity to assess payment system use cases that promote access to formal financial services and reduce remittance costs
    5. Documented organizational systems and methodologies for conducting diagnostics, stakeholder consultations, and technical assessments in the context of payment system modernization.
    6. Capacity to address data protection, cybersecurity, and business continuity considerations relevant to payment system infrastructure, as required for robust and resilient digital financial services.
    7. Ability to coordinate with the Central Bank of Samoa and other relevant stakeholders, reflecting experience in multi-institutional environments and government-led financial sector reforms.
    8. Sufficient organizational resources to field a multidisciplinary team with expertise in payment systems, digital finance, regulatory analysis, and IT systems, appropriate to the assignment’s scope and complexity
    9. Compliance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Fifth Edition, September 2023) and absence of conflict of interest or debarment
    10. If joint ventures or subconsultants are proposed, the lead firm must be clearly identified, and the proposal must specify how relevant experience will be aggregated to meet the above requirements.

The Consultants should demonstrate availability of and/or access to the key experts for the performance of the services described in the TOR (e.g., by providing a list of key experts they are working with). The Consultants should demonstrate sound administrative and financial capacity. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

9. Eligibility and Shortlisting Criteria:

Interested consulting firms must:

  • Be legally registered entities.
  • Have been in operation for at least 15 years.
  • Have no conflict of interest related to this assignment.
  • Not be subject to suspension, debarment, or ineligibility by any applicable authority, development partner, or international financing institution.

Annex 1: Terms of Reference

 

SAMOA FINANCE SECTOR RESILIENCE AND DEVELOPMENT PROJECT

TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR A CONSULTING FIRM

TO CONDUCT A DIAGNOSTIC ASSESSMENT FOR A NATIONAL RETAIL PAYMENT SWITCH

 

1. BACKGROUND

The Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) is the monetary authority responsible for maintaining financial stability, managing currency issuance, and overseeing the payment systems in Samoa.

Under the Samoa Finance Sector Resilience and Development project supported by the World Bank, the CBS is pursuing initiatives to strengthen the national payments ecosystem, increase digital financial inclusion, improve payment efficiency, and support the country's broader digital transformation agenda. As electronic payment channels continue to expand across banks, mobile money operators, government agencies, merchants, and consumers, the need for more efficient interoperability arrangements has become increasingly important.

Currently, retail payment transactions may be processed through bilateral arrangements, proprietary networks, or international payment schemes, resulting in potential inefficiencies, higher transaction costs, limited interoperability, and constraints on innovation. A National Retail Payment Switch could provide a shared infrastructure enabling seamless, secure, and real-time interoperability among payment service providers.

Before making investment and policy decisions, CBS seeks the services of a consultancy firm to conduct a comprehensive diagnostic assessment to determine whether a National Retail Payment Switch is necessary, feasible, and economically viable, and if so, to identify the most appropriate implementation model for Samoa.

 

2. OBJECTIVES

 

The overall objective of this assignment is to undertake a diagnostic assessment of Samoa's retail payments ecosystem and evaluate the need, feasibility, and potential design options for establishing a National Retail Payment Switch.

 

Specific objectives include:

1.  Assess the current state of retail payment systems and interoperability arrangements.

2.  Identify gaps, inefficiencies, and constraints within the existing payment ecosystem.

3.  Evaluate current and future demand for interoperable retail payment services.

4. Assess the business, technical, operational, regulatory, and financial viability of a National Retail Payment Switch.

5.  Examine alternative interoperability models and determine whether a national switch is the most appropriate solution.

6.  Provide recommendations and an implementation roadmap, if deemed necessary.

 

 

3. SCOPE OF WORK

The consultancy firm shall undertake, but not be limited to, the following activities:

Task 1: Inception and Stakeholder Consultation

  • Conduct a kick-off meeting with CBS.
  • Review relevant national policies, legislation, regulations, strategies, and previous studies.
  • Identify key stakeholders including:
    • Commercial banks
    • Mobile money operators
    • Government agencies
    • Payment service providers
    • Merchants
    • Telecommunications providers
    • Consumer groups
    • Development partners
  • Develop a stakeholder engagement plan.
  • Conduct interviews, workshops, and consultations.

 

 
  

 

Task 2: Assessment of the Current Payment Ecosystem

Review and assess, at minimum the:

Market Structure

  • Number and type of payment service providers.
  • Customer adoption and usage trends.
  • Existing payment products and services.

Payment Infrastructure

  • Retail payment systems.
  • Automated clearing arrangements.
  • Card payment networks.
  • Mobile money platforms.
  • Internet and mobile banking systems.
  • Government payment platforms.

Interoperability Arrangements

  • Existing bilateral and multilateral arrangements.
  • Connectivity among market participants.
  • Domestic and cross-border payment linkages.

Payment Volumes and Trends

  • Transaction volumes and values.
  • Channel usage patterns.
  • Cash versus digital payment trends.
  • Future market projections.

 

 
  

 

Task 3: Gap Analysis

Assess challenges and constraints including:

  • Fragmented payment arrangements.
  • Lack of interoperability.
  • Operational inefficiencies.
  • High transaction costs.
  • Customer inconvenience.
  • Limited innovation opportunities.
  • Financial inclusion barriers.
  • Settlement and liquidity risks.

 

The consultant shall identify root causes and quantify impacts where possible.

 

 
  

 

Task 4: Assessment of the Need for a National Retail Payment Switch

 

Conduct a comprehensive assessment addressing at minimum :

Strategic Assessment

  • Alignment with national development objectives.
  • Financial inclusion goals.
  • Digital economy initiatives.
  • Government digitization priorities.

 

Functional Assessment

Potential services supported by a switch, including:

  • Account-to-account payments
  • Instant payments
  • Mobile money interoperability
  • QR code payments
  • Merchant payments
  • Government collections and disbursements
  • Bill payments
  • Agency banking transactions
  • Cross-border payment connectivity

 

Demand Assessment

  • Market demand by consumers.
  • Demand by merchants.
  • Demand by financial institutions.
  • Future growth projections.

 

Economic Assessment

  • Cost-benefit analysis.
  • Transaction cost savings.
  • Efficiency gains.
  • Expected economic impact.

 

 
  

 

Task 5: Evaluation of Alternative Models

Assess and compare alternatives such as:

Option 1 - Maintain current arrangements with incremental improvements.

Option 2 - Enhanced bilateral interoperability model.

Option 3 - Shared interoperability platform.

Option 4 – National Retail Payment Switch.

Option 5 - Regional interoperability arrangements.

 

 

For each option, assess:

  • Cost
  • Benefits
  • Scalability
  • Sustainability
  • Risk profile
  • Governance implications
  • Market readiness

Task 6: Design Considerations (If a Switch is Recommended)

Assess at minimum:

  1. Governance Model
  • Central bank-owned.
  • Industry-owned.
  • Public-private partnership.
  • Independent operator.
  1. Technology Architecture
  • Centralized versus distributed architecture.
  • Real-time payment capabilities.
  • ISO 20022 readiness.
  • API-based integration.
  • Cybersecurity requirements.
  • Business continuity and disaster recovery.
  1. Settlement Arrangements
  • Deferred net settlement.
  • Real-time gross settlement linkages.
  • Hybrid models.
  1. Operational Framework
  • Participation criteria.
  • Pricing model.
  • Operating rules.
  • Risk management framework.
  1. Legal and Regulatory Framework
  • Required regulatory changes.
  • Oversight arrangements.
  • Consumer protection considerations.
  1. Future Readiness
    • Readiness for:
      • ISO 20022 migration.
      • Real-time payments.
      • QR payments.
      • Request-to-Pay services.
      • Proxy addressing services.
      • Digital identity integration
      • Regional interoperability initiatives

 

 
  

 

 

Task 7: Implementation Roadmap

Where applicable, develop:

  • Phased implementation roadmap.
  • Governance and institutional arrangements.
  • Procurement strategy.
  • Capacity-building requirements.

 

 

 

  • Change management strategy.
  • Budget estimates.
  • Key milestones and timelines.
  • Risk mitigation measures.

 

 

4. DELIVERABLES

During the consultancy, the consultant will deliver where necessary:

    • Reports, analyses, and recommendations. 
    • Presentations and workshops. 
    • Implementation plans.

 

With specific and satisfactorily completed outputs/milestones being:

Milestone

Include at minimum:

Milestone 1: Inception Report

  • Understanding of assignment.
  • Methodology.
  • Work plan.
  • Stakeholder engagement plan.
  • Inception presentation.

Milestone 2: Diagnostic Assessment Report

(Comprehensive report on the existing payment landscape and clear justification/need for a switch)

  • Current-state assessment.
  • Market analysis.
  • Gap analysis.
  • Stakeholder consultation findings.
  • Demand assessment.

 

Milestone 3: Draft Final Report

 

  • Assessment findings.
  • Options analysis.
  • Cost-benefit analysis.
  • Recommendations.
    • Recommended governance structure, and legal recommendations
    • Technical blueprint and TOR for vendor
      • high level technical specifications and a draft RFP for switch vendors.
  • Draft implementation roadmap.

Milestone 4: Final Report and Presentation

  • Final diagnostic report including risk mitigation matrix
  • Executive summary.
  • Implementation roadmap
  • Executive presentation.

 

 

 

 

5. SELECTION METHOD

The consultant will be selected through the “Quality and Cost-Based Selection method” in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Procurement Regulations) of September 2023.

 

 

6. QUALIFICATIONS and EXPERIENCE

Firm Experience

The consulting firm (or eligible joint venture) team shall demonstrate the qualifications outlined below.

1.            Demonstrated experience in assignments of comparable scope, specifically in conducting diagnostics and advisory services for national or regional payment systems, with a focus on retail payment switch design, implementation, or assessment within the last 10 years.

2.            Proven track record in supporting the modernization of payment systems to enhance efficiency, security, and interoperability of digital financial services, including experience with regulatory and supervisory frameworks for payment systems in developing country contexts.

3.            Experience advising central banks, financial sector regulators, or payment system operators on the development, evaluation, or integration of payment infrastructure, including interoperability standards (e.g., API, QR) and digital financial services ecosystems.

4.            Familiarity with financial inclusion strategies and demonstrated capacity to assess payment system use cases that promote access to formal financial services and reduce remittance costs

5.            Documented organizational systems and methodologies for conducting diagnostics, stakeholder consultations, and technical assessments in the context of payment system modernization.

6.            Capacity to address data protection, cybersecurity, and business continuity considerations relevant to payment system infrastructure, as required for robust and resilient digital financial services.

7.            Ability to coordinate with the Central Bank of Samoa and other relevant stakeholders, reflecting experience in multi-institutional environments and government-led financial sector reforms.

8.            Sufficient organizational resources to field a multidisciplinary team with expertise in payment systems, digital finance, regulatory analysis, and IT systems, appropriate to the assignment’s scope and complexity.

9.            Compliance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Fifth Edition, September 2023) and absence of conflict of interest or debarment

10.          If joint ventures or subconsultants are proposed, the lead firm must be clearly identified, and the proposal must specify how relevant experience will be aggregated to meet the above requirements.

 

Key Experts

The consulting firm shall field a multidisciplinary team with expertise in digital payments, financial sector diagnostics, and technology architecture. The assignment will require adherence to international standards for payment systems, data protection, and interoperability. The team must demonstrate capacity for stakeholder engagement, and inclusion considerations, and knowledge transfer to CBS staff.

  • Understanding of the CPMI-IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMI).
  • Knowledge of retail payment interoperability and switch governance.
  • Familiarity with ISO 20022, EMV, QR payment standards, and API-based integrations.
  • Experience working with central banks and financial institutions.
  • Strong analytical, stakeholder consultation, and report-writing skills.
  • Ability to develop actionable recommendations, implementation roadmaps, and costed investment plans.

  • Minimum 8 years of cybersecurity experience.
